How do I use ESPN Search Beta?

You can start by selecting one of the prepopulated questions—like “Catch Me Up,” which uses your favorited teams to generate timely questions about news or games happening right now, or “Today in Sports History,” which highlights memorable moments from years past. You can also simply type your own question. As long as it’s about sports, ESPN Search Beta will do its best to help.

How does ESPN Search Beta work?

We developed ESPN Search Beta with help from our partners at Microsoft. When you ask a question, it only searches ESPN’s own data — news articles, and schedules, scores, standings, and stats feeds — before giving you a response, sometimes with an AI summary of what it found, or a table of data pulled directly from ESPN’s feeds.

What does ESPN Search do with my information?

We use your favorited teams to improve your experience—for example, prioritizing results from the teams you care about most. Beyond that, we do not use personal information for ESPN Search. We may retain aggregate search data—such as what users search for—to help train and improve the product. To learn more, please visit our privacy policy.

What does it mean that ESPN Search is in Beta?

To ensure ESPN Search can reliably answer all sports-related questions, we need to make sure every cable, plug, and connection behind the scenes is working exactly as it should. A big part of that process is understanding how real fans search and what matters most to them. That’s why we’re inviting a small percentage of users to try ESPN Search while it’s still a work in progress. Your use—and your feedback—will help make it better.

What is ‘ESPN Search Beta’?

At ESPN, we love sports—really, really love sports. We obsess over every stat, headline, and play, and we can’t get enough of discussing, analyzing, and (yes) arguing about them. Over the past 45 years, we’ve built a digital vault packed with one of the most comprehensive collections of sports information anywhere. So we asked ourselves: What if we gave fans the keys to dive into it? That’s why we’re excited to introduce ESPN Search Beta—an AI-enhanced search experience designed to help you quickly find the score, game time, headline, stat, or story you’re looking for (and maybe discover something new along the way). Over time, we believe ESPN Search will make discovering sports content faster, easier, and more engaging—and we’re inviting users to help shape what comes next. ESPN Search Beta is designed to deliver actionable results through tables, links, and direct answers, while also creating new entry points into the ESPN App experience. We’ve integrated features like “Where to Watch”, streaming content from Watch ESPN, and breaking news and analysis from ESPN contributors directly into search results. We’re also beginning to unlock deeper layers of ESPN stats and analytics that were previously unavailable to fans, giving users more of the information they care about most. Looking ahead, we see opportunities to bring the technology behind ESPN Search Beta into other ESPN products, helping surface relevant insights, recommendations, and prompts across the ESPN ecosystem.

Who built ESPN Search Beta?

We did! ESPN Search Beta was built by an internal team at ESPN with help from our partners over at Microsoft.

Why does ESPN Search Beta get it wrong?

We work hard to avoid errors, but ESPN Search is a rookie—full of potential but still learning the playbook. That means some responses may include mistakes or outdated information. Questions about sports topics with limited ESPN coverage can be challenging. And sometimes ESPN Search Beta may simply misunderstand what you’re asking, looking in the wrong drawer for the answer. This is where you come in: The more feedback we receive, the fewer unforced errors ESPN Search Beta will make.

What does ESPN stand for?

When ESPN started in 1979, we were the Entertainment and Sports Programming Network (hence the name ESPN). However, that name took too long to paint across our chests on game day, so we dropped it in 1985 and adopted a new corporate name – ESPN, LLC.– and a new logo. ESPN, LLC is 72 percent owned by The Walt Disney Company, 18 percent by Hearst, and 10 percent by the National Football League.

Login Error Resolution- Apple Safari

Users receiving the following error message when attempting to log in to their ESPN.com account may resolve this issue by flushing the DNS cache on their browser and/or device. #### (image: Fhockey_Login_Error_Resolution_1.png) If receiving an error when attempting to login to an ESPN.com account using Safari, the user should follow the below steps to be guided toward a successful login: Browser DNS Flushing in Apple Safari DNS caching on Mac devices is handled by the operating system, see “Device DNS Flushing ” below and locate the version of Apple OS X you are running.   Device DNS Flushing:        Apple OS X Mac OS X El Capitan If you are running Mac OS X 10.11, you need to follow the below steps: Open up the command terminal. Run the command sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder Return to ESPN.com and attempt to Log In Mac OS X Yosemite If you are running Mac OS X 10.10, you need to follow the below steps: Open up the command terminal. Run the command sudo discoveryutil udnsflushcaches Return to ESPN.com and attempt to Log In Mac OS X Mavericks If you are running Mac OS X 10.9, you need to follow the below steps: Open up the command terminal. Run the command sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder Return to ESPN.com and attempt to Log In Mac OS X Mountain Lion If you are running Mac OS X 10.8, you need to follow the below steps: Open up the command terminal. Run the command sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder Return to ESPN.com and attempt to Log In If you are still having difficulty logging in after attempting these steps or need assistance, please contact ESPN Customer Care

Login Error Resolution- Mozilla Firefox

Users receiving the following error message when attempting to log in to their ESPN.com account may resolve this issue by flushing the DNS cache on their browser and/or device. #### (image: Fhockey_Login_Error_Resolution_1.png) If you receive an error when attempting to login to an ESPN.com account using Firefox, try the steps below: #### Step-by-step guide:  1. Open Firefox. 2. Type: about:networking#dns into the address bar at the top of the browser window. 3. Press Enter: to load the DNS page. 4. Click: the “Clear DNS Cache” button. 5. Restart Firefox: to ensure the changes take effect.

Why flush the DNS cache?

A DNS cache stores information about website addresses to speed up future browsing. However, this cache can sometimes become outdated or corrupted, leading to an inability to access certain websites. Flushing the cache can resolve these issues.

Fantasy Baseball: Draft

Autopick Draft

What is an Autopick Draft?

The Autopick Draft option automatically drafts players for every team on a scheduled draft date. Team managers do not need to be online during the draft. #### Preparing Your Draft List - Team managers can pre-rank players to improve their chances of building their preferred roster. - Draft lists can be edited until midnight the day before the scheduled draft.

If No Draft List Is Submitted

  • The system will use the default ESPN draft rankings.

How the Autopick Draft Works

When the draft begins: 1. The system loads each team manager’s draft list. 2. For each pick, the system selects the highest-ranked available player from that list. 3. The player must fit an open roster slot and not exceed roster position limits. 4. The process continues until all roster spots for each team are filled.

Autopick Draft: Post Draft

Conclusion of The Draft

  • After the system finishes processing the autopick draft, it requires a few minutes to convert the league to regular-season mode.
  • Team managers will receive an email notifying them when the draft is complete so they can begin managing their team.

Post-Draft

  • The system automatically fills all of the team rosters with each team’s selected players

  • All undrafted players are put on waivers for two days.

  • Team managers can place claims on undrafted players. Once the two-day waiver period ends, the system will automatically execute the pending waiver claims in priority order.

  • When the waiver period ends, all remaining unclaimed players become free agents and can be picked up on a first-come, first-served basis.

  • League Manager leagues’ waiver rules are based on the League Manager’s initial setup and preferences.

Custom Keeper Rounds (LM Leagues)

League managers can manually determine which round and pick a player should be kept in. The League Manager must have their draft set to Snake or Autopick. NOTE: This feature is not available for Salary Cap or Offline drafts. Within Keeper Rules, the League Manager can manually set the Keeper Designated Round. Once this is set, on the Keepers page, the League Manager can click on Edit Keeper Draft Rounds and select whatever round they want each player kept in. IMPORTANT NOTE: The Draft Keepers in the Original Round feature will NOT work with the Random Draft Order setting. The league’s draft order must be manually set by the League Manager to utilize this feature. If a user changes the draft order after setting the rounds players will be kept in, they will be prompted that making this change will revert all of their selections. #### How to Set Custom Keeper Rounds (LM Only / Web Only) NOTE: This setting only works for Keeper leagues in their second and later fantasy years. PRO TIP: Edit your Keeper Draft AFTER the Keeper Selection Lock Time has passed. 1. Click on LM Tools 2. Click on Edit Keepers under Roster Tools 3. You will see each team’s selected Keepers 4. Click on the blue Edit Keeper Draft Rounds button 5. Use the dropdown to select the Round and Pick for each Keeper 6. When finished, click Save Changes.

Draft Dates

  • Teams that join a preseason league will draft on the date listed on the league page
  • Always check the listed draft day and draft type before joining a group
  • In Free Standard Leagues, ESPN reserves the right to merge undrafted leagues if they are not filled by the draft time. Leagues will not be split to complete other leagues in order to run a draft.
  • However, if the number of teams in each league equals five, they can be combined to make one full league (at the discretion of the ESPN Fantasy League Office)

Draft Methods

Draft Overview

Your draft is an important factor for a successful season. Teams that begin with a strong draft are most likely to find themselves in good shape for the rest of the season. #### ESPN Standard Leagues  Each team receives a specified number of players during the draft. For example, in a 10-team league where each team has 9 roster slots each, a total of 90 players will be drafted for that league. In ESPN Standard Leagues, there are two draft options available: - Live Snake draft - Live Salary Cap draft

League Manager Leagues

In League Manager (LM) leagues, your final player total depends on your roster settings. LMs have the option of four different draft methods: - Autopick - Live Online Draft - Offline Draft - Salary Cap Draft

LIVE AND MOCK DRAFT LOBBY LEAGUES

The Live Draft Lobby is where it all starts once you are ready to join a Free Standard or League Manager league. Once you’re there, click on a room name. NOTE: The listed Standard League names are for quick identity purposes only, and will change to generic league names, which you can customize by league vote after the draft is complete. After entering the lobby you will see the “Join This League” button. Another method is to locate a Standard league via the League Directory. NOTE: The listed Standard League names are for quick identity purposes only, and will change to generic league names, which you can customize by league vote after the draft is complete. After entering the lobby you will see the “Join This League” button. A #### WAITING FOR THE DRAFT TO START After you successfully join a lobby league, your team name and info will appear on the page in bold. The league’s draft start time is displayed in the middle of the page and on the countdown clock below it. NOTE: In order for a league draft in the live draft lobby to move into drafting mode, all Open Slots must be filled before the listed draft start time. If open slots remain, try recruiting members to join via the message board or simply wait and hope the room will fill itself in time (the page automatically reloads itself every 30 seconds). Any live draft Lobby league (ESPN created league) that is not full before the draft start will have their draft time continually pushed back in five-minute intervals until the league is filled. NOTE: Once your draft has been filled, it will convert once the scheduled time arrives. #### STARTING THE DRAFT If your league is full at the listed start time the lobby room page will automatically reload itself with a link to Launch Draft. #### THE MOCK DRAFT LOBBY The Mock Draft Lobby is a great way to practice drafting. It works in the same way as the Live Draft Lobby. The only difference is that the Mock Draft does not count! The Mock Draft Lobby can be used for draft practice or testing. We encourage you to try it out and practice drafting from different draft positions (we can’t all get the first draft pick). Good luck with your season!

Draft Schedule Issues

If your draft did not take place at its scheduled time, reference the following steps: #### Standard (Public) Leagues - In Standard (Public) leagues, the draft will only start once all 8-, 10-, or 12-team managers have joined. If one of the managers doesn’t join the league at least 1 hour before the scheduled draft time, your draft cannot start. - The missing team manager(s) need to officially join the league, and then at least six of your league members need to vote on when the new draft should take place.

League Manager Leagues

  • League Manager leagues must be filled at least one hour before the scheduled Draft.  Leagues that do not have all slots filled sixty (60) minutes before the scheduled draft time will be reset, and the LM will need to reschedule their draft.
  • League Manager leagues enable the League Manager to set the new draft date/time. Click on the “LM Tools” tab if on the web
  • League Manager Tools from the menu in the ESPN fantasy app
On the ESPN Fantasy App
  1. Tap on the Menu Icon (top left corner of the screen)
  2. Tap on League Manager Tools in the dropdown menu
  3. Tap on Edit Draft Settings
  4. Select the new draft date
  5. Tap Update Draft Settings
On the Web
  1. Click on LM Tools
  2. Click on Edit Draft Settings
  3. Select a New Draft Date/Time 
  4. Click Save Changes

Edit Draft Type, Date, Order and/or Reset the Draft

Edit Draft Settings on the ESPN Fantasy App (LM Leagues)

  • League managers can edit the draft settings on the ESPN Fantasy App
  • Tap the League Manager Tools in the menu.
  • Tap Edit Draft Settings.
  • ​From this screen, the LM can change draft type, date, and time. All other changes must be done on the web.

Edit Draft Settings on the Web

  • You can access the draft settings page up to one hour before your league’s draft is scheduled to begin.
  • Changes to live drafts can be made up to one hour before the scheduled live draft time. Additional draft times will be added as required.
  • Changes for** Autopick Drafts** can be made until 2:59 a.m. ET the day the Autopick Draft is scheduled to process.
  • Changes for offline drafts can be made until the time the League Manager begins entering the offline results.
  • Click on** LM Tools** then click on Edit Draft Settings.
  • On this page, you can change any of your draft settings and edits submitted to the system will automatically trigger an e-mail to each team manager in the league, notifying them of the changes.

Set Draft Order on the Web

  • Click on LM Tools then click on** Edit Draft Order.**
  • Click on the Edit button.
  • Click on the Randomize Order button or Drag-and-Drop each team into the desired order.
  • Click on the Save button.​

Reset Draft on the Web

  • You can access the** Reset Draft** page after your league’s draft is complete. If you wish to reset the draft, the system will completely change the league’s status from post-draft to pre-draft. CAUTION: This will undo all draft picks and allow team managers to set their draft list again if they wish.
  • Click on LM Tools then click on Reset Order.
  • Once you are certain you wish to go through with the reset, click on Reset Draft.  NOTE: This cannot be undone!

Editing Autopick Draft Strategy

If you’re worried about missing your draft or getting disconnected, you can set an Auto-Pick Draft Strategy ahead of time so the system drafts according to your preferences. #### Accessing Draft Strategy You can edit your draft strategy from your main team page before the draft begins. 1. Click Edit Auto-Pick Strategy. 2. The edit page displays each round of the draft with a pulldown menu.

Choosing a Draft Strategy

For each round, you can select how the system should draft. - The default option is Best Available. - On this setting, the system drafts the highest-ranked remaining player from any position.

You can also choose a specific position. Example: In Fantasy Baseball (applies to all fantasy sports), selecting First Base (1B) will cause the system to draft the highest available First Baseman during that round. #### Setting Position Limits You can control how many players are drafted at each position. - This is managed in the Position Limits table on the right side of the page. - Set the minimum and maximum number of players you want drafted for each position.

Drafting by Stat

You can also instruct the system to draft based on a specific statistic. Example: In Fantasy Baseball (applies to all fantasy sports), selecting RBIs will prioritize players who perform best in that category. #### Editing Deadline You can edit your draft strategy any time until one hour before the scheduled draft time. #### Availability The Edit Auto-Pick Strategy page is only available for leagues using: - Live Snake Draft - Auto-Pick Draft

Enable/Disable Draft Pick Trading in LM Leagues

The League Manager (LM) is the only person who can enable or disable Draft Pick Trading in a league. Draft Pick Trading allows team managers to trade draft slots before the draft begins. Example: A manager might trade their 2nd- and 3rd-round picks to another manager in exchange for that manager’s 1st-round pick. Draft pick trades can be completed on both the ESPN Fantasy App and the web. Note: Draft pick trades can only be made before the draft and apply only to the current season. #### Enabling Draft Pick Trading 1. Go to LM Tools. 2. Select Edit Draft Settings. 3. Set Draft Order to Manually Set by League Manager. 4. Set Allow Draft Pick Trading to Yes. 5. Click Save Changes.

Alternative method: 1. Go to LM Tools. 2. Select Begin Draft Pick Trading. 3. Click Allow Draft Pick Trading and Confirm.

Disabling Draft Pick Trading

  1. Go to LM Tools.
  2. Select Stop Draft Pick Trading and Reset Draft Picks.
  3. Click Confirm.
Important Note

When Draft Pick Trading is disabled: - All traded draft picks are returned to their original teams. - Any players traded along with those picks will remain on their current teams.

To move those players back, the League Manager must manually adjust rosters using LM Tools.

Keeper Leagues

Keeper leagues (also known as Dynasty leagues) allow Team Managers to keep players on their roster over multiple seasons without having to redraft them.  Keepers are only available in League Manager leagues.  Team Managers may select as few players or as many players as the league creator selected during league creation. For example, if your league allows 3 Keepers per team, a Team Manager may elect to designate between 0-3 players to stay on their roster for the next season. League Manager can enable or disable Keeper settings via LM Tools. #### A few important facts about Keepers on ESPN Fantasy:  - The default draft method in Keeper leagues is to draft/assign selected Keepers in the first rounds.  Keeper rounds are Non-Snake. (For Snake Drafts) This means that if the league allows 2 keepers in the upcoming draft, the first 2 rounds would be non-snake. 1-10, 1-10, then from the 3rd round, 1-10, 10-1, 1-10, etc.

  • Example: Last season, a Team Manager drafted a player in the 5th round.  The Team Manager decides to mark that player as one of their team’s Keepers for the next season.  When the next season’s draft occurs, that Keeper will be drafted automatically in the 5th round.

To enable Keepers in an LM league:

  1. Open** LM Tools**
  2. Go to League and Scoring Settings Tools
  3. Select League Settings
  4. Select** Transactions and Keepers**
  5. Scroll down to Keepers Rules and click on Edit
  6. Click on Yes for Use Keepers for (next) Season.
  7. You can now select how many players can be designated as a Keeper (Minimum 1, maximum full roster size)
  8. You can set the date when Keepers Lock. The default is one hour before your next season Draft Date/Time.
  9. Click Save Changes

Keeper Salaries

Keeper salaries are how much a manager will “pay for” out of their salary cap prior to the draft in order to keep that player. Kind of how draft right works.  Most leagues use the player salaries from the prior season(s), but LM’s can change that. ##### To Edit Keeper Salaries 1. Open** LM Tools 2. You can now select the salary. 8. Click Save Changes**

Live Online Snake Drafts

In the Live Online Snake Draft, each team’s manager drafts unique players via a back-and-forth, round-by-round draft order (i.e., 1-10, 10-1, 1-10, 10-1, etc.) until all roster slots are full. Like any prospective team manager, you want to assemble the best possible roster of players, so it’s smart to be prepared before you set out. The following information will brief you on the ins-and-outs of how the Snake Draft works: #### Editing Draft Lists - We highly recommend that all live draft participants customize their draft list before the actual draft. This protects you in case you are unable to participate in your live draft. - The Player list can be reordered using our Pre-Rank tool.  You can also determine which position to draft each round with the Draft Strategy tool.  Both are available on your preseason “My Team” page.  PRO-TIP: Make sure you SAVE your changes before you leave! - NOTE: You may edit your draft list as often as you like, up until one hour before your scheduled draft time.

  1. On your preseason League Office page in the “Draft Info” box.
  2. On your main team page.

Entering Your Live Online Draft 

  • You may enter your live draft as early as one hour before the scheduled start time.
  • Links to enter the draft are available on your “League Office” and “My Team” pages.
  • Please keep in mind that all leagues MUST be full in order for a draft to begin. If a league is not full, it will NOT convert into draft mode, and the draft time will be rescheduled.IMPORTANT: League Managers, make sure that all of your league’s team managers have joined the league at least one hour before your draft! If not, then you will have to select a new Draft Date/Time.

Input Offline Draft Results - Click on LM Tools, then click on “Input Offline Draft Results” - Click on the roster slot you wish to fill. Salary Cap Draft

Salary Cap Drafts use a competing-offer format and differ considerably from traditional Snake Live Drafts. In Salary Cap Drafts, two first-round ranked players could be signed by the same team, which would rarely happen in a Snake Draft, because both players are so early and close to one another in the Snake Draft ranking order. For example, in ESPN Fantasy Baseball, it’s possible to get Shohei Ohtani and Aaron Judge on the same team in a Salary Cap Draft, but that is almost impossible to achieve in a Snake or Auto-draft. - Private league LMs can edit the budget under draft settings. - Salary Cap drafts are available to Standard (Public)  and League Manager (LM) Leagues. - Teams can sign any player, provided they have the funds available. - Public leagues are set up with a preset $200 budget to sign enough players to fill their rosters.

NOTE: ALL teams will start the draft with the same budget. If you are in a keeper league and have different “salaries” for keepers, please visit “Keeper Leagues.” - To edit draft settings pre-draft, please visit “Pre-Draft League Manager Abilities.” - To edit in-draft settings, please visit “Salary Cap Draft- League Manager Tools.”

Process:

  1. Once a player is nominated for signing, the offer process begins.
  2. Team managers can offer any monetary value that their budget permits.
  3. Team managers continue to submit offers until only a single high-salary offer remains. The system will then alert team managers, and the winning team will have the winning salary amount deducted from their budget.
  4. This process repeats until EVERY team’s roster is completely filled.
  5. When the draft is complete, the league will move into “in-season” mode, where teams can start making roster moves, waiver claims, trades, etc.

NOTE: Unused budgets DO NOT carry over into* “in-season”* mode. There is no advantage in finishing the draft with a remaining budget!

Salary Cap Draft: Absentee Team Managers

It is strongly recommended that all team managers be present when the draft begins. #### If Team Managers Are Missing - If one or two managers are missing, the League Manager should pause the draft and attempt to contact them. - If three or more managers are missing, it is recommended to reset the draft for a later time when more managers can attend.

How Auto Draft Works for Absent Managers

  • Any team whose manager is not present will be placed on Auto.
  • The system will actively draft players on their behalf.

During Auto drafting: - The system may offer up to a randomly determined percentage of the player’s preset salary limit. - If no salary limit is preset, the system will use the default value.

This ensures that absent team managers can still build a competitive team. #### If a Manager Gets Disconnected - If a team manager loses connection during the draft, their team will automatically switch to Auto mode.

Salary Cap Draft: League Manager Tools

In League Manager leagues, League Managers (LMs) have full commissioner controls over the league, including draft admin functions at any time during the draft. These admin functions can be accessed in the “LM Tools” tab in the LM’s main window. The LM can perform the following draft functions if the draft is paused: #### Pause Draft LMs can pause the draft at any time. If the LM pauses the draft the countdown clock stops. The app displays a “Draft is Paused” message. Once the LM resumes the draft, the clock will start for the current offer. #### Configure Time LMs can set the time for each nomination and offer. The system default for both is 30 seconds and can be changed by 5-second increments. Once the draft is resumed, the new time configurations will be in place. #### Reset Draft (on the web only) LMs can “reset” the draft at any time. If the draft is reset, the Salary Cap draft will start over from scratch: all players returned, all winning offers refunded, all picks reversed. #### Undo Picks LMs have the ability to “undo” any picks during any rounds. If the draft is in the 5th round and LM decides to undo a 2nd-round pick, doing so will also undo any picks made after that pick.

Salary Cap Drafts: How to Draft

Things to Know for Salary Cap Drafts

Nominating a Player
  • Team managers have 30 seconds to nominate a player.
  • To nominate, select a player from the main Players table (shows the player’s image and stats).
  • If no player is selected within 30 seconds, the system auto-nominates in this order:

Top player in the Player Queue panel (if any) - The available player with the highest starting salary - The default nomination offer is $1. - The nominating manager can raise the offer before submitting.

What Happens After a Nomination
  • Once nominated, the player appears at the top of the screen (with profile and stats) under the list of team managers.
  • The countdown clock begins immediately.
Making Offers
  • The offer clock starts at 30 seconds.
  • Any offer made with 10 seconds or less remaining will reset the clock back to 10 seconds. This continues until the player is won.

Offers can be placed in two ways: - +1 bidding - Entering a custom dollar amount

The app includes two buttons for submitting an offer (depending on how you’re bidding). ##### Offer Limits and Max Bids - The current offer is shown on the right and will also indicate whether you’re winning. - Teams can only bid amounts that still allow them to fill the rest of their roster with at least $1 per remaining roster slot. - You can view a team’s maximum offer by hovering over the team jerseys. - The maximum offer can also be displayed via an option in the Options tab. - Once a team reaches its max offer:

The app will reject additional bids - Offer buttons will be grayed out

Snake Draft Settings for LM leagues

In League Manager (custom) leagues, League Managers (LMs) have full commissioner controls over the league, including draft admin functions at any time during the draft. These admin functions can be accessed in the “LM Tools” tab in the LM’s main window. The LM can perform the following draft functions if the draft is paused: 1. Pause Draft:  LMs can pause the draft at any time. If the LM pauses the draft, the countdown clock stops, and the app displays a “Draft is Paused” message. Once the LM resumes the draft, the clock will start for the current offer. 2. Allow managers who have disconnected to remain off autopick until their allotted pick time expires. Choosing these settings would allow more time for managers who are not present more often to join the draft. 3. Configure Time:  LMs can set the time per pick. The system default is 30 seconds. Once the draft is resumed, the new time configurations will be in place. 4. Make picks for other managers (draft on behalf of missing managers) Use this to draft for managers who could not attend the draft (or LM can let the system autopick; it’s all up to the LM!). The league will see a message indicating LM is picking on behalf of someone, then the LM can proceed to the Players tab and pick. 5. Reset Draft (on the web only):  LMs can “reset” the draft at any time.  NOTE for Salary Cap Drafts: If a Salary Cap draft is reset, the draft will start over from scratch: all players are returned to teh draft pool, all winning offers are refunded, and all picks are reversed as if the draft never happened. 6. Undo picks LMs have the ability to “undo” any picks during any rounds. If the draft is in the 5th round and LM decides to undo a 2nd-round pick, doing so will also undo any picks made after that pick.

Trade Draft Picks

Draft Pick Trading enables Team Managers to trade draft slots - for example, a team manager might trade their 2nd and 3rd round pick slots to another team manager for their 1st round pick slot in return. Trades can be performed on the ESPN Fantasy App and on the web. NOTE: Draft Pick Trading is only available if it is enabled by the LM. #### Trade Draft Picks on the ESPN Fantasy App ##### Trade Draft Picks in a Non-Keeper League - Go to “Opposing Teams” and select the team you want to trade with - Click on “Propose Trade - Propose the draft pick trade

Note: If you trade and receive a net total of draft picks greater than the number of rounds in the draft (i.e., more players than you have roster slots for), your draft will end once you’ve reached the maximum, and you won’t be able to select any more players. If you have traded away multiple picks but not received as many in return, you will end the draft with empty roster slots and be required to fill via Free Agency after the draft has finished. Draft pick trading is available until one hour before your draft. ##### Trade Draft Picks in a Keeper League - Draft pick trades can be made as a swap of picks or as a combination of keepers and picks. Draft pick trades can only be done prior to the Keeper deadline for League Manager LeaguesThe Keeper deadline is determined by League Managers

Trade Draft Picks On the Web

Trade Draft Picks in a Non-Keeper League
  • Go to the “Opposing Teams” menu and select the team you want to trade with
  • Click on “Propose Trade”.
  • Propose the draft pick trade
Trade Draft Picks In a Keeper League
  • Draft pick trades can be made as a straight-up swap of picks or as a combination of keepers and picks. Draft pick trades can only be done prior to the Keeper deadline for League Manager Leagues
  • You are trading for a team manager’s pick in a given round, not the pick itself
  • If there’s no assurance that your League Manager won’t switch the draft order, it might be wise to avoid making such a trade. Otherwise, that 2nd overall pick you thought you traded for could become the 10th pick just like that

Updating Your Draft Rankings and Strategy

Already know who your top picks are, but worried you won’t be online during the draft? You can pre-rank players and set your Draft Strategy, allowing your draft to auto-pick for you! #### How to Pre-Rank Players (Web Only) - Access the “Edit Draft Strategy” page from your team’s home page once your draft date is set. - Next, rank the players in the order of your choice. To change your selections, slide each player up or down to determine their ranking, and click save. ​For Auto-Pick Draft Leagues, the ranking order of your desired players determines when the system will auto-select the “Best Available” player. - For “Live Online Draft Leagues”, rankings are only used when a team manager doesn’t pick a player within the allotted time and has no players on the pending pick queue. - IMPORTANT: Make sure you SAVE before leaving the page, or all your edits will be reset to the default!

How to set your Draft Strategy (Web Only)

  • Access the “Edit Draft Strategy” page from your team’s home page once your draft date is set.
  • Click on “Edit Autopick Strategy”
  • First, you can select Position Minimums and Maximums. For example, you can set it to draft a minimum of one (1) but a maximum of two (2) in a particular position.  This way you dont inadvertantly wind up with too many players at one position and not enough at another.
  • Next, you can designate which position you want in a particular round.  The default is “Best Available,” which tells the system to draft the highest-ranked available player.  But in some fantasy sports, there are positions you don’t want to draft until later rounds. For example, in Fantasy Football, many team managers like to draft a single Kicker (K) and only in the final round of their draft.

Drafts after the first pitch of the MLB Season

 Important: Using the Reset Draft feature will permanently delete all scores and stats for the current season. Previous scores and matchups cannot be adjusted, and scoring will not be retroactive. The timing of your league’s draft determines when your fantasy season officially begins. The rules differ depending on your league format: - Head-to-Head (H2H) Leagues - Rotisserie (Roto) and Season Points Leagues

Head-to-Head (H2H) Leagues

The key cutoff for H2H leagues is the start of Sunday Night Baseball on the last day of the first matchup period. Whether your league’s season includes that first matchup period depends on when your draft ends relative to that cutoff. - Draft ends before Sunday Night Baseball begins (last day of first matchup period): Your league’s season will include the first H2H matchup period. Note that you will not be able to adjust lineups for any days that passed before your league drafted. - Draft ends after Sunday Night Baseball begins (last day of first matchup period): Your league’s season will begin at the start of the next full H2H matchup period. The first matchup period will not be retroactively scored and will not count in your league’s stats.

H2H Scenarios

Scenario 1 — Draft ends well before the season opener - Your league drafts and finishes several days before the first MLB game of the season. Since the draft concluded before Sunday Night Baseball on the last day of the first matchup period, your league’s season includes the first matchup period in full.

Scenario 2 — Draft ends after the season starts, but before the cutoff - Your league drafts and finishes after the official start of the MLB season, but still before Sunday Night Baseball begins on the last day of the first matchup period. Your league’s season still includes the first matchup period. However, you will not be able to adjust lineups for any days that had already passed before your draft ended.

Scenario 3 — Draft starts before the cutoff but ends after it - Your league begins drafting before Sunday Night Baseball starts on the last day of the first matchup period, but the draft runs long and finishes after the game begins. Because the draft ended after the cutoff, your league’s season will start at the next full matchup period. The first matchup period will not be retroactively scored.

Scenario 4 — Draft occurs mid-matchup period - Your league drafts in the middle of an ongoing H2H matchup period. Your league’s season will begin at the start of the next full matchup period. Any matchup periods that began before your draft will not be retroactively scored and will not be included in your league’s stats.

Rotisserie (Roto) and Season Points Leagues

For Roto and Season Points leagues, the key cutoff is the first pitch of the day, rather than a specific matchup period boundary. - Draft ends before the first pitch of the MLB season: Your league’s season starts on the first day of the MLB season. - Draft ends after the first pitch of the MLB season has already occurred: The start of your league’s season depends on when your draft finishes relative to that day’s first pitch:

  1. Draft ends before the first pitch of that day: League scoring begins on the same day.
  2. Draft ends after the first pitch of that day; League scoring begins the following day with MLB games. Previous scores will not be retroactively counted.
Roto/Season Points Scenario

Scenario — Draft ends after the first pitch of the day - Your league drafts and finishes after the first MLB game of the day has already begun. Because the draft concluded after that day’s first pitch, your league’s season will start on the next day with MLB games. Stats from prior days will not be retroactively scored and will not be included in your league’s totals.

You cannot edit the number of divisions after the draft. - Multiple Divisions will affect your playoff schedule. Add a Division Click Add a Division (NOTE: Must be even; only 2, 4, 6, 8, etc.). - Name your Division. - To fill the division, use the Dropdown menu next to each Team and select which Division you want them in. - Click on Save Changes. - Remove a Division Move all Teams to a Division you intend to retain. - Once emptied, click on the Delete Division button. - Click on Save Changes.

Games Started / Pitching Limits

The Games Started (GS) limit controls how many starting pitcher appearances count toward your team’s stats each week or season. The rules differ between Head-to-Head and Rotisserie league formats. #### Finding Your Games Started Limit You can find GS-related information in two places: - Current week’s starts: Visit your League Scoreboard and click the Full Box Score link on your matchup. - League GS limit setting: Visit your League Settings page.

Head-to-Head (H2H) Leagues

In League Manager (LM) H2H leagues, the weekly Games Started limit is set by the League Manager. Once the weekly limit is reached: - Starting pitchers will no longer accumulate points or statistics for the remainder of the week. - Relief pitchers are unaffected and will continue to accumulate points and statistics normally.

Important exception — same-day overflow: If your team reaches the weekly limit during a given day’s games, all pitchers who started that day will still receive full credit — even if the total exceeds the limit. The limit then applies beginning the following day. EXAMPLE: Your league has a 12-start weekly limit. You have 10 starts through Saturday. On Sunday, 4 of your pitchers start. All 4 receive full credit, bringing your total to 14. Because the limit was crossed on Sunday (the final day), there are no further starts that week to restrict. MID-WEEK EXAMPLE: Same 12-start limit. You have 10 starts through Wednesday. On Thursday, 4 pitchers start — all 4 receive credit, bringing your total to 14. For Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, no starting pitcher stats will count. #### Rotisserie (Roto) Leagues Rotisserie leagues use a seasonal Games Started limit of 200 starts. How the limit is applied: 1. A team will not accumulate starting pitcher stats beginning the day after the Games Started limit is reached. 2. Because the limit activates the following day, a team may slightly exceed 200 starts.

Example: A manager has 198 Games Started late in the season. On a single day, 5 pitchers start — bringing the total to 203. Starting the next day, the team will no longer receive credit for any starting pitcher stats for the remainder of the season. #### Relief Pitchers Are Never Affected The Games Started limit applies only to starting pitcher appearances. Relief pitcher statistics are always counted, regardless of the GS total. NOTE: If a pitcher who typically starts appears in relief, that outing is counted as a relief appearance — not a start — and is not subject to the Games Started limit.

How does the Trade Deadline work?

The Trade Deadline is the latest a trade can be offered and accepted.  After the trade deadline passes, managers will NOT be able to send/accept trade offers from other teams. This is to ensure the playoffs are not influenced by trades between contenders and eliminated teams.  The date of the Trade Deadline depends on which type of league you are in. #### TRADE DEADLINES IN PUBLIC LEAGUES In all ESPN Public fantasy leagues, there is a universal Trade Deadline set by ESPN. #### TRADE DEADLINES IN LEAGUE MANAGER / CUSTOM LEAGUES When creating a League Manager (LM) league, you can choose different trade deadlines for the available dates/times.  After the trade deadline has passed, managers will NOT be able to send/accept trade offers to other teams. ##### IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS - Trades must be ACCEPTED by the trade deadline - Voting must be finished PRIOR to the trade deadline - Team managers are still free to add and drop players via free agency and waivers throughout the entire season - LM vetoes/upholds must be executed PRIOR to the trade deadline

EXAMPLE SCENARIOS

NOTE: For these examples, the Trade Deadline is August 19 at 12:00 EDT
Scenario #1 

Public League - 1-day trade review period Team A proposed a trade to Team B on Aug 18 at 7 pm EDT, and Team B accepted the offer at 8:30 pm EDT the same day. (would process Aug 19 at 8:30 pm EDT. Other teams will have until the trade deadline (Aug 19 at 12:00 PM EDT) to either vote to uphold or veto the trade. After the deadline, if the trade does not have enough veto votes, it will be processed as normal on August 19 at 8:30 pm EDT. ##### Scenario #2 Public League - 1-day trade review period Team A proposed a trade to Team B on Aug 19 at 11:15 am EDT, and the manager of Team B did NOT see the offer till 1 pm EDT the same day.  Team B will NOT be able to accept the offer as the trade deadline has passed. The trade will automatically disappear when it expires. ##### Scenario #3 Private League - 2-day trade review period Team A proposed a trade to Team B on Aug 18 at 2 pm EDT, and Team B accepted the offer at 8:30 pm EDT the same day (Aug 18). The trade would be scheduled to process on Aug 20 at 8:30 pm EDT.

Other teams will have until the trade deadline (Aug 19, at 12:00 PM EDT) to either vote to uphold or veto the trade. After the deadline, if the trade does not have enough veto votes, it will process as normal on Aug 20 at 8:30 pm EDT. If the League Manager wants to bypass the trade review period, the request must be made BEFORE the trade deadline. For League Managers who want to uphold/veto the trade after the trade deadline has passed, they will need to extend the trade deadline. Please note the deadline CANNOT be reverted to the original.

What is a League ID? 

A League ID is the unique numeric identifier for your league among all ESPN Fantasy leagues. While there are millions of individual leagues, this League ID helps locate your exact league for any troubleshooting you may need. It is very important that you note and keep safe any IDs for the leagues you’re part of, whether public or private. #### Why do I need my League ID? A league ID can be used to locate a league among others when the account email has been lost/compromised. This ID can be used by ESPN Fan Support staff to locate leagues and investigate reported issues. Without the League ID, ESPN cannot guarantee we can locate your league among the millions of others in the system. Keep your league ID in a safe location for future reference, if needed. #### Where can I find a League ID? The League ID can be found in multiple spots. #### Traditional Web Browser - ESPN.com (image: league_ID.png) - 1. Email, text, or direct link invites: - Locate the email, click “join this league”.  A new window will appear from fantasy.espn.com - Within the URL bar of the new window will be LeagueID=

On the ESPN Fantasy App (iOS or Android)

League Manager Powers

The League Manager (LM) is the title of the creator of a League Manager league. As the league creator, the LM has the power to customize the league rules to create the fantasy league of their dreams. The default ruleset is identical to the standard ESPN Fantasy leagues available to the public (referred to as Public Leagues). The LM then gets to decide what options to add/remove, adjust points, add/remove roster slots, set the schedule, draft date/time/type, and more. Because these leagues are highly customized, they are private. This means that the only way to join one is to be invited by the LM via email. Additionally, the LM is the ultimate authority for all aspects of their league, including but not limited to league business, player trades, infractions of these rules, and disputes among franchise team managers. The LM will investigate all overall winners for collusion before awarding overall prizes and it has the right to disqualify team managers or remove them from the leaderboard if deemed necessary. The decisions of the LM shall be final and irreversible. The League Manager has the right to make any necessary changes to the game and rules as the season progresses. Any changes will be properly noted on the league’s homepage. If a League Manager ever wants to relinquish his/her role within a League Manager League, all they have to do is navigate to the “LM Tools” tab and click on “Assign League Manager Powers” and select another team manager for that role.

(NOTE: League CREATOR cannot be removed from the league and will always have a spot in the league as long as the league is active) The use of ESPN.com and participation in ESPN Fantasy games are subject to ESPN’s Terms of Use Agreement.

League Types in ESPN Fantasy

ESPN Fantasy offers two primary league types: Standard Leagues and League Manager (LM) Leagues. The main difference between these league types is who controls the league settings and rules. #### Quick Comparison - Feature: Standard League: League Manager League - League control: ESPN: League Manager - Rule customization: Not available: Fully customizable - Draft setup: Automatic: Controlled by LM - Ideal for: Quick public leagues: Private or custom leagues

Standard Leagues

Standard Leagues are public leagues with preset rules managed by ESPN. These leagues are designed for players who want a quick and simple way to start playing without customizing league settings. ##### Key Characteristics - League rules and scoring are set by ESPN - League operations are automatically managed - Drafts are scheduled automatically - Roster sizes and scoring formats follow standard settings for that sport

Standard leagues are ideal for players who want a ready-to-play fantasy experience. #### League Manager (LM) Leagues League Manager leagues are custom leagues created and controlled by a player, known as the League Manager (LM). The League Manager controls most league settings and can customize the league to suit a specific group or style of play. LM leagues are commonly used by friends, families, coworkers, or established fantasy groups. ##### Customization Options League Managers can adjust settings such as: - Scoring format - Roster size and lineup settings - Draft type and draft schedule - Waiver rules and free agency settings - Trade rules and review process - Playoff format

Some leagues may also use advanced features, including: - Keeper leagues (players can be retained for future seasons) - Offline drafts - Other custom rule configurations

Overall League Participation Limits

Each ESPN Fantasy account can join up to 25 leagues per sport, including both Standard and League Manager leagues. #### Quick Tip If you’re unsure which league type you’re in, check the League Settings page. If the league has a League Manager listed, it is a League Manager League.

Leave a League or Remove a Team Manager

Sometimes you may need to relinquish management of a team. You can always leave your team BEFORE the league draft.  Things get trickier after the draft has occurred. In Public Leagues, you may not leave once the draft has completed.  In League Manager leagues, you can leave your team, but you will need to ask your LM to remove you as a Team Manager. - Click the** Leave League** link on your team page** *****before the league’s draft.***Team managers can’t leave a league after the draft occurs.

How to Remove a Team Manager (LM only / Web Only) - Open** LM Tools. - Click on League Membership Tools. - Click on Edit Managers and Send Invitations. - Click on the red Remove Manager** button to the right of the Team Manager to be removed. - You will be prompted to** sign in** again for confirmation. - You will then need to confirm the removal by clicking on Remove Manager from the pop-up.

Lineup and Roster Lock Times

The Lock Time is when team lineups lock each week. This only applies to moving players between active slots or between active slots and bench slots. Any moves involving trades or add/drops will be locked at the first scheduled game of the day. There are two different types of “locks” – Roster Lock and Lineup Lock - Roster Lock: occurs at the scheduled game time of the first MLB game of the day. (e.g., if the first game is scheduled at 2:10 pm ET but the first pitch does not happen till 2:15pmET, the roster still locks at 2:10pmET) Any players added or dropped via free agency, waivers, trades, or by activating/putting players on the IL will not appear on your roster until the following day or the next matchup, depending on the Lineup Lock setting. (Note: Roster locking will occur at the start of the first game of the day, even if that game is between AL or NL opponents.) - Lineup Lock: Depending on your league settings, your active team lineup will lock daily or weekly. More information about Lineup Locks is available below.

NOTE: In League Manager Leagues, the League Manager may change the Lineup Lock Time settings up until one hour prior to the draft. #### Lineup Change Settings available in League Manager Leagues - Daily - Lock Individually at Scheduled Game TimeThis is the default setting and is used by most leagues. Team managers can make moves to their rosters until the scheduled start of each player’s game. Only players whose games have started will be locked, and the remaining players whose games have not started will remain unlocked and can be shifted.

  • Team managers can make moves to their roster until the scheduled first game of the week. Once the first pitch of the day is thrown, the entire roster will be locked, and moves can no longer be made for the current day.

  • Each roster position will lock once the game of the player slotted has started. Team managers can still make moves to other roster positions until the game starts for the player slotted. The entire lineup will then be locked for the rest of the period and cannot be modified until the following match.

  • All roster moves will lock at the first game of the week, even if the first game falls on a Thursday. Once the first game of the scoring period starts, the entire roster is locked for the rest of the period and cannot be changed until the following matchup.

Making a Private League Viewable to the Public (LM Only)

By default, all League Manager Leagues are Private.  This means that only members of that league can view it. League managers can set their league to public. Public leagues can be viewed by anyone at any time. NOTE: All leagues, Public and Private, Standard and League Manager are obligated to adhere to the ESPN Rules of Conduct and Fair Play. Please review Offensive Content and Team Managers. Important: Making your league viewable does not make it joinable. All League Manager leagues remain private — this setting only controls whether non-members can view certain pages via a shared link. It can be changed at any time during the season. Pages non-members can view (when given a direct URL): - League Office, Standings, Box Scores, and Team Pages.

Pages that are always private, regardless of this setting: - The list of team managers and league message boards is never visible to non-members.

To make a League Public or Private (Web Only):

  1. Go to the** League** tab
  2. Click Settings
  3. Click Basic Settings
  4. Click Edit Basic Settings
  5. Set the public viewability option to Yes to allow non-members to view league pages when given a direct URL (such as one shared via email or a message board)
  6. Click on Save Changes

Offensive Content and Team Managers

ESPN Fantasy Sports are available to everyone with the understanding that we are here for fun. However, a distinction must be made between playful banter between competitors and abuse/hostility.  ALL leagues, ESPN Standard and League Manager, both Public and Private, are subject to the ESPN Terms of Use** and Fair Play and Conduct when playing Fantasy games on ESPN. #### Team managers are expected to communicate in a respectful and gracious manner** - Threats and obscenities are against the rules and are illegal in many jurisdictions. - Team managers who send threatening emails to another team manager will be warned and/or kicked out of the game and can be banned from ESPN.com altogether. - Threats and obscenities are not allowed at any time.

Offensive language, league, or team names are prohibited

  • Any posts, including league and team names, that are derogatory in nature are strictly prohibited. This restriction includes chat rooms, message boards, and the league’s bulletin board.
  • There is a zero-tolerance level concerning offensive posts, including personal attacks, sexist remarks, and/or racist remarks.

Violators of the above rules are subject to being banned from ESPN.com and/or Disney sites. Furthermore, violations containing threats may be referred to the appropriate authorities.

REGULAR SEASON SCHEDULE 

All Standard leagues play with a fixed 22-week regular season. To view your team’s schedule, click on the “Schedule” link on your main team page. To view any individual matchup period, click the main “Scoreboard” tab (it defaults to the current period). NOTE: Matchup (period) 1 is 9 game days, and matchup 16 (All-Star break) is 14 game days. #### REACHING THE PLAYOFFS The top four teams in a league make the playoffs. These four are comprised of the two-division champs and two wild-card teams. Division champs are the teams that win the league divisions. The next two teams, according to the tie-breaker below, are the wild-card teams. #### PLAYOFF BRACKET SETUP The Head-to-Head fantasy playoffs take place during the last four weeks. To view your league playoff bracket, click on the “Playoff Bracket” link on the “Scoreboard” tab. The playoffs start on MLB Week 23 and run through MLB Week 26 of the MLB season (4 weeks). Round 1 takes place during Weeks 23 and 24 (two weeks), and Round 2 takes place during Weeks 25 and 26 (two weeks). #### PLAYOFF SCHEDULE In Round One of the playoffs, the division winner with the best win/loss record plays the wild-card team with the worst win/loss record; the other division winner plays the wild-card team with the better win/loss record. In Round Two, the winners of Round One (see table below) compete for the League Championship. Each round of the playoffs spans a two-week period. The remaining teams in each league compete in the consolation bracket. League Championship bracket: - 1st place - Winner of game 1, round 2 - 2nd place - Loser of game 1, round 2 - 3rd place - Winner of game 2, round 2 - 4th place - Loser of game 2, round 2

Consolation bracket:  - 5th place - Winner of game 1, round 2 - 6th place - Loser of game 1, round 2 - 7th place - Winner of game 2, round 2 - 8th place - Loser of game 2, round 2 - 9th place - Winner of game 3, round 2 - 10th place - Loser of game 3, round 2

Scoring Formats

STANDARD SCORING FORMATS (Free) 

Standard leagues have five scoring formats available during league creation: These are the most commonly used scoring formats in fantasy baseball are Rotisserie and Head-to-Head: Each Category. The five formats are defined below. #### LEAGUE MANAGER LEAGUE SCORING FORMATS  League Manager leagues can be created using one of five different scoring formats. These formats can be further customized by the league creator by tweaking individual categories and points. The five formats are defined below: - Rotisserie - Head-to-Head: Points - Head-to-Head: Each Category - Head-to-Head: Most Categories - Season Points

Rotisserie

Rotisserie, or “Roto,” is the most common way to play fantasy baseball. In this scoring type, teams are ranked from first to last in each statistical category. Points are then awarded according to the order in each category and totaled to determine an overall score and league rank. #### Head-to-Head: Points H2H Points is very similar to how fantasy football is played. It allows you to assign a point value to individual statistic categories (e.g., HR=4, RBI=1), and each scoring period’s winner is determined solely by which team accumulates the most fantasy points against a single opponent. The end result is a win (1-0-0), loss (0-1-0), or tie (0-0-1). If selected, your league will have team schedules/playoffs, and you will have the option to set up divisions. #### Head-to-Head: Each Category H2H Each Category is the most common type of head-to-head play in fantasy baseball. It allows you to select the “X” number of statistical categories. For each scoring period, team totals are accumulated, and a win, loss, or tie is credited in each category based on the matchup results (i.e., 6-3-1 in a 10-category league). If selected, your league will have team schedules/playoffs, and you will have the option to set up divisions. NOTE: If the League Manager sets Home Team wins as a tiebreaker, the home team will win every tied category. #### Head-to-Head: Most Categories H2H Most Categories allows you to set “X” number of statistic categories. For each scoring period (usually Monday through Sunday), team totals are accumulated across each category. At the end of the scoring period, the winner is determined by which team wins the most categories. The end result is a win (1-0-0), loss (0-1-0), or tie (0-0-1). These results correspond directly to each team’s overall record. If selected, your league will have team schedules/playoffs, and you will have the option to set up divisions. #### Season Points Season Points scoring allows you to assign a point value to each statistical category (e.g., HR=4, RBI=1). Standings are based on the accumulation of points across all statistical categories and are combined into a single total points column. The team with the most overall points wins.

Scoring Settings

When creating a League Manager (LM) league, you can choose from many different scoring options. Our default settings will be pre-selected, and these can be edited by clicking on the “Scoring” link. On this page, all of the available stat categories and their corresponding point values can be edited to create your league’s unique scoring system. Edit Scoring Settings (Web Only) - In “League Manager” Leagues, the League Manager needs to click on the “LM Tools” tab. - Click on “Edit League Settings”. - Scroll down to the “Scoring” section and click  “Edit”. - You can edit any scoring for any stat group on the next page. Be sure to click “Submit Scoring Settings” when done. - ​If any settings are changed, the action will be listed in your league’s Transaction Log page.

NOTE: Scoring categories and their corresponding point values can be changed by the League Manager in a League Manager League at any time during the season. If either is changed after the season has begun, the system will automatically change all previous game results to match the changed settings.

Standard Scoring for Public Baseball leagues

Listed below are the standardized scoring for categories and points in all ESPN Fantasy Baseball public leagues. #### Points and categories for “Head-to-Head (H2H)” and “Season Points” leagues ##### Batting: Runs Scored (R) 1 Total Bases (TB)  1 Runs Batted In (RBI) 1 Walks (BB) 1 Strikeouts (K) -1 Stolen Bases (SB) 1 ##### Pitching: Innings Pitched (IP)  3 Hits Allowed (H) -1 Earned Runs (ER) -2 Holds (HD) 2 Walks Issued (BB) -1 Strikeouts 1 Wins (W) 5 Losses (L) -2 Saves (SV) 5 #### Categories for “Most Categories”, “Each Category”, and “Rotisserie (ROTO)” leagues ##### Batting: Runs Scored (R) Home Runs (HR) Runs Batted In (RBI) Stolen Bases (SB) Batting Average (AVG) ##### Pitching: Strikeouts (K) Wins (W) Saves (SV) Holds (HD) Earned Run Average (ERA) Walks plus Hits per Innings Pitched (WHIP)​

Stat Corrections

Sometimes during the fantasy season, you may find that one of your players has had their points changed. A player’s score/stats will be impacted when the official MLB statistics used to calculate them are adjusted, updated, or corrected. ESPN always works to ensure that matchup scores accurately reflect the real, official MLB statistics and if you notice changes, it is to correct previously incorrect data or react to a stat correction from the league. There are several scenarios when you might see these changes: 1. Live Scoring – During the game, scores/stats are updated as they are received. This information may change as more accurate data from the league is reported. Each player’s individual points and stats will be accurately reflected once the game is final. 2. Post-game adjustments – There are times when the MLB decides to adjust stats after a game has been concluded. For example, during the game the MLB credits one player with a single then after the post-game review decides the player had reached on a fielding error by an outfielder. 3. Post-game corrections – Sometimes ESPN receives incorrect data in the stats feeds. Most of the time when inaccurate data is detected, the incorrect score/stat is corrected within minutes. Rarely, incorrect scores/stats may not be corrected until the next day. This type of stat correction can appear up to seven (7) days after the game was played. 4. League Manager changes: In League Manager H2H POINTS leagues, the LM has the power to adjust scores manually. The reasons for changing a player’s score are completely up to the League Manager.  CAUTION: If the LM notices the incorrect scoring before ESPN has updated the stats and uses the Adjust Scoring League Manager tool to manually change the score then afterward when the system updates automatically to reflect the same correction, the impacted team will be awarded double credit for the correction. If this occurs, you should contact your LM and ask them to re-adjust the scoring by reversing their manual adjustment.

ADDITIONAL NOTES: - The deadline for all weekly scoring or stat corrections made by the system during the season is 7 days after the game in question. - Only official stat corrections made by the MLB after a game’s conclusion will appear on the stat correction page. https://fantasy.espn.com/baseball/statcorrections Corrections to incorrect data received by ESPN will NOT appear on that page - Any changes entered in the system will reflect in both your Box Score and your Standings pages, via overnight update.

Team Manager Inactivity (LM Leagues)

The League Manager may contact the team managers of teams that remain inactive for extended periods. - The League Manager will send notifications to the email on record for the inactive team manager. - If the account still remains inactive after the email was sent by the League Manager, the League Manager reserves the right to reassign team managership of the inactive team.

Team Manager Invitation Issues (LM Leagues)

There are three common scenarios related to Team Manager issues:

No Invitation Received

If your League Manager claims to have sent you an invitation to the league, but you never received one in your inbox, there are a couple of potential reasons why: - Your League Manager could have entered your email address incorrectly. Double-check that they used your correct email address. - Your corporate or ISP’s firewall might potentially block emails from ESPN servers. We recommend that your League Manager use the “Send Me a Copy of Each Invite” option.

Once your League Manager receives the “cc’ed” email containing your team’s unique join URL, they can forward it to you from their personal email. #### Invitation Received but Unable to Join If you received the invitation from your League Manager, but the unique URL page says you can’t join the league, there is a potential reason why: - Your League Manager changed your email address after sending you the unique URL invitation, thereby nullifying and voiding the original invitation. Contact your League Manager to determine if this was the case.

Other Options Available

  • Speak to your League Manager about another email invitation; you can do this by removing and re-adding your email to the league.
  • Use an alternate email address, preferably one that is not work-related, such as Hotmail, Outlook, or Gmail.
  • Be sure to check your spam and junk folders, as it may have bounced in there by mistake. If that’s the case, add espnfantasy@fantasygames.com to your contact list.

What happens if a professional game is suspended then resumed at a later date?

If the suspended game is resumed within seven (7) days of being suspended, all stats from the suspended game will count for the scoring period when the game began. If the suspended game is resumed after eight (8) or more days have passed, the stats from the resumed portion of the game will not count towards your fantasy output or totals. This is consistent with how other Stat Corrections are handled. #### EXAMPLE A game on Monday is suspended and then resumed on Friday. The points/stats for both parts of the game will appear in Monday’s results. NOTE: This is the case even if the resumption of the suspended game occurs within the next matchup period. Additionally, your team will accrue points/stats generated in the resumed game based on the players who were in your original lineup on Monday (not those in your lineup on Friday). Please note that stats from the resumed portion of the game may not appear immediately on the site or in the app. The points/stats will appear overnight, the day the game concludes.

Fantasy Baseball: Managing Your Team

Adjusting Fantasy Alert Preferences

The ESPN Fantasy app allows users to customize their alert settings across all different Fantasy Games. You can even change specific settings for each individual league.

In the ESPN app settings menu, select Alert Preferences.

From the Alert Preferences menu, you can toggle Game Alerts and News Alerts for each of the Fantasy sports offered on ESPN.com (Football, Baseball, Hockey, or Men’s and Women’s Basketball)

Game Alerts refer to the results of your Fantasy teams and players. News Alerts cover real-world news and results from professional leagues.

Scrolling further down on this menu will allow you to customize alerts for each individual Fantasy League you manage.

Just select any one of your leagues from the list to open a new alert menu. You can turn alerts on or off for categories such as Trades, Add/Drops, Home Runs, etc. 

Changes in alert settings to one league won’t affect any others. Alerts settings will have to be customized for each league individually.

Fair Play / Conduct: Impeding Other Team Managers

ESPN Fantasy Sports is a place for sports fans to have fun competing with each other while enjoying the sports we love. ESPN is committed to providing a fair and respectful experience for everyone. The following behaviors are examples of unacceptable behaviors. Please note this is NOT a comprehensive list. - Losing games solely to deny another team’s manager the chance to make the playoffs - Cycling through players in free agency to make them unavailable to other teams in your league - Collusive trading where one team obtains top-ranked players for bottom-ranked players in order to stack one team at the expense of another

How do I create a League Message?

League Message Boards are only available in League Manager (LM) leagues. IMPORTANT NOTE: Even though LM leagues are private, everyone is still accountable for adhering to the ESPN Fair Play and Conduct Policy. 1. Tap on your league from the League Directory. 2. You will then see a list of conversations in that League. 3. To add a direct or group conversation, tap the create message icon and select one or more league mates to create a private conversation.

After a waiver period has concluded, or in a league that does not use waivers, all players will be listed as free agents. You will see a green “Add” button (Free Agent; immediately available) or a yellow “Claim” button (On Waivers; not available until the waiver claims process). 3. Select the player you would like to drop 4. Confirm the transaction. 

If the player is a Free Agent, the transaction will execute immediately and the new player will appear on your bench. 5. If you are claiming a player, you must wait for league’s waivers to process.

Lineup Protection

The Lineup Protection feature provides lineup insurance.  This optional feature handles the case where a player in your starting lineup is marked “Out” or on “IL” but still occupies a starting slot on your roster. With Lineup Insurance active, a player from your bench who is eligible and available for that slot will be selected and replaced for you. NOTE: This only replaces players who are “Out” or “IL” with available, eligible players on your bench.  It is NOT a lineup optimizer!

Move a Player On or Off Injured Reserve (IR) or Injured List (IL)

The system will automatically assign the IR (injured reserve) or Injured List (IL) tag to a player once ESPN receives a report from the real-world leagues (NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL, or WNBA). NOTE: Only players with the (IR), (IL), or (O) tag can be placed on the IR (injured reserve) or IL (Injured List) slot. All other players must be moved to the bench if you do NOT want them on the active roster. NOTE: IL and Day to Day (DTD) are only used by MLB and Fantasy Baseball. LM NOTE: League Managers can increase the number of IR/IL slots in their league’s Roster Settings after the league draft; however, it is not possible to reduce the number of IR slots at any time after the draft. #### Managing IR/IL on the ESPN Fantasy App - On your team’s home page, click on any IR/IL-eligible player. - In addition to the Bench slot, IR/IL-eligible players will have an option to be placed in the IR slot. - It should be noted that this option will only appear in leagues that use IR slot(s)- if you don’t see an IR/IL slot open to receive your player, it could mean that your player is not eligible for IR/IL or that your league doesn’t include an IR/IL slot in the league’s custom settings. - League Managers can enable IR/IL slots in a league by going under the “League Manager Tools” tab and selecting “Edit League Settings.” - To activate an injured player from IR/IL, click on that player and then select an empty roster space, either on the bench or starting lineup, for him to fill. This may require dropping a player if the team’s roster is full.

Managing IR/IL on the Web - ESPN.com

  • Click on the “Manage IR/IL” link at the top of your team page and follow the instructions in order to place a player on IR
  • To move a player back from IR/IL to your active roster, follow the same steps - click on the “Manage IR/IL” link on your team page and then activate the player
  • Note that the link will only appear in leagues that use IR/IL slot(s). If you don’t see the link, let your League Manager know he or she needs to add that feature
  • League Managers can enable IR/IL slots in a league by going under the “League Manager Tools” tab and selecting “Edit League Settings.”

Moving Players After Rosters Have Locked

Why Are Some of My Players Locked?

Player slots lock individually as each NFL game kicks off — so if you left an injured player in an active slot and their game has already started, you won’t be able to swap them out for this week. Once a player’s slot is locked, only your League Manager (LM) can make roster changes on your behalf. This is how the LM keeps things fair and prevents any mid-game lineup adjustments that could give a team an unfair advantage. #### Roster Adjustment on the ESPN Fantasy App (LM Only) - Tap on “League Manager Tools” in the three stacked lines icon (AKA the ‘burger’).

  • Tap on “Edit Rosters” under the Roster Tools section.

  • Select the team to edit and move the player(s) as desired.

Roster Adjustment on the Web - ESPN.com (LM Only)

  • Click the “League Manager Tools” tab

  • Click “Edit Rosters” under the Roster Tools section

  • Select the team to edit and move the player(s) as desired.
