If a league is not full, it will NOT convert into draft mode, and the draft time will be rescheduled.IMPORTANT: League Managers, make sure that all of your league’s team managers have joined the league at least one hour before your draft! If not, then you will have to select a new Draft Date/Time.

Salary Cap Draft

Salary Cap Drafts use a competing-offer format and differ considerably from traditional Snake Live Drafts. In Salary Cap Drafts, two first-round ranked players could be signed by the same team, which would rarely happen in a Snake Draft, because both players are so early and close to one another in the Snake Draft ranking order. For example, in ESPN Fantasy Baseball, it’s possible to get Shohei Ohtani and Aaron Judge on the same team in a Salary Cap Draft, but that is almost impossible to achieve in a Snake or Auto-draft. - Private league LMs can edit the budget under draft settings. - Salary Cap drafts are available to Standard (Public)  and League Manager (LM) Leagues. - Teams can sign any player, provided they have the funds available. - Public leagues are set up with a preset $200 budget to sign enough players to fill their rosters.

NOTE: ALL teams will start the draft with the same budget. If you are in a keeper league and have different “salaries” for keepers, please visit “Keeper Leagues.” - To edit draft settings pre-draft, please visit “Pre-Draft League Manager Abilities.” - To edit in-draft settings, please visit “Salary Cap Draft- League Manager Tools.”

Process:

  1. Once a player is nominated for signing, the offer process begins.
  2. Team managers can offer any monetary value that their budget permits.
  3. Team managers continue to submit offers until only a single high-salary offer remains. The system will then alert team managers, and the winning team will have the winning salary amount deducted from their budget.
  4. This process repeats until EVERY team’s roster is completely filled.
  5. When the draft is complete, the league will move into “in-season” mode, where teams can start making roster moves, waiver claims, trades, etc.

NOTE: Unused budgets DO NOT carry over into* “in-season”* mode. There is no advantage in finishing the draft with a remaining budget!

Salary Cap Draft: Absentee Team Managers

It is strongly recommended that all team managers be present when the draft begins. #### If Team Managers Are Missing - If one or two managers are missing, the League Manager should pause the draft and attempt to contact them. - If three or more managers are missing, it is recommended to reset the draft for a later time when more managers can attend.

How Auto Draft Works for Absent Managers

  • Any team whose manager is not present will be placed on Auto.
  • The system will actively draft players on their behalf.

During Auto drafting: - The system may offer up to a randomly determined percentage of the player’s preset salary limit. - If no salary limit is preset, the system will use the default value.

This ensures that absent team managers can still build a competitive team. #### If a Manager Gets Disconnected - If a team manager loses connection during the draft, their team will automatically switch to Auto mode.

Salary Cap Draft: League Manager Tools

In League Manager leagues, League Managers (LMs) have full commissioner controls over the league, including draft admin functions at any time during the draft. These admin functions can be accessed in the “LM Tools” tab in the LM’s main window. The LM can perform the following draft functions if the draft is paused: #### Pause Draft LMs can pause the draft at any time. If the LM pauses the draft the countdown clock stops. The app displays a “Draft is Paused” message. Once the LM resumes the draft, the clock will start for the current offer. #### Configure Time LMs can set the time for each nomination and offer. The system default for both is 30 seconds and can be changed by 5-second increments. Once the draft is resumed, the new time configurations will be in place. #### Reset Draft (on the web only) LMs can “reset” the draft at any time. If the draft is reset, the Salary Cap draft will start over from scratch: all players returned, all winning offers refunded, all picks reversed. #### Undo Picks LMs have the ability to “undo” any picks during any rounds. If the draft is in the 5th round and LM decides to undo a 2nd-round pick, doing so will also undo any picks made after that pick.

Salary Cap Drafts - How to Draft

Things to Know for Salary Cap Drafts

Nominating a Player
  • Team managers have 30 seconds to nominate a player.
  • To nominate, select a player from the main Players table (shows the player’s image and stats).
  • If no player is selected within 30 seconds, the system auto-nominates in this order:

Top player in the Player Queue panel (if any) - The available player with the highest starting salary - The default nomination offer is $1. - The nominating manager can raise the offer before submitting.

What Happens After a Nomination
  • Once nominated, the player appears at the top of the screen (with profile and stats) under the list of team managers.
  • The countdown clock begins immediately.
Making Offers
  • The offer clock starts at 30 seconds.
  • Any offer made with 10 seconds or less remaining will reset the clock back to 10 seconds. This continues until the player is won.

Offers can be placed in two ways: - +1 bidding - Entering a custom dollar amount

The app includes two buttons for submitting an offer (depending on how you’re bidding). ##### Offer Limits and Max Bids - The current offer is shown on the right and will also indicate whether you’re winning. - Teams can only bid amounts that still allow them to fill the rest of their roster with at least $1 per remaining roster slot. - You can view a team’s maximum offer by hovering over the team jerseys. - The maximum offer can also be displayed via an option in the Options tab. - Once a team reaches its max offer:

The app will reject additional bids - Offer buttons will be grayed out

Salary Cap Drafts - In Draft Process

When you enter the Salary Cap Draft, you will see this as the home screen (the example is from Fantasy Football but the format is identical): (image: mceclip0.png) There are a few places to get to know within the draft. Please reference the following locations on the screen (corresponding letters and descriptions follow): A. Toggle “Auto” on or off B. The starting salary amount for each player. Displayed in the column with the “$” C. Search players by position D. Search players by team E. Button to “Queue” a player for signing F: Nomination and Offer area #### Things to know for Salary Cap Drafts: - Team managers have 30 seconds to nominate a player to be put up for signing. - Players are nominated for signing by selecting them in the main players table, displaying the player’s image and their stats. - If no player is selected within the 30-second time frame, the system will automatically nominate a player in the following priority:

The top player in the Player Queue panel (if any). - The player with the highest starting salary that is still available. - The default offer for all player nominations is $1.

This amount can be raised by the nominating team manager before submitting it if desired.

A successfully nominated player appears, with stats and a profile, in the top area of the screen under the list of team managers, and the countdown clock commences. The offering clock countdown will start at 30 seconds and any offers inside of 10 seconds remaining will reset the clock back to 10 seconds until an offer is won. Offers can be made on a “+1” basis or by manually entering a dollar amount. There are two buttons in the application to submit an offer. The current offer amount for the player up for drafting is displayed as the current offer on the right. This will also tell you if you have the winning offer or not. Teams can only offer dollar amounts, allowing at least $1 for each remaining roster slot. A team’s maximum offer is viewable by hovering over the team hats. The maximum offer can also be set as an option in the options tab. t

Snake Draft Settings for LM leagues

In League Manager (custom) leagues, League Managers (LMs) have full commissioner controls over the league, including draft admin functions at any time during the draft. These admin functions can be accessed in the “LM Tools” tab in the LM’s main window. The LM can perform the following draft functions if the draft is paused: 1. Pause Draft:  LMs can pause the draft at any time. If the LM pauses the draft, the countdown clock stops, and the app displays a “Draft is Paused” message. Once the LM resumes the draft, the clock will start for the current offer. 2. Allow managers who have disconnected to remain off autopick until their allotted pick time expires. Choosing these settings would allow more time for managers who are not present more often to join the draft. 3. Configure Time:  LMs can set the time per pick. The system default is 30 seconds. Once the draft is resumed, the new time configurations will be in place. 4. Make picks for other managers (draft on behalf of missing managers) Use this to draft for managers who could not attend the draft (or LM can let the system autopick; it’s all up to the LM!). The league will see a message indicating LM is picking on behalf of someone, then the LM can proceed to the Players tab and pick. 5. Reset Draft (on the web only):  LMs can “reset” the draft at any time.  NOTE for Salary Cap Drafts: If a Salary Cap draft is reset, the draft will start over from scratch: all players are returned to teh draft pool, all winning offers are refunded, and all picks are reversed as if the draft never happened. 6. Undo picks LMs have the ability to “undo” any picks during any rounds. If the draft is in the 5th round and LM decides to undo a 2nd-round pick, doing so will also undo any picks made after that pick.

Trade Draft Picks

Draft Pick Trading enables Team Managers to trade draft slots - for example, a team manager might trade their 2nd and 3rd round pick slots to another team manager for their 1st round pick slot in return. Trades can be performed on the ESPN Fantasy App and on the web. NOTE: Draft Pick Trading is only available if it is enabled by the LM. #### Trade Draft Picks on the ESPN Fantasy App ##### Trade Draft Picks in a Non-Keeper League - Go to “Opposing Teams” and select the team you want to trade with - Click on “Propose Trade - Propose the draft pick trade

Note: If you trade and receive a net total of draft picks greater than the number of rounds in the draft (i.e., more players than you have roster slots for), your draft will end once you’ve reached the maximum, and you won’t be able to select any more players. If you have traded away multiple picks but not received as many in return, you will end the draft with empty roster slots and be required to fill via Free Agency after the draft has finished. Draft pick trading is available until one hour before your draft. ##### Trade Draft Picks in a Keeper League - Draft pick trades can be made as a swap of picks or as a combination of keepers and picks. Draft pick trades can only be done prior to the Keeper deadline for League Manager LeaguesThe Keeper deadline is determined by League Managers

Trade Draft Picks On the Web

Trade Draft Picks in a Non-Keeper League
  • Go to the “Opposing Teams” menu and select the team you want to trade with
  • Click on “Propose Trade”.
  • Propose the draft pick trade
Trade Draft Picks In a Keeper League
  • Draft pick trades can be made as a straight-up swap of picks or as a combination of keepers and picks. Draft pick trades can only be done prior to the Keeper deadline for League Manager Leagues
  • You are trading for a team manager’s pick in a given round, not the pick itself
  • If there’s no assurance that your League Manager won’t switch the draft order, it might be wise to avoid making such a trade. Otherwise, that 2nd overall pick you thought you traded for could become the 10th pick just like that

Bonus Wins and Losses (LM Leagues Only)

Bonus Wins and Losses is a setting in League Manager (LM) leagues only that rewards teams that may score a ton of points but face high-scoring teams more often than not. LMs can activate this scoring setting to award an additional Win or Loss based on a team’s matchup score versus the rest of the league. - If the team’s scoring matchup places them in the top half of the league for that week, that team will receive an extra Win. - If that team’s matchup score for the week is in the bottom half of the rest of the league for that week, the team will receive an additional loss.

Deleting a league that has conducted a draft is a serious decision, as league deletion is final and can NOT be reversed by anyone, including ESPN! #### To Delete Your League (Web Only) 1. Click on LM Tools 2. Click on Delete League under League and Scoring Settings ToolsYou will be presented with a** confirmation pop-up. This pop-up warns that deleting a league is final and cannot be reversed. 3. Click on the red Delete League** button to continue the deletion process.Another pop-up will confirm your decision to delete your league.  This is the last chance to change your mind. 4. Click on** Confirm** to delete your league. All league information will be deleted and can not be recovered or restored by anyone, including ESPN. 5. Your league will disappear in a few minutes.

Fair Play/Conduct (Collusive Transactions)

Collusive Transactions: When one team makes moves to benefit another team without trying to improve its own position. - An example of collusive transactions is one-sided trades or dropping a player so another team can pick up that player. - Teams found in violation of this policy will be canceled and their team managers prohibited from participating in future ESPN Fantasy Games. - Standard league members are expected to veto/protest all unfair/collusive trades. Four votes are required in a Standard league for a trade to be denied. - ​In League Manager leagues, a different veto system may be in place to veto all trades. For more information on vetoing trades, click here.

Fair Play/Conduct (Multiple Teams)

Fair Play and Conduct

  • One person cannot manage more than one team in the same league.
  • If two or more teams in the same league are under the same account, the teams must be controlled by different people sharing an account.
  • Violations of this will lead to disqualifications of teams from the league and cancellations of the team.

How do I create a League Message?

League Message Boards are only available in League Manager (LM) leagues. IMPORTANT NOTE: Even though LM leagues are private, everyone is still accountable for adhering to the ESPN Fair Play and Conduct Policy. 1. Tap on your league from the League Directory. 2. You will then see a list of conversations in that League. 3. To add a direct or group conversation, tap the create message icon and select one or more league mates to create a private conversation.

  2. Email Invite: Email invites provide each recipient with a unique link through which they can join your league. Only your League Manager can designate who is invited. Invites can be sent out by entering each email address into the “New Invitations” textbox.

Issues Joining a League

If you’re having issues joining your league, try the following steps: - Try telling your League Manager to resend the invitation to your email address. If you still don’t receive an email in your inbox, try an alternate email address - Be sure to check your spam and junk folders, as it may have been bounced in there by mistake. If so, add espnfantasy@fantasygames.go.com to your contact list - Your corporate or ISP’s firewall might potentially block emails from ESPN servers. We recommend your League Manager uses the “Send Me a Copy of Each Invite” option. Once your League Manager receives the “cc’ed” email containing your team’s unique join URL, they can forward it to you off their personal email.

If you received an invite, but can’t join, try the following steps: Note: If you are getting an error or it says your league is full (even though it isn’t showing as full), your League Manager likely invited you via the web (desktop, laptop, etc.), which reserves your place in the league. If you are in the app and trying to accept the invite, your League Manager likely invited you via the web AND the app. The web overrides the app invite, so you will be sent the error message. Simply have your League Manager delete the web invite and only send it to you through the app. Or you can always just accept the invite through the web (desktop, laptop, etc.) - Your League Manager changed your email address after inviting you, thereby voiding the invitation - Talk with your League Manager and make sure you have the right email address in place - If problems persist, you may be having account issues. Click here for additional information on how to fix any account issues.

Keeper Leagues

Keeper leagues (also known as Dynasty leagues) allow Team Managers to keep players on their roster over multiple seasons without having to redraft them.  Keepers are only available in League Manager leagues.  Team Managers may select as few players or as many players as the league creator selected during league creation. For example, if your league allows 3 Keepers per team, a Team Manager may elect to designate between 0-3 players to stay on their roster for the next season. League Manager can enable or disable Keeper settings via LM Tools. #### A few important facts about Keepers on ESPN Fantasy:  - The default draft method in Keeper leagues is to draft/assign selected Keepers in the first rounds.  Keeper rounds are Non-Snake. (For Snake Drafts) This means that if the league allows 2 keepers in the upcoming draft, the first 2 rounds would be non-snake. 1-10, 1-10, then from the 3rd round, 1-10, 10-1, 1-10, etc.

  • Example: Last season, a Team Manager drafted a player in the 5th round.  The Team Manager decides to mark that player as one of their team’s Keepers for the next season.  When the next season’s draft occurs, that Keeper will be drafted automatically in the 5th round.

To enable Keepers in an LM league:

  1. Open** LM Tools**
  2. Go to League and Scoring Settings Tools
  3. Select League Settings
  4. Select** Transactions and Keepers**
  5. Scroll down to Keepers Rules and click on Edit
  6. Click on Yes for Use Keepers for (next) Season.
  7. You can now select how many players can be designated as a Keeper (Minimum 1, maximum full roster size)
  8. You can set the date when Keepers Lock. The default is one hour before your next season Draft Date/Time.
  9. Click Save Changes

Keeper Salaries

Keeper salaries are how much a manager will “pay for” out of their salary cap prior to the draft in order to keep that player. Kind of how draft right works.  Most leagues use the player salaries from the prior season(s), but LM’s can change that. ##### To Edit Keeper Salaries 1. Open** LM Tools 2. Go to League and Scoring Settings Tools 3. Select League Settings 4. Select Transactions and Keepers 5. Scroll down to Keepers Rules and click on Edit 6. Click on Edit Keeper Salaries. 7. You can now select the salary. 8. Click Save Changes**

Change Keeper Lock Date

NOTE: Once the keeper lock date passes, only the league manager will be able to modify a team’s keeper selection.  Alternatively, choose “Lock One Hour before Draft” to allow league members to edit their keepers in the last minute. 1. Open** LM Tools 2. Go to League and Scoring Settings Tools 3. Select League Settings 4. Select Transactions and Keepers 5. Scroll down to Keepers Rules and click on Edit 6. You can set the date when Keepers Lock. The default is one hour before your next season Draft Date/Time. 7. Click Save Changes**

What is a League ID? 

A League ID is the unique numeric identifier for your league among all ESPN Fantasy leagues. While there are millions of individual leagues, this League ID helps locate your exact league for any troubleshooting you may need. It is very important that you note and keep safe any IDs for the leagues you’re part of, whether public or private. #### Why do I need my League ID? A league ID can be used to locate a league among others when the account email has been lost/compromised. This ID can be used by ESPN Fan Support staff to locate leagues and investigate reported issues. Without the League ID, ESPN cannot guarantee we can locate your league among the millions of others in the system. Keep your league ID in a safe location for future reference, if needed. #### Where can I find a League ID? The League ID can be found in multiple spots. #### Traditional Web Browser - ESPN.com (image: league_ID.png) - 1. Email, text, or direct link invites: - Locate the email, click “join this league”.  A new window will appear from fantasy.espn.com - Within the URL bar of the new window will be LeagueID=

  • Locate the invite message
  • Within the link, you will be able to find LeagueID=

On the ESPN Fantasy App (iOS or Android)

  • Access your league under the “League” tab.
  • Click “League Info”
  • League ID is available to view.

League Manager Powers

The League Manager (LM) is the title of the creator of a League Manager league. As the league creator, the LM has the power to customize the league rules to create the fantasy league of their dreams. The default ruleset is identical to the standard ESPN Fantasy leagues available to the public (referred to as Public Leagues). The LM then gets to decide what options to add/remove, adjust points, add/remove roster slots, set the schedule, draft date/time/type, and more. Because these leagues are highly customized, they are private. This means that the only way to join one is to be invited by the LM via email. Additionally, the LM is the ultimate authority for all aspects of their league, including but not limited to league business, player trades, infractions of these rules, and disputes among franchise team managers. The LM will investigate all overall winners for collusion before awarding overall prizes and it has the right to disqualify team managers or remove them from the leaderboard if deemed necessary. The decisions of the LM shall be final and irreversible. The League Manager has the right to make any necessary changes to the game and rules as the season progresses. Any changes will be properly noted on the league’s homepage. If a League Manager ever wants to relinquish his/her role within a League Manager League, all they have to do is navigate to the “LM Tools” tab and click on “Assign League Manager Powers” and select another team manager for that role.

(NOTE: League CREATOR cannot be removed from the league and will always have a spot in the league as long as the league is active) The use of ESPN.com and participation in ESPN Fantasy games are subject to ESPN’s Terms of Use Agreement.

League Types in ESPN Fantasy

ESPN Fantasy offers two primary league types: Standard Leagues and League Manager (LM) Leagues. The main difference between these league types is who controls the league settings and rules. #### Quick Comparison - Feature: Standard League: League Manager League - League control: ESPN: League Manager - Rule customization: Not available: Fully customizable - Draft setup: Automatic: Controlled by LM - Ideal for: Quick public leagues: Private or custom leagues

Standard Leagues

Standard Leagues are public leagues with preset rules managed by ESPN. These leagues are designed for players who want a quick and simple way to start playing without customizing league settings. ##### Key Characteristics - League rules and scoring are set by ESPN - League operations are automatically managed - Drafts are scheduled automatically - Roster sizes and scoring formats follow standard settings for that sport

Standard leagues are ideal for players who want a ready-to-play fantasy experience. #### League Manager (LM) Leagues League Manager leagues are custom leagues created and controlled by a player, known as the League Manager (LM). The League Manager controls most league settings and can customize the league to suit a specific group or style of play. LM leagues are commonly used by friends, families, coworkers, or established fantasy groups. ##### Customization Options League Managers can adjust settings such as: - Scoring format - Roster size and lineup settings - Draft type and draft schedule - Waiver rules and free agency settings - Trade rules and review process - Playoff format

Some leagues may also use advanced features, including: - Keeper leagues (players can be retained for future seasons) - Offline drafts - Other custom rule configurations

Overall League Participation Limits

Each ESPN Fantasy account can join up to 25 leagues per sport, including both Standard and League Manager leagues. #### Quick Tip If you’re unsure which league type you’re in, check the League Settings page. If the league has a League Manager listed, it is a League Manager League.

Leave a League or Remove a Team Manager

Sometimes you may need to relinquish management of a team. You can always leave your team BEFORE the league draft.  Things get trickier after the draft has occurred. In Public Leagues, you may not leave once the draft has completed.  In League Manager leagues, you can leave your team, but you will need to ask your LM to remove you as a Team Manager. - Click the** Leave League** link on your team page** *****before the league’s draft.***Team managers can’t leave a league after the draft occurs.

How to Remove a Team Manager (LM only / Web Only) - Open** LM Tools. - Click on League Membership Tools. - Click on Edit Managers and Send Invitations. - Click on the red Remove Manager** button to the right of the Team Manager to be removed. - You will be prompted to** sign in** again for confirmation. - You will then need to confirm the removal by clicking on Remove Manager from the pop-up.

Lineup Lock Times

The Lineup Lock Time is when team lineups lock each week. This applies to moving players between active slots, or between active slots and bench slots. NOTE: In League Manager Leagues, the League Manager may change the Lineup Lock Time settings up until one hour prior to the draft. Below are the two options available in League Manager Leagues: - Lock Individually at Scheduled Gametime: This is the default setting and is used by the majority of leagues. If selected, team managers can make moves to their weekly rosters until the scheduled kickoff time of each player’s game. - Lock at First Game of the Week: All roster moves will lock at the first game of the week, even if the first game falls on a Thursday.

Making a Private League Viewable to the Public

Making a Private League Viewable to the Public (LM Only) By default, all League Manager Leagues are Private.  This means that only members of that league can view it. League managers can set their league to public. Public leagues can be viewed by anyone at any time. NOTE: All leagues, Public and Private, Standard and League Manager are obligated to adhere to the ESPN Rules of Conduct and Fair Play. Please review Offensive Content and Team Managers . Important: Making your league viewable does not make it joinable. All League Manager leagues remain private — this setting only controls whether non-members can view certain pages via a shared link. It can be changed at any time during the season. Pages non-members can view (when given a direct URL): - League Office, Standings, Box Scores, and Team Pages.

Pages that are always private, regardless of this setting: - The list of team managers and league message boards is never visible to non-members.

To make a League Public or Private (Web Only):

  1. Go to the** League** tab
  2. Click Settings
  3. Click Basic Settings
  4. Click Edit Basic Settings
  5. Set the public viewability option to Yes to allow non-members to view league pages when given a direct URL (such as one shared via email or a message board)
  6. Click on Save Changes

Offensive Content and Team Managers

ESPN Fantasy Sports are available to everyone with the understanding that we are here for fun. However, a distinction must be made between playful banter between competitors and abuse/hostility.  ALL leagues, ESPN Standard and League Manager, both Public and Private, are subject to the ESPN Terms of Use** and Fair Play and Conduct when playing Fantasy games on ESPN. #### Team managers are expected to communicate in a respectful and gracious manner** - Threats and obscenities are against the rules and are illegal in many jurisdictions. - Team managers who send threatening emails to another team manager will be warned and/or kicked out of the game and can be banned from ESPN.com altogether. - Threats and obscenities are not allowed at any time.

Offensive language, league, or team names are prohibited

  • Any posts, including league and team names, that are derogatory in nature are strictly prohibited. This restriction includes chat rooms, message boards, and the league’s bulletin board.
  • There is a zero-tolerance level concerning offensive posts, including personal attacks, sexist remarks, and/or racist remarks.

Violators of the above rules are subject to being banned from ESPN.com and/or Disney sites. Furthermore, violations containing threats may be referred to the appropriate authorities.

Position Eligibility

  • The NBA sends ESPN an updated list of every player’s position eligibility, including rookies, prior to the start of each season.
  • ESPN reserves the right to designate a different position for a player.
  • Once the season has begun, ESPN cannot change the primary position. However, a player can gain additional eligibility for other positions during the season if circumstances warrant it. *****
  • League Managers DO NOT have the ability to change a player’s position.

***  Under certain circumstances, ESPN reserves the right to change a player’s primary position. NOTE**: It’s important to note that roster minimums and maximums within your league’s settings relate to the primary position only (the first position listed next to a player), not any secondary positions granted.

Regular Season and Playoffs Schedule in Standard Leagues

REGULAR SEASON SCHEDULE

All Standard leagues play with a fixed 19-week regular season. To view your team’s schedule click on the “Schedule” link on your main team page. To view any individual matchup period click on the main “Scoreboard” tab (it will default to the current period). #### REACHING THE PLAYOFFS The top four teams in a league make the playoffs. These four are comprised of the two division champs and two wild-card teams. Division champs are the teams that win the league divisions. The next two teams according to the tie-breaker below are the wild card teams. #### PLAYOFF BRACKET SETUP The Head-to-Head fantasy playoffs take place during the last four and half weeks of the NBA’s regular season. To view your league’s playoff bracket click on the “Playoff Bracket” link on the “Scoreboard” tab. The playoffs start on Week 20 and run through the end of the NBA’s regular season (4½ weeks). Round 1 takes place during Weeks 20 and 21 (two weeks), and Round 2 takes place during Weeks 22 and 23 (2 weeks). #### PLAYOFF SEEDING AND TIEBREAKERS (Standard Leagues) When your league converts into playoff mode the system automatically generates a seed for each team in the league based on the regular season results. The seeds determine where the system places each team in the playoffs. The primary factors which determine seeds are: In the event that two or more teams have the same winning percentage at the conclusion of the regular season, and have played the same number of head-to-head games between them, the following tiebreaking system determines the seed:

winning percentage. 

In the event that two or more teams have the same winning percentage at the conclusion of the regular season, and have NOT played the same number of head-to-head games between them, the following tiebreaking system determines seed: 1. Overall Record 2. Division Record 3. Coin Flip

SCORING DURING THE PLAYOFFS

Scoring during the playoffs works much the same way as during the regular season, with the object to win as many categories as possible. The big difference is that each playoff round lasts two weeks, not one week (as during the regular season). As such the Games Started Limits are increased and you get two full weeks to accumulate stats in each stat category. By winning 6 or more of the 10 categories during each playoff matchup you’ll guarantee yourself a win. In the event that two teams have the same win-loss-tie record at the conclusion of their two-week playoff game, the following tie-breaking system is employed: #### Tie Breaker for Playoff Games Higher seeded team Note: During the playoffs, once your matchup ends, the scoring is final and no scoring corrections will be applied. All Standard leagues play with a fixed 19-week regular season. After that, the playoffs begin! To view your team’s schedule click on the “Schedule” link on your main team page. To view any individual matchup period click on the main “Scoreboard” tab (it will default to the current period). #### PLAYOFF SCHEDULE - “Who plays Who?” In Round One of the playoffs, the division winner with the best win/loss record plays the wild-card team with the worst win/loss record; the other division winner plays the wild-card team with the better win/loss record. In Round Two, the winners of Round One (see table below) compete for the League Championship. Each round of the playoffs spans a two-week period. The remaining teams in each league compete in the consolation bracket. From the League Championship bracket: - 1st place - Winner of game 1, round 2 - 2nd place - Loser of game 1, round 2 - 3rd place - Winner of game 2, round 2 - 4th place - Loser of game 2, round 2

From the Consolation Bracket - 5th place - Winner of game 1, round 2 - 6th place - Loser of game 1, round 2 - 7th place - Winner of game 2, round 2 - 8th place - Loser of game 2, round 2 - 9th place - Winner of game 3, round 2 - 10th place - Loser of game 3, round 2

Scoring Formats

STANDARD SCORING FORMATS (Free) 

Standard leagues have five scoring formats available during league creation: These are the most commonly used scoring formats in fantasy baseball are Rotisserie and Head-to-Head: Each Category. The five formats are defined below. #### LEAGUE MANAGER LEAGUE SCORING FORMATS  League Manager leagues can be created using one of five different scoring formats. These formats can be further customized by the league creator by tweaking individual categories and points. The five formats are defined below: - Rotisserie - Head-to-Head: Points - Head-to-Head: Each Category - Head-to-Head: Most Categories - Season Points

Rotisserie

Rotisserie, or “Roto,” is the most common way to play fantasy baseball. In this scoring type, teams are ranked from first to last in each statistical category. Points are then awarded according to the order in each category and totaled to determine an overall score and league rank. #### Head-to-Head: Points H2H Points is very similar to how fantasy football is played. It allows you to assign a point value to individual statistic categories (e.g., HR=4, RBI=1), and each scoring period’s winner is determined solely by which team accumulates the most fantasy points against a single opponent. The end result is a win (1-0-0), loss (0-1-0), or tie (0-0-1). If selected, your league will have team schedules/playoffs, and you will have the option to set up divisions. #### Head-to-Head: Each Category H2H Each Category is the most common type of head-to-head play in fantasy baseball. It allows you to select the “X” number of statistical categories. For each scoring period, team totals are accumulated, and a win, loss, or tie is credited in each category based on the matchup results (i.e., 6-3-1 in a 10-category league). If selected, your league will have team schedules/playoffs, and you will have the option to set up divisions. NOTE: If the League Manager sets Home Team wins as a tiebreaker, the home team will win every tied category. #### Head-to-Head: Most Categories H2H Most Categories allows you to set “X” number of statistic categories. For each scoring period (usually Monday through Sunday), team totals are accumulated across each category. At the end of the scoring period, the winner is determined by which team wins the most categories. The end result is a win (1-0-0), loss (0-1-0), or tie (0-0-1). These results correspond directly to each team’s overall record. If selected, your league will have team schedules/playoffs, and you will have the option to set up divisions. #### Season Points Season Points scoring allows you to assign a point value to each statistical category (e.g., HR=4, RBI=1). Standings are based on the accumulation of points across all statistical categories and are combined into a single total points column. The team with the most overall points wins.

Scoring Settings

When creating a League Manager (LM) league, you can choose from many different scoring options. Our default settings will be pre-selected, and these can be edited by clicking on the “Scoring” link. On this page, all of the available stat categories and their corresponding point values can be edited to create your league’s unique scoring system. Edit Scoring Settings (Web Only) - In “League Manager” Leagues, the League Manager needs to click on the “LM Tools” tab. - Click on “Edit League Settings”. - Scroll down to the “Scoring” section and click  “Edit”. - You can edit any scoring for any stat group on the next page. Be sure to click “Submit Scoring Settings” when done. - ​If any settings are changed, the action will be listed in your league’s Transaction Log page.

NOTE: Scoring categories and their corresponding point values can be changed by the League Manager in a League Manager League at any time during the season. If either is changed after the season has begun, the system will automatically change all previous game results to match the changed settings.

Team Manager Inactivity (LM Leagues)

The League Manager may contact the team managers of teams that remain inactive for extended periods. - The League Manager will send notifications to the email on record for the inactive team manager. - If the account still remains inactive after the email was sent by the League Manager, the League Manager reserves the right to reassign team managership of the inactive team.

Team Manager Invitation Issues (LM Leagues)

There are three common scenarios related to Team Manager issues:

No Invitation Received

If your League Manager claims to have sent you an invitation to the league, but you never received one in your inbox, there are a couple of potential reasons why: - Your League Manager could have entered your email address incorrectly. Double-check that they used your correct email address. - Your corporate or ISP’s firewall might potentially block emails from ESPN servers. We recommend that your League Manager use the “Send Me a Copy of Each Invite” option.

Once your League Manager receives the “cc’ed” email containing your team’s unique join URL, they can forward it to you from their personal email. #### Invitation Received but Unable to Join If you received the invitation from your League Manager, but the unique URL page says you can’t join the league, there is a potential reason why: - Your League Manager changed your email address after sending you the unique URL invitation, thereby nullifying and voiding the original invitation. Contact your League Manager to determine if this was the case.

Other Options Available

  • Speak to your League Manager about another email invitation; you can do this by removing and re-adding your email to the league.
  • Use an alternate email address, preferably one that is not work-related, such as Hotmail, Outlook, or Gmail.
  • Be sure to check your spam and junk folders, as it may have bounced in there by mistake. If that’s the case, add espnfantasy@fantasygames.com to your contact list.

Select the player you would like to drop 4. Confirm the transaction. 

If the player is a Free Agent, the transaction will execute immediately and the new player will appear on your bench. 5. If you are claiming a player, you must wait for league’s waivers to process.

ON ESPN.com FANTASY

  5. You now have three choices:

Select from ESPN Fantasy Logo Packs. Choosing this lets you choose from a variety of pre-generated logos. 6. Upload From Your Device. Drop a Player

Drop a Player on the ESPN Fantasy App

  1. Tap on the Roster tab
  2. Tap the NAME of the player you wish to drop.
  3. Tap the Drop Player button to process the transaction.NOTE: Some players will have a “Can’t Drop” status, indicating they are currently on the Undroppable Players list.
  4. You will need to confirm the transaction before it is processed.

Drop a Player On Web

  1. Click on the My Team tab in the clubhouse
  2. Click on the NAME of the player you wish to drop.
  3. The Player Card will open. Click on the red Drop button.  NOTE: Some players will have a “Can’t Drop” status, indicating they are currently on the Undroppable Players list.
  4. A confirmation pop-up will appear. Click on Confirm to execute the drop.

Fair Play/Conduct: Impeding Other Team Managers

ESPN Fantasy Sports is a place for sports fans to have fun competing with each other while enjoying the sports we love. ESPN is committed to providing a fair and respectful experience for everyone. The following behaviors are examples of unacceptable behaviors. Please note this is NOT a comprehensive list. - Losing games solely to deny another team’s manager the chance to make the playoffs - Cycling through players in free agency to make them unavailable to other teams in your league - Collusive trading where one team obtains top-ranked players for bottom-ranked players in order to stack one team at the expense of another

Games Played Limit

On ESPN Fantasy Basketball, Games Played Limit indicates the number of games a team may use in a given matchup. If a team exceeds this value, it will continue to accrue stats for the rest of the day until the end of matchup. This value represents the limit for a standard matchup,  which is 7 days in length. Longer or shorter matchups will have their limits scaled proportionally. For example: In a normal H2H leagues where it ends on Sunday night and league settings have 42 games set as the limit, - If Team A has 41 games by the end of Saturday’s games, Team A can start whatever amount of players for Sunday. - If Team A has 41 games by the end of Thursday’s games, Team A can start whatever amount of players on Friday. If he starts even 1 player on Friday, his Saturday and Sunday’s stats will not be counted. This is because at start of Saturday’s game, the team has 42 games played and that is the limit.

In another words: If a team starts the day below the limit, the team can go over such limit till all his players finishes playing for the day. If a team starts the day over or at the limit, stats won’t count until end of matchup.

Join a Private League

Private leagues are an option available only in League Manager leagues. To join one, you must be invited by the League Manager (LM).

  1. All invitations to join Private Leagues are sent in the form of an email containing a unique URL. This unique URL is the ticket to play in the league.
  2. Click on the URL or copy and paste it into your browser’s ‘Address’ field to accept the invitation.
  3. Upon joining, your ESPN.com Member ID will be associated with a Team ID and you will become a team manager.
  4. Only league creators can invite people to play in their private league.

Join a Public (Standard) League

Public leagues offer the opportunity to dive right into fantasy sports by providing a prebuilt league with standardized rules. ESPN offers a wide variety of options for players of every level. ESPN acts as the commissioner for these leagues to ensure a fair and friendly environment for everyone to enjoy Fantasy Sports. All Team Managers must adhere to theESPN Code of Conduct. NOTE: Once your Public League has drafted, you may not leave that league. #### Joining a Public (Standard) League On the ESPN Fantasy App 1. Open the** ESPN Fantasy App** and sign in. 2. At the top of the screen, scroll to** Create or Join A League. 3. Swipe (left/right) to locate the Fantasy Game you wish to play. 4. Select Join a Public League**. 5. You can now make a series of selections to find the best Public League for you to join: Your Experience Level - We’ll match you with leagues that have players of similar experience. 6. Scoring type 7. Draft Type 8. Draft Date & Time

  2. Click on the Sign Up link
  3. Click on** Join a Public League**

Lineup and Roster Lock Times

The Lock Time is when team lineups lock each week. This ONLY applies to moving players between active slots, or between active slots and bench slots. Any moves involving trades or add/drops will be locked at the first scheduled game of the day. There are two different types of “locks” – Lineup Lock and Roster Lock. Rosters (meaning the makeup of players on the team) are still locked at the start of the day or week as has always been the case. NOTE: In League Manager Leagues, the League Manager may change the Lineup Lock Time settings up until one hour prior to the draft. #### Below are the two options available in League Manager Leagues: - Lock Individually at Scheduled Game Time: This is the default setting and is used by the majority of leagues. If selected, team managers can make moves to their weekly rosters until the scheduled start of each player’s game. Only players whose games have started will be locked. The remaining players whose games have not started will remain unlocked and can be shifted. - Lock at First Game of the Day/Week: All roster moves will lock at the first game of the day/week, even if the first game falls on a Thursday. Once the first game starts for the scoring period, the entire roster is locked for the rest of the period and cannot be changed until the next scoring period.

Moving Players on and off of the Injured Reserve (IR) and Injury List (IL)

The system will automatically place the IR (injured reserve) or Injury List (IL) tag on a player once ESPN receives the league report. NOTE: Only players with the (IR), (IL), or (O) tag can be placed on the IR (injured reserve)/Injury List (IL) slot. All other players must be moved to the bench if you do NOT want them on the active roster. NOTE: IR/IL is available in all Standard leagues and only in League Managers that use IR/IL slot(s). If you don’t see the link, let your League Manager know they need to add this feature. - League Managers can enable IR/IL slots in a league by going under the LM Tools tab and selecting Edit League Settings.

Managing IR on the ESPN Fantasy App

  1. On your team’s Roster page, click on the** IR or IL button**
  2. ​You will be provided with a short list of players eligible for the IR/IL slot and a list of either open slots or players already in those slots.
  3. Tap To IR/IL to move the player into an open slot
  4. If you have no open slots, you will need to select a player to move from IR/IL by tapping on the Activate button.
  5. You will see a confirmation pop-up as this change is automatically saved.

Managing IR on ESPN.com

  1. Click on the Manage IR/IL link at the top of your team page a
  2. You will be shown a short list of IR/IL eligible players. Click on To IR/IL to place them in an available IR/IL slot. NOTE: If all of your IR/IL slots are occupied, you will need to Activate a player to make the change.

To move a player back from IR to your active roster, follow the same steps: 1. Click on the Manage IR/IL link at the top of your team page a 2. You will be shown a short list of players in your IR/IL. Click on Activate a player to move the player to your active roster.

Naming Your Team

Team Names Overview

Your team name has two parts: a Location (such as a city or region) and a Nickname (such as your team’s actual name). Each part has a maximum of 15 characters. There’s no rule against two teams in the same league sharing a name, so get creative! You can also set a 4-character abbreviation for your team. Pro Tip: Several pages in the app use only abbreviations, so we recommend choosing one that makes sense on its own. Good to know: If you’re joining an existing team, it may already have a name — but you can change it at any time during the season, so don’t worry if you inherit something you’re not crazy about! IMPORTANT NOTE: Offensive team names in ESPN Fantasy leagues are subject to change and may result in further consequences. Please review our Offensive Content and Team Managers policy for more details. #### On the ESPN Fantasy App (Mobile) 1. Tap your team icon from the My Team dropdown to go to your Team Homepage 2. Tap your team icon again to open your Team Info section 3. Tap Edit in the top-right corner 4. Update your Location, Nickname, and/or abbreviation as desired 5. Tap Save when you’re done

On ESPN.com (Desktop)

  1. Click the Team Settings link in your team’s navigation menu, or find it just beneath your team logo
  2. Update your Location, Nickname, and/or abbreviation as desired
  3. Click Save when you’re done

Offensive Content and Team Managers

ESPN Fantasy Sports are available to everyone with the understanding that we are here for fun. However, a distinction must be made between playful banter between competitors and abuse/hostility.  ALL leagues, ESPN Standard and League Manager, both Public and Private, are subject to the ESPN Terms of Use** and Fair Play and Conduct when playing Fantasy games on ESPN. #### Team managers are expected to communicate in a respectful and gracious manner** - Threats and obscenities are against the rules and are illegal in many jurisdictions. - Team managers who send threatening emails to another team manager will be warned and/or kicked out of the game and can be banned from ESPN.com altogether. - Threats and obscenities are not allowed at any time.

Offensive language, league, or team names are prohibited

  • Any posts, including league and team names, that are derogatory in nature are strictly prohibited. This restriction includes chat rooms, message boards, and the league’s bulletin board.
  • There is a zero-tolerance level concerning offensive posts, including personal attacks, sexist remarks, and/or racist remarks.

Violators of the above rules are subject to being banned from ESPN.com and/or Disney sites. Furthermore, violations containing threats may be referred to the appropriate authorities.

Stat corrections

Sometimes during the fantasy season, you may find that one of your players has had their points changed. A player’s score/stats will be impacted when the official NBA statistics used to calculate them are adjusted, updated, or corrected. ESPN always works to ensure that matchup scores accurately reflect the real, official NBA statistics and if you notice changes, it is to correct previously incorrect data or react to a stat correction from the league. There are several scenarios when you might see these changes: 1. Live Scoring – During the game, scores/stats are updated as they are received. This information may change as more accurate data from the league is reported. Each player’s individual points and stats will be accurately reflected once the game is final. 2. Post-game adjustments – There are times when the NBA decides to adjust stats after a game has been concluded. For example, during the game the NBA credits one player with a block, then after the post-game review decides instead to award him with a steal instead. This type of stat correction can appear up to seven (7) days after the game was played. 3. Post-game corrections – Sometimes ESPN receives incorrect data in the stats feeds. Most of the time when inaccurate data is detected, the incorrect score/stat is corrected within minutes. Rarely, incorrect scores/stats may not be corrected until the next day. 4. League Manager changes: In League Manager H2H points leagues, the LM has the power to adjust scores manually. The reasons for changing a player’s score are completely up to the League Manager.  CAUTION: If the LM notices the incorrect scoring before ESPN has updated the stats and uses the Adjust Scoring League Manager tool to manually change the score then afterward when the system updates automatically to reflect the same correction, the impacted team will be awarded double credit for the correction. If this occurs, you should contact your LM and ask them to re-adjust the scoring by reversing their manual adjustment.

ADDITIONAL NOTES: - The deadline for all weekly scoring or stat corrections made by the system during the season is the Saturday following the week of the game in question. - Only official stat corrections made by the NBA after a game’s conclusion will appear on the stat correction page. Corrections to incorrect data received by ESPN will not appear on that page - Any changes entered in the system will automatically reflect in both your Box Score and your Standings pages.

Undroppable Players List

The Undroppable Players List is a list of the top Fantasy players who can’t be sent to waivers/free agency. Without this feature, a team manager who is out of contention could drop a star player for their buddy, who is first on the waiver order, to pick up, thereby bolstering their team for the playoffs. Please Note: If a player designated Undroppable becomes injured, this does not mean they will be automatically removed from the ESPN Undroppable List. Players are put on the list before the season begins due to their star potential. ESPN may choose not to remove a player from the list who is still expected to return at some point during the season/playoffs. The Undroppable Player List is used in all Standard Leagues. In a League Manager League, the League Manager (LM) can turn off the Undroppable List by doing the following: #### Turn off Undroppable Players List for League Manager leagues (Web Only).  NOTE: If necessary, the LM can do this temporarily. Once a player is dropped, the LM can turn it on again to prevent further drops. 1. Click on the** LM Tools** tab 2. Click on Edit League Settings 3. Click on Edit next to Player Rules 4. Select No next to Observe ESPN’s Undroppable Player List 5. Save Changes

H2H Each Category League: Playoff Seeding Tiebreakers

When your fantasy league enters playoff mode, every team receives a seed based on their regular season results. That seed determines their bracket position. This article explains how seeds are assigned and how ties are broken in H2H Each Category leagues. Applies to: H2H Each Category leagues with playoff settings. For H2H Points leagues or H2H Most Categories leagues, refer to the tiebreaker articles for those formats. #### How Seeds Are Assigned When the regular season ends, the system assigns seeds automatically using two primary factors, in order: 1. Division Winners — Division winners always occupy the top seeds. This step is skipped in leagues with no divisions. 2. Winning Percentage — Among remaining seeds, the team with the best winning percentage earns the higher seed.

Reminder: Division winners always claim the first seeds in the bracket. In LM leagues, the League Manager has final authority over playoff rules. #### Tiebreaker Sequence: H2H Each Category When two or more teams finish with identical winning percentages, the following tiebreakers are applied in order. Once a team is seeded, the process resets from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams. - Step: Tiebreaker: How it works - 1: H2H Record (among tied teams)* Default setting; can be changed by the League Manager: Best head-to-head record among the tied teams wins. Only valid if all tied teams have played each other an equal number of times; otherwise, skip to Step 2. - 2: Intradivisional Record Only applies in leagues with multiple divisions*: Best head-to-head record within the same division wins. - 3: Coin Flip: A virtual coin flip determines the seed if all other tiebreakers are exhausted.

Tiebreaker Example: Four Teams, All have 86–88–16 records

The following example walks through the full seeding process for a four-team tie competing for seeds #3 through #6. All teams finished 86–88–16. - Team: Division: Intradivisional Record: vs. A: vs. B: vs. C / vs. D - Team A: Div 1, 2nd: 56–54–10: —: 6–4 (1 game): vs. C: 6–4 (1 game) vs. D: 6–4 (1 game) - Team B: Div 2, 2nd: 64–52–4: 4–6 (1 game): —: vs. C: 10–10 (2 games) vs. D: 16–4 (2 games) - Team C: Div 2, 3rd: 32–70–18: 4–6 (1 game): 10–10 (2 games): vs. D: 10–10 (2 games) - Team D: Div 2, 4th: 33–69–18: 4–6 (1 game): 4–16 (2 games): vs. C: 10–10 (2 games)

Round 1: Determine the #3 Seed (Teams A, B, C, D)

We start with H2H records among all four teams: - Team A: played 3 games among the tied group - Team B: played 5 games among the tied group - Team C: played 5 games among the tied group - Team D: played 5 games among the tied group

H2H tiebreaker is invalid: The four teams did not all play each other an equal number of times (Team A played only 3 games vs. the others’ 5). We move to Intradivisional Record. Intradivisional Record comparison (by winning percentage): - Team A: 56–54–10 (.509) - Team B: 64–52–4 (.547) ← best - Team C: 32–70–18 (.317) - Team D: 33–69–18 (.325)

Team B earns the #3 seed. Reset: The tiebreaker process restarts from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams (A, C, and D). ##### Round 2: Determine the #4 Seed (Teams A, C, D) We check H2H records among the three remaining teams: - Team A: played 2 games among the remaining group - Team C: played 3 games among the remaining group - Team D: played 3 games among the remaining group

H2H tiebreaker is invalid: Teams A, C, and D did not all play each other an equal number of times. We move to Intradivisional Record. Intradivisional Record comparison: - Team A: 56–54–10 (.509) ← best - Team C: 32–70–18 (.317) - Team D: 33–69–18 (.325)

Team A earns the #4 seed. Reset: The tiebreaker process restarts from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams (C and D). ##### Round 3: Determine the #5 Seed (Teams C and D) We check H2H records between the two remaining teams: - Team C vs. Team D: 10–10 across 2 games — a draw

H2H tiebreaker is a draw: A tied head-to-head record doesn’t break the tie. We move to Intradivisional Record. Intradivisional Record comparison: - Team C: 32–70–18 (.317) - Team D: 33–69–18 (.325) ← better

Team D earns the #5 seed. Team C receives the #6 seed. #### League Manager (LM) Leagues In LM leagues, the League Manager can customize or override the default tiebreaker sequence using the Edit Playoffs page in LM Tools. Best practice: If your league uses custom tiebreakers, define and publish them clearly on the League Office page before the season begins to avoid disputes.

H2H Most Categories League Playoff Seeding: How Tiebreakers Work

When your fantasy league enters playoff mode, every team receives a seed based on its regular-season results. That seed determines their bracket position. This article explains how seeds are assigned and how ties are broken in H2H Most Categories leagues. Applies to: H2H Most Categories leagues with playoff settings. For H2H Points leagues or H2H Each Categories leagues, refer to the tiebreaker articles for those formats. #### How Seeds Are Assigned When the regular season ends, the system assigns seeds automatically using two primary factors, in order: 1. Division Winners — Division winners always occupy the top seeds. This step is skipped in leagues with no divisions. 2. Winning Percentage — Among remaining seeds, the team with the best winning percentage earns the higher seed.

Reminder: Division winners always claim the first seeds in the bracket. In LM leagues, the League Manager has final authority over playoff rules. #### Tiebreaker Sequence: H2H Most Categories When two or more teams finish with identical winning percentages, the following tiebreakers are applied in order. Once a team is seeded, the process resets from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams. - Step: Tiebreaker: How it works - 1: H2H Record (among tied teams)* Default setting; can be changed by the League Manager: Best head-to-head record among the tied teams wins. Only valid if all tied teams have played each other an equal number of times; otherwise, skip to Step 2. - 2: Intradivisional Record Only applies in leagues with multiple divisions*: Best head-to-head record within the same division wins. - 3: Coin Flip: A virtual coin flip determines the seed if all other tiebreakers are exhausted.

Tiebreaker Example: Three Teams, All with 8–8–3 records

The following example walks through the full seeding process for a three-team tie. All teams finished 8–8–3. - Team: Division: Intradivisional Record: H2H vs. A: H2H vs. B - Team A: Div 1, 2nd: 4–3–2: —: 1–0 - Team B: Div 2, 2nd: 6–2–1: 0–1: — - Team C: Div 2, 3rd: 3–5–1: 0–0–1 (tie): 1–1–1

Step 1: Check H2H Records Among All Three Teams

We compare how many times each team played the others: - Team A played 2 games among the tied group (1–0–1 overall) - Team B played 4 games among the tied group (1–2–1 overall) - Team C played 4 games among the tied group (1–1–2 overall)

H2H tiebreaker is invalid: The three teams did not all play each other an equal number of times (Team A only played 2 games vs. the others’ 4). We move to Intradivisional Record. ##### Step 2: Compare Intradivisional Records Comparing winning percentages within each team’s division: - Team A: 4–3–2 (.556) - Team B: 6–2–1 (.722) ← best - Team C: 3–5–1 (.389)

Team B earns the top seed among the three tied teams. Reset: The tiebreaker process now restarts from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams (A and C). ##### Step 3: Break the Tie Between Teams A and C Both teams are 8–8–3. We start again at H2H record: - Team A vs. Team C: 0–0–1 (they tied their only matchup)

H2H tiebreaker is a draw: A tied matchup doesn’t break the tie. We move to Intradivisional Record. Intradivisional Record comparison: - Team A: 4–3–2 (.556) ← better - Team C: 3–5–1 (.389)

Team A earns the next seed. Team C receives the final seed. What if Teams A and C had identical intradivisional records? If both were, say, 4–4–1, the next tiebreaker would be a coin flip. #### League Manager (LM) Leagues In LM leagues, the League Manager can customize or override the default tiebreaker sequence using the Edit Playoffs page in LM Tools. Best practice: If your league uses custom tiebreakers, define and publish them clearly on the League Office page before the season begins to avoid disputes.

H2H Points League Playoff Seeding: How Tiebreakers Work

When your fantasy league enters playoff mode, every team receives a seed based on its regular-season results. That seed determines their bracket position. This article explains how seeds are assigned and how ties are broken. Applies to: H2H Points leagues with playoff settings, and all ESPN Fantasy Football leagues (which use the H2H Points format). For H2H Most Categories or H2H Each Category leagues, refer to the tiebreaker article for those formats. #### How Seeds Are Assigned When the regular season ends, the system assigns seeds automatically using two primary factors, in order: 1. Division Winners — Division winners always occupy the top seeds. This step is skipped in leagues with no divisions. 2. Winning Percentage — Among non-division-winner seeds, the team with the best winning percentage earns the higher seed.

Reminder: Division winners always claim the first seeds in the bracket. In LM leagues, the League Manager has final authority over playoff rules. #### Standard Tiebreaker Sequence When two or more teams finish the regular season with identical winning percentages, the following tiebreakers are applied in order until the tie is resolved. Once a team is seeded, the process restarts from the top for the next seed. - Step: Tiebreaker: How it works - 1: H2H Record (among tied teams): Best head-to-head record among the tied teams wins. Only valid if all tied teams have played each other an equal number of times; otherwise, skip to Step 2. - 2: Points For: Most total points scored during the regular season wins. - 3: Intradivisional Record: Best head-to-head record within the same division wins. - 4: Points Against: Most points scored against the team wins. A higher total suggests a tougher schedule. - 5: Coin Flip: A virtual coin flip determines the seed if all other tiebreakers are exhausted.

Tiebreaker Process: Two Teams Tied

  1. Compare H2H records between the two teams. Best record wins.
  2. If H2H records are equal, compare Points For. Most points wins.
  3. If Points For are equal, compare Intradivisional Record.
  4. If Intradivisional Record is equal, compare Points Against. Most points wins.
  5. If still tied, a** virtual coin flip** determines the seed.

Tiebreaker Process: Multiple Teams Tied

When more than two teams are tied, the process works one seed at a time — determine the top seed among the tied group, remove that team, then repeat for the next seed. 1. Compare H2H records among all tied teams. The team with the best overall record earns the top seed. 2. Among the remaining tied teams, compare H2H records again. 3. If the remaining teams did not play each other an equal number of times, skip to Points For. The team with the highest Points For earns the next seed. 4. Repeat until all tied teams are seeded.

Key rule: After each seed is assigned, the tiebreaker process resets from Step 1 (H2H Record) for the remaining tied teams. #### Tiebreaker Example: Five Teams, All win 7–5 records The following example shows the full seeding process for a five-team tie. All teams finished 7–5. - Team: Division / Standing: Points For: H2H Results vs. Other Tied Teams - Team A: Div 1, 3rd: 825: Beat B and E; lost to C and D - Team B: Div 1, 2nd: 918: Beat C; lost to A and E; did not play D - Team C: Div 2, 1st ★: 725: Beat A; lost to B, D, and E - Team D: Div 2, 2nd: 720: Beat A, C, and E; did not play B - Team E: Div 1, 1st ★: 920: Beat B and C; lost to A and D

★ = Division winner ##### Step 1: Seed the Division Winners (#1 and #2 seeds) Teams E and C are division winners. They go to the top two seeds. To determine which gets #1: - Team E beat Team C in their head-to-head matchup. - Team E → #1 seed. Team C → #2 seed.

No divisions? If your league has no divisions, skip this step. The team with the best winning percentage earns the #1 seed directly. ##### Step 2: Determine the #3 Seed (Teams A, B, D) All three teams are 7–5. We start with H2H records among the three: - Team A: 1–1 (beat B, lost to D) - Team B: 0–1 (lost to A; did not play D) - Team D: 1–0 (beat A; did not play B)

H2H tiebreaker is invalid here: The three teams did not all play each other an equal number of times (B and D never met). We move to Points For. Points For comparison: - Team A: 825 - Team B: 918 ← highest - Team D: 720

Team B earns the #3 seed. ##### Step 3: Determine the #4 Seed (Teams A and D) The tiebreaker resets. Both teams are 7–5. We compare their head-to-head matchup: - Team D beat Team A.

Team D earns the #4 seed. Team A receives the #5 seed. ##### League Manager (LM) Leagues In LM leagues, the League Manager can customize or override the default tiebreaker sequence using the Edit Playoffs page in LM Tools. Best practice: If your league uses custom tiebreakers, define and publish them clearly on the League Office page before the season begins to avoid disputes. Grandfathered Custom Leagues only: ”Most Points from Bench” is available as a tiebreaker option exclusively for grandfathered Custom Leagues that used this rule in prior seasons. It is not available for new leagues.

Playoff Scoring & Tiebreakers

Scoring

Playoff scoring follows the same rules as the regular season, with one key difference: Standard leagues: Each playoff round spans two weeks rather than the one-week matchup periods used during the regular season. League Manager leagues: Each playoff round is two weeks by default, but the LM can adjust the length to their desires. #### Tiebreakers If a playoff matchup ends in a tie: - The higher-seeded team advances. This is the default behavior in both standard leagues and League Manager leagues. - League Manager leagues: The League Manager has final authority over which team advances in a tied matchup. Custom tiebreaker systems can be configured using the Edit Head-to-Head Schedule option in LM Tools. The League Manager manually advances the winning team under the league’s chosen tiebreaker rules. - Grandfathered Custom Leagues only: ”Most Points from Bench” is available as a tiebreaker option exclusively for grandfathered Custom Leagues that used this rule in prior seasons. It is not available for new leagues.

Fantasy Basketball: Trades and Waivers
