Change League Schedule and/or Head-to-Head Matchups (LM Leagues)

Adjust League Schedule (Web Only):

Only the League Manager (LM) can adjust your league’s schedule. There are two options available for modifying the league schedule. NOTE: We recommend modifying and finalizing the league’s Schedule Settings and Head-to-Head Schedules before the scheduled draft time. - Edit Schedule Settings - allows the LM to modify the overall league schedule, including regular-season matchups, tiebreakers, and home-field advantages. The “Reset Schedule” option should only be used at the LM’s risk and cannot be reverted in any way. - Edit Head-to-Head Schedule - allows the LM to modify individual Head-to-Head matchups. League Managers can modify Head-to-Head matchups at any time. Teams can also be assigned Bye Weeks to meet the needs and desired schedules of every league.

Edit Schedule Settings (Web Only)

  1. Click on** LM Tools.**
  2. Click** Edit Schedule Settings** under League and Scoring Settings Tools.
  3. Options available for modification include:  Change the length of the Regular Season
  4. Modify Tie-Breakers
  5. Assign points for Home Field Advantage
  6. Modify Playoff brackets, Matchup duration, Seeding Tiebreaker, Playoff Home Field Advantage
  7. Reset Schedule
  8. Scroll down and click Save Changes.

Edit Head-to-Head Schedule

  1. Click on LM Tools.
  2. Click on Edit Head-to-Head Schedule under Schedule and Standings Tools.
  3. ​Choose Team Schedule for a quick view of the entire season schedule.
  4. Click Edit next to a Matchup to edit the individual scoring period.
  5. Select the checkbox appearing next to the team that you wish to move.
  6. Click Switch Teams to change the matchup.
  7. Select Save Changes.

Changing Your League’s Divisions (Web Only)

Once your league has been created, the League Manager can edit the number of divisions on the “Teams and Divisions” page. The default is two divisions; however, the LM can change this number. #### IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS - Divisions must have at least two teams and must be balanced in size. - You must remove all teams from a division before deleting it. - Divisions can be updated until your league has drafted. You cannot edit the number of divisions after the draft. - Multiple Divisions will affect your playoff schedule. We encourage you to check your Playoff settings after adding/removing divisions to avoid future issues.

Manage League Divisions

  • Click on** LM Tools**.
  • Click on** Edit Teams and Divisions** under League and Scoring Settings Tools.
  • Options available include adding and removing divisions:

Add a Division Click Add a Division (NOTE: Must be even; only 2, 4, 6, 8, etc.). - Name your Division. - To fill the division, use the Dropdown menu next to each Team and select which Division you want them in. - Click on Save Changes. - Remove a Division Move all Teams to a Division you intend to retain. - Once emptied, click on the Delete Division button. - Click on Save Changes.

Create a League

On the ESPN Fantasy App:

  2. Enter your desired league name, the number of teams, scoring preference, draft preference, and draft time and date.

On ESPN.com:

  2. Select Create a New League 
  3. Enter your desired league name, the number of teams, scoring preference, draft preference, and draft time and date.

League and Draft Information:

  • League Manager (LM) leagues: League Managers have access to League Manager Tools throughout the season to control aspects of their league, such as draft settings, the number of teams in the league, regular season and playoff schedules, and scoring adjustments. League Manager leagues are private/invite-only.
  • Standard Leagues: Standard ESPN rules.
  • Draft Type: Salary Cap, Live Online “Snake” Draft, or Autopick Draft.
  • Draft Date: Select from the available dates in the pull-down menu or via the calendar.
  • Draft Time: Select from the available time slots (hour/minute). If a particular time slot is unavailable, all slots at that time are taken. However, if a league changes its time or is deleted, time slots may open up.

*****Make sure all your settings are entered correctly because after they are submitted, they can only be changed with a league vote (via the League Referenda).

Delete Your League (LM Only)

Only the League Manager who created the league (the League Creator) can delete it. While the League Creator can assign LM powers to other Team Managers, their powers are limited. Deleting a league that has conducted a draft is a serious decision, as league deletion is final and can NOT be reversed by anyone, including ESPN! #### To Delete Your League (Web Only) 1. Click on LM Tools 2. Click on Delete League under League and Scoring Settings ToolsYou will be presented with a** confirmation pop-up. This pop-up warns that deleting a league is final and cannot be reversed. 3. Click on the red Delete League** button to continue the deletion process.Another pop-up will confirm your decision to delete your league.  This is the last chance to change your mind. 4. Click on** Confirm** to delete your league. All league information will be deleted and can not be recovered or restored by anyone, including ESPN. 5. Your league will disappear in a few minutes.

Fair Play/Conduct (Collusive Transaction)

Collusive Transactions: When one team makes moves to benefit another team without trying to improve its own position. - An example of collusive transactions is one-sided trades or dropping a player so another team can pick up that player - Teams found in violation of this policy will be canceled, and their team managers will be prohibited from participating in future ESPN Fantasy Games - Standard League members are expected to veto/protest all unfair/collusive trades. Four votes are required in a Standard League for a trade to be denied - ​In League Manager Leagues, a different veto system may be in place that allows vetoing all trades. For more information on vetoing trades, click here.

Fair Play/Conduct (Multiple Teams)

Fair Play and Conduct - One person cannot manage more than one team in the same league. - If two or more teams in the same league are under the same account, the teams must be controlled by different people sharing an account. - Violations of this will lead to disqualifications of teams from the league and cancellations of the team.

How to activate Auto Control (AI) Team Management (LM Leagues only)

The Auto Control feature enables the League Manager (LM) to toggle any team to be managed by Artificial Intelligence (AI) i.e. “by the computer.” When active, the AI will make roster moves, free agent pickups, and waiver claims. Trades will not be processed by the active AI. To enable AI management, the LM will need to go into the Send Invites section of LM Tools. There they will be able to toggle  “Auto Control” On/Off for the desired team(s) using the checkboxes. NOTE: In order for this option to appear, the league must first be filled and completed its draft. NOTE: If the Team Manager of a team that is under Auto Control makes any changes (roster, name, etc) Auto Control will immediately be toggled Off. (image: mceclip0.png)

How To Set Up Your League: Injured Reserve (IR) Settings

NOTE: As of October 7, 2020, League Managers are able to add IR slots to their league’s Roster setting. ** **

Impeding Other Team Managers

  • Losing games for the sole purpose of denying another team manager the chance of making the playoffs is not allowed
  • Cycling through players in free agency to make them unavailable to other teams in your league is prohibited and is grounds for expulsion from the league

Step-by-Step Directions

Sending Invites for League Manager Leagues - ESPN Fantasy App - ESPN.com Website - Other methods available

Invite team managers to a League Manager League via the ESPN Fantasy App
  1. The League Manager can click on the “League Manager Tools” link from the menu
  2. Click on “Edit team managers”

  4. Select the method of invitation.

  1. League Managers click on the “LM Tools” link

  3. Enter the new team manager’s email, then click Submit team manager Changes and/or Send Invites
Other Methods of Inviting Team Managers
  1. League Invite Link: League Managers can copy/paste the invite link to the league located on the Members page and post it on a message board, blog, chat, or personal email. Anyone who uses the link can join the league on a first-come, first-served basis until the league is full.
  2. Email Invite: Email invites provide each recipient with a unique link through which they can join your league. Only your League Manager can designate who is invited. Invites can be sent out by entering each email address into the “New Invitations” textbox.

Inviting Team Manager(s) Issues - LM Leagues

There are three common scenarios related to Team Manager issues:

No Invitation Received

If your League Manager claims to have sent you an invitation to the league, but you never received one in your inbox, there are a couple of potential reasons why: - Your League Manager could have entered your email address incorrectly. Double-check that they used your correct email address. - Your corporate or ISP’s firewall might potentially block emails from ESPN servers. We recommend that your League Manager use the “Send Me a Copy of Each Invite” option.

Once your League Manager receives the “cc’ed” email containing your team’s unique join URL, they can forward it to you from their personal email. #### Invitation Received but Unable to Join If you received the invitation from your League Manager, but the unique URL page says you can’t join the league, there is a potential reason why: - Your League Manager changed your email address after sending you the unique URL invitation, thereby nullifying and voiding the original invitation. Contact your League Manager to determine if this was the case.

Other Options Available

  • Speak to your League Manager about another email invitation; you can do this by removing and re-adding your email to the league.
  • Use an alternate email address, preferably one that is not work-related, such as Hotmail, Outlook, or Gmail.
  • Be sure to check your spam and junk folders, as it may have bounced in there by mistake. If that’s the case, add espnfantasy@fantasygames.com to your contact list.

Issues Joining a League

If you’re having issues joining your league, try the following steps: - Try telling your League Manager to resend the invitation to your email address. If you still don’t receive an email in your inbox, try an alternate email address - Be sure to check your spam and junk folders, as it may have been bounced in there by mistake. If so, add espnfantasy@fantasygames.go.com to your contact list - Your corporate or ISP’s firewall might potentially block emails from ESPN servers. We recommend your League Manager uses the “Send Me a Copy of Each Invite” option. Once your League Manager receives the “cc’ed” email containing your team’s unique join URL, they can forward it to you off their personal email.

If you received an invite, but can’t join, try the following steps: Note: If you are getting an error or it says your league is full (even though it isn’t showing as full), your League Manager likely invited you via the web (desktop, laptop, etc.), which reserves your place in the league. If you are in the app and trying to accept the invite, your League Manager likely invited you via the web AND the app. The web overrides the app invite, so you will be sent the error message. Simply have your League Manager delete the web invite and only send it to you through the app. Or you can always just accept the invite through the web (desktop, laptop, etc.) - Your League Manager changed your email address after inviting you, thereby voiding the invitation - Talk with your League Manager and make sure you have the right email address in place - If problems persist, you may be having account issues. Click here for additional information on how to fix any account issues.

​Note: If you are instead experiencing issues trying to invite team managers to join your league, click here for additional troubleshooting.

Join a Private League

Private leagues are an option available only in League Manager leagues. To join one, you must be invited by the League Manager (LM).

  1. All invitations to join Private Leagues are sent in the form of an email containing a unique URL. This unique URL is the ticket to play in the league.
  2. Click on the URL or copy and paste it into your browser’s ‘Address’ field to accept the invitation.
  3. Upon joining, your ESPN.com Member ID will be associated with a Team ID and you will become a team manager.
  4. Only league creators can invite people to play in their private league.

Keeper Leagues

Keeper leagues (also known as Dynasty leagues) allow Team Managers to keep players on their roster over multiple seasons without having to redraft them.  Keepers are only available in League Manager leagues.  Team Managers may select as few players or as many players as the league creator selected during league creation. For example, if your league allows 3 Keepers per team, a Team Manager may elect to designate between 0-3 players to stay on their roster for the next season. League Manager can enable or disable Keeper settings via LM Tools. #### A few important facts about Keepers on ESPN Fantasy:  - The default draft method in Keeper leagues is to draft/assign selected Keepers in the first rounds.  Keeper rounds are Non-Snake. (For Snake Drafts) This means that if the league allows 2 keepers in the upcoming draft, the first 2 rounds would be non-snake. 1-10, 1-10, then from the 3rd round, 1-10, 10-1, 1-10, etc.

  • Example: Last season, a Team Manager drafted a player in the 5th round.  The Team Manager decides to mark that player as one of their team’s Keepers for the next season.  When the next season’s draft occurs, that Keeper will be drafted automatically in the 5th round.

To enable Keepers in an LM league:

  1. Open** LM Tools**
  2. Go to League and Scoring Settings Tools
  3. Select League Settings
  4. Select** Transactions and Keepers**
  5. Scroll down to Keepers Rules and click on Edit
  6. Click on Yes for Use Keepers for (next) Season.
  7. You can now select how many players can be designated as a Keeper (Minimum 1, maximum full roster size)
  8. You can set the date when Keepers Lock. The default is one hour before your next season Draft Date/Time.
  9. Click Save Changes

Keeper Salaries

Keeper salaries are how much a manager will “pay for” out of their salary cap prior to the draft in order to keep that player. Kind of how draft right works.  Most leagues use the player salaries from the prior season(s), but LM’s can change that. ##### To Edit Keeper Salaries 1. Open** LM Tools 2. Go to League and Scoring Settings Tools 3. Select League Settings 4. Select Transactions and Keepers 5. Scroll down to Keepers Rules and click on Edit 6. Click on Edit Keeper Salaries. 7. You can now select the salary. 8. Click Save Changes**

Change Keeper Lock Date

NOTE: Once the keeper lock date passes, only the league manager will be able to modify a team’s keeper selection.  Alternatively, choose “Lock One Hour before Draft” to allow league members to edit their keepers in the last minute. 1. Open** LM Tools 2. Go to League and Scoring Settings Tools 3. Select League Settings 4. Select Transactions and Keepers 5. Scroll down to Keepers Rules and click on Edit 6. You can set the date when Keepers Lock. The default is one hour before your next season Draft Date/Time. 7. Click Save Changes**

League Manager Powers

The League Manager (LM) is the title of the creator of a League Manager league. As the league creator, the LM has the power to customize the league rules to create the fantasy league of their dreams. The default ruleset is identical to the standard ESPN Fantasy leagues available to the public (referred to as Public Leagues). The LM then gets to decide what options to add/remove, adjust points, add/remove roster slots, set the schedule, draft date/time/type, and more. Because these leagues are highly customized, they are private. This means that the only way to join one is to be invited by the LM via email. Additionally, the LM is the ultimate authority for all aspects of their league, including but not limited to league business, player trades, infractions of these rules, and disputes among franchise team managers. The LM will investigate all overall winners for collusion before awarding overall prizes and it has the right to disqualify team managers or remove them from the leaderboard if deemed necessary. The decisions of the LM shall be final and irreversible. The League Manager has the right to make any necessary changes to the game and rules as the season progresses. Any changes will be properly noted on the league’s homepage. If a League Manager ever wants to relinquish his/her role within a League Manager League, all they have to do is navigate to the “LM Tools” tab and click on “Assign League Manager Powers” and select another team manager for that role.

(NOTE: League CREATOR cannot be removed from the league and will always have a spot in the league as long as the league is active) The use of ESPN.com and participation in ESPN Fantasy games are subject to ESPN’s Terms of Use Agreement.

League Scoring Types: Standard and Non-PPR

League Scoring Types

Non-PPR or No-Points-Per-Reception

League Types

PUBLIC (STANDARD) Public (Standard) 10-team standard scoring leagues that use fixed rule settings and are managed by ESPN. Standard Leagues draft players from the whole NFL Universe. That means you will be able to draft both NFC (National Football Conference) and AFC (American Football Conference) players for your team. Free Standard League rosters have slots for a total of 16 players per team. There are 9 starting slots and 7 bench slots. You may also select which level of competition you prefer. - PRO - for fantasy veterans seeking competition - BEGINNER - for people who are new to fantasy football.

LEAGUE MANAGER League Manager (LM) leagues use customized rule settings and are managed by one of the players in the league, known as the League Manager (LM). The LM is able to choose from a variety of scoring formats and rule options to create a unique fantasy game suited to specific settings. The League Manager version provides a wide variety of additional scoring and rules options such as Keepers and Offline Draft.

League Types in ESPN Fantasy

ESPN Fantasy offers two primary league types: Standard Leagues and League Manager (LM) Leagues. The main difference between these league types is who controls the league settings and rules. #### Quick Comparison - Feature: Standard League: League Manager League - League control: ESPN: League Manager - Rule customization: Not available: Fully customizable - Draft setup: Automatic: Controlled by LM - Ideal for: Quick public leagues: Private or custom leagues

Standard Leagues

Standard Leagues are public leagues with preset rules managed by ESPN. These leagues are designed for players who want a quick and simple way to start playing without customizing league settings. ##### Key Characteristics - League rules and scoring are set by ESPN - League operations are automatically managed - Drafts are scheduled automatically - Roster sizes and scoring formats follow standard settings for that sport

Standard leagues are ideal for players who want a ready-to-play fantasy experience. #### League Manager (LM) Leagues League Manager leagues are custom leagues created and controlled by a player, known as the League Manager (LM). The League Manager controls most league settings and can customize the league to suit a specific group or style of play. LM leagues are commonly used by friends, families, coworkers, or established fantasy groups. ##### Customization Options League Managers can adjust settings such as: - Scoring format - Roster size and lineup settings - Draft type and draft schedule - Waiver rules and free agency settings - Trade rules and review process - Playoff format

Some leagues may also use advanced features, including: - Keeper leagues (players can be retained for future seasons) - Offline drafts - Other custom rule configurations

Overall League Participation Limits

Each ESPN Fantasy account can join up to 25 leagues per sport, including both Standard and League Manager leagues. #### Quick Tip If you’re unsure which league type you’re in, check the League Settings page. If the league has a League Manager listed, it is a League Manager League.

Leave a League or Remove a Team Manager

Sometimes you may need to relinquish management of a team. You can always leave your team BEFORE the league draft.  Things get trickier after the draft has occurred. In Public Leagues, you may not leave once the draft has completed.  In League Manager leagues, you can leave your team, but you will need to ask your LM to remove you as a Team Manager. - Click the** Leave League** link on your team page** *****before the league’s draft.***Team managers can’t leave a league after the draft occurs.

How to Remove a Team Manager (LM only / Web Only) - Open** LM Tools. - Click on League Membership Tools. - Click on Edit Managers and Send Invitations. - Click on the red Remove Manager** button to the right of the Team Manager to be removed. - You will be prompted to** sign in** again for confirmation. - You will then need to confirm the removal by clicking on Remove Manager from the pop-up.

Length of Fantasy Football Season

Standard League Settings - ESPN has set fourteen (14) weeks in the regular season as the fixed setting for all Public (standard) leagues and it thus cannot be altered. - Playoffs will begin in Week 15 and finish in Week 18. - If you wish to play in a league which offers a flexible regular season that lasts any amount of time other than 14 weeks you can create or join a League Manager League.

Change the Length of Your Custom League Regular Season on Web Only - The League Manager can change this setting by clicking on the “LM Tools” tab - Click on “Edit League Settings”

Lineup Lock Times

The Lineup Lock Time is when team lineups lock each week. This applies to moving players between active slots, or between active slots and bench slots. NOTE: In League Manager leagues, the League Manager (LM) may change the Lineup Lock Time settings up until one hour prior to the draft. Below are the two options available in League Manager Leagues: Lock Individually at Scheduled Gametime: This is the default setting and is used by the majority of leagues. If selected, team managers can make moves to their weekly rosters until the scheduled kickoff time of each player’s game. Lock at First Game of the Week: All roster moves will lock at the first game of the week, even if the first game falls on a Thursday.

Click on LM Tools 2. Click on Roster Moves 3. Click on Drop Player under the Action dropdown 4. Click on the Team you will be modifying 5. Click Continue 6. Click** Drop** next to the player you wish to drop 7. Click** Continue 8. You will need to confirm** the transaction 9. Now go back to LM Tools -> Roster Moves 10. Click on Add Player under the Action dropdown 11. Click on the Team you will be modifying 12. Click Continue 13. Click on the “+” button next to the dropped player to add them back to the team

Offensive Content and Team Managers

ESPN Fantasy Sports are available to everyone with the understanding that we are here for fun. However, a distinction must be made between playful banter between competitors and abuse/hostility.  ALL leagues, ESPN Standard and League Manager, both Public and Private, are subject to the ESPN Terms of Use** and Fair Play and Conduct when playing Fantasy games on ESPN. #### Team managers are expected to communicate in a respectful and gracious manner** - Threats and obscenities are against the rules and are illegal in many jurisdictions. - Team managers who send threatening emails to another team manager will be warned and/or kicked out of the game and can be banned from ESPN.com altogether. - Threats and obscenities are not allowed at any time.

Offensive language, league, or team names are prohibited

  • Any posts, including league and team names, that are derogatory in nature are strictly prohibited. This restriction includes chat rooms, message boards, and the league’s bulletin board.
  • There is a zero-tolerance level concerning offensive posts, including personal attacks, sexist remarks, and/or racist remarks.

Violators of the above rules are subject to being banned from ESPN.com and/or Disney sites. Furthermore, violations containing threats may be referred to the appropriate authorities.

Changing the Player Universe would reset any previously set draft lists - To edit this setting, your League Manager must click on “settings” under the “League” tab

(image: mceclip0.png) - Click on Transactions and Keepers - Click on the Edit button for Player Rules - Make your changes then click the Save button.

Regular Season and Playoffs Schedule in Public Leagues

REGULAR SEASON SCHEDULE

ESPN has set fourteen(14) weeks in the regular season for Public Leagues. This is a fixed setting and thus can not be altered. If you wish to play in a league that offers flexible regular season and playoff schedules, you must create or join a League Manager league. #### REACHING THE PLAYOFFS The top four teams in a league make the playoffs. These four comprise the two division champions and two wild-card teams. Division champions are the teams that win the league divisions. The next two teams, according to the tiebreaker below, are the wild card teams. #### PLAYOFF BRACKET SETUP All teams continue to compete throughout the playoffs. The two Divisional Champions and two wild-card teams (teams with the next best overall records) compete for the League Championship. The wild card teams may come from either division and are selected by their records, with ties resolved according to the tiebreaker categories below. The top-ranked division champion plays the lowest-ranked wild card team, i.e., the first-place team faces the fourth-place team, while the second-place team faces the third-place team. The remaining teams compete in the consolation bracket. Throughout the championship run, this consolation bracket remains competitive since no one wants to finish last! #### PLAYOFF SEEDING AND TIEBREAKERS (Public/Standard Leagues) Public League Playoffs: Playoff Seeding and Tiebreakers If two or more teams have identical won-loss records at the conclusion of the Fantasy Football regular season, the following tiebreaking system is used. 1. Overall Points-For 2. Head-to-Head Record 3. Division Record 4. Overall Points-Against 5. Coin Flip

NOTE: The Overall record is based on winning percentage. Therefore, a team that is 9-5-0 and a team that is 8-4-2 have the same winning percentage, and thus would be considered tied for overall record. #### PUBLIC LEAGUE PLAYOFFS: TIEBREAKER FOR PLAYOFF GAMES If two teams have the same number of points at the conclusion of their two-week playoff, the tiebreaker is each team’s original playoff seeding. In short, the team with the higher seed wins. #### PLAYOFF SCHEDULE Winner’s Bracket: In the first round of the playoffs, the division winner with the best win-loss record plays the wild-card team with the worst win-loss record; the other division winner plays the wild-card team with the better win-loss record. In the second round, the winners of the first-round games compete for the league championship. Each round of the playoffs spans a two-week period. The 5th through 10th-seeded teams in each league compete in the Consolation bracket. ##### The Winner’s Bracket: - 1st place - Winner of game 1, round 2 - 2nd place - Loser of game 1, round 2 - 3rd place - Winner of game 2, round 2 - 4th place - Loser of game 2, round 2

The Consolation Bracket:
  • 5th place - Winner of game 1, round 2
  • 6th place - Loser of game 1, round 2
  • 7th place - Winner of game 2, round 2
  • 8th place - Loser of game 2, round 2
  • 9th place - Winner of game 3, round 2
  • 10th place - Loser of game 3, round 2

Roster Dumping

Roster Dumping: dumping your players to the player pool in an attempt to undermine the league. - Team managers that have “roster dumped” may be subject to expulsion from the game. - If a manager no longer wants to compete in the league, it is recommended that the player giving up still provides a full lineup each week to keep the integrity of the league’s competition intact.

Roster Settings

The “Rosters” page in “League Setup” allows the league creator to customize: 1. The roster positions (slots) used in the league 2. How many players start at each position 3. The maximum number of players allowed from each slot 4. When setting the number of starters and max on roster for each slot, it is important to carefully consider the number of teams in the league versus the number of available players in the game. For example, if you’re in an 18 team league and select two starting positions at the quarterback slot, there will not be enough actual starting NFL quarterbacks for each team in your league (18 x 2 = 36, and there’s only 32 teams in the NFL). 5. If the league has a high number of teams and the league rules set the slot maximum to a large number, some teams in the league could hoard all the players in that position, leaving no players available in free agency. Select your roster settings wisely! Roster settings are controlled via the pull down menus in the starters and max on roster columns.

NOTE: As of October 7, 2020, League Managers are able to add IR slots to their league’s Roster setting.

Roster Slots (Defense)

Defensive Roster Slots - Defensive Tackle (DT): The league will draft individual NFL defensive tackles. The maximum number of starters at the DT slot is five (5). - Defensive End (DE): The league will draft individual NFL defensive ends. The maximum number of starters at the DE slot is five (5). - Linebacker (LB): The league will draft individual NFL linebackers. The maximum number of starters at the LB slot is five (5). - Cornerback (CB): The league will draft individual NFL cornerbacks. The maximum number of starters at the CB slot is five (5). - Safety (S): The league will draft individual NFL safeties. The maximum number of starters at the S slot is five (5). - Defensive Back (DB): Team managers have the option to start either a CB or S each week during the season. The maximum number of starters at the DB slot is six (6). - Defensive Player Utility (DP): Team managers have the option to start any defensive roster slot. The maximum number of starters at the DP slot is fifteen (15).

Team Roster Slots - Team Defense/Special Team (D/ST): This roster slot combines both the Team Defense and Special Teams. The maximum number of starters at the D/ST slot is four (4).

Roster Slots (Offense)

  • Quarterback (QB): If this option is selected, the league will draft individual NFL quarterbacks. If the QB slot is selected, the league cannot use the TQB option. The maximum number of starters at the QB slot is six.
  • Team Quarterback (TQB): All quarterbacks from a specified NFL team are included in this unique scoring option. If selected, the league will draft a team and will receive stats for all QBs who play for the NFL team. So if you have the Patriots QBs and their starter gets hurt in the first quarter, you’ll get all the points put up by his replacement(s) for the remainder of the game. The max number of starters at the TQB slot is four.NOTE: If your league is set for each team to have a Team QB, you will be able to place the Team QB only in the Team QB position. If your league offers an Offensive Player Utility slot, you cannot place a Team QB in the Offensive Player Utility roster spot. However, if your league is set for individual QB players, you can place your starting QB in the QB roster slot AND your backup QB in the Offensive Player Utility slot.

Scheduling Your Draft

Step-by-Step Directions

  1. Click “schedule your draft” on the league home page
  2. Select your draft typeSnake is the most common draft type. Snake means that the order goes 1-10 and then 10-1
  3. Pick the date and time of your draft, followed by how many seconds each team manager will get per pick
  4. Drafts can also be scheduled by going to the League Settings page and clicking on Draft Settings

NOTE:  League Manager Leagues must be filled at least sixty-one (61) minutes before the scheduled Draft.  Leagues that do not have all slots filled sixty (60) minutes before the scheduled draft time will be reset, and the LM will need to reschedule their draft.

Scoring & Stat Corrections

Sometimes during the fantasy season, you may find that one of your players has had their points changed. A player’s score/stats will be impacted when the official NFL statistics used to calculate them are adjusted, updated, or corrected. ESPN always works to ensure that matchup scores accurately reflect the real, official NFL statistics and if you notice changes, it is to correct previously incorrect data or react to a stat correction from the league. There are several scenarios when you might see these changes: 1. Live Scoring – During the game, scores/stats are updated as they are received. This information may change as more accurate data from the league is reported. Each player’s individual points and stats will be accurately reflected once the game is final. 2. Post-game adjustments – There are times when the NFL decides to adjust stats after a game has been concluded. For example, during the game the NFL credits one player with a full sack, then after the post-game review decides instead to award two players half a sack each. This type of stat correction can appear up to seven (7) days after the game was played. 3. Post-game corrections – Sometimes ESPN receives incorrect data in the stats feeds. Most of the time when inaccurate data is detected, the incorrect score/stat is corrected within minutes. Rarely, incorrect scores/stats may not be corrected until the next day. This type of stat correction can appear up to seven (7) days after the game was played. 4. League Manager changes: In League Manager leagues, the LM has the power to adjust scores manually. The reasons for changing a player’s score are completely up to the League Manager.  CAUTION: If the LM notices the incorrect scoring before ESPN has updated the stats and uses the Adjust Scoring League Manager tool to manually change the score then afterward when the system updates automatically to reflect the same correction, the impacted team will be awarded double credit for the correction. If this occurs, you should contact your LM and ask them to re-adjust the scoring by reversing their manual adjustment.

ADDITIONAL NOTES: - The deadline for all weekly scoring or stat corrections made by the system during the season is the Saturday following the week of the game in question. - Only official stat corrections made by the NFL after a game’s conclusion will appear on the stat correction page. https://fantasy.espn.com/football/statcorrections  Corrections to incorrect data received by ESPN will not appear on that page - Any changes entered in the system will automatically reflect in both your Box Score and your Standings pages.

Scoring Formats

STANDARD SCORING FORMATS (Public Leagues) 

ESPN Fantasy Football offers two types of public leagues to join:  Points-Per-Reception (PPR)  scoring leagues and Standard (non-PPR) Scoring leagues. The difference between a Points-Per-Reception (PPR) league and a Standard Scoring (Non-PPR) league in ESPN Fantasy Football lies in how they reward receptions made by offensive players, especially wide receivers, tight ends, and pass-catching running backs. In a PPR league, players who catch a reception will earn a point. Standard (non-PPR) leagues do not award a point for a successful catch. From a strategic perspective, Standard (non-PPR) leagues favor big plays and touchdowns over consistent volume, while Points-Per-Reception (PPR) leagues favor consistent volume, such as players who catch many short passes. WRs with high target percentages and pass-catching RBs are valuable in PPR leagues because of their additional opportunities to score points.  Standard (Non-PPR) League: - No points awarded for a reception. - Points come from: Yardage (e.g., 1 point per 10 rushing or receiving yards) - Touchdowns (typically 6 points) - Other stats like field goals, extra points, or turnovers

Points-Per-Reception (PPR) League: - Adds 1 point for every catch a player makes - Points come from: Successful receptions - Yardage (e.g., 1 point per 10 rushing or receiving yards) - Touchdowns (6 points) - Other stats like field goals, extra points, or turnovers

Example: Your running back has this stat line: - 50 rushing yards - 6 catches for 30 receiving yards - One touchdown

Standard Scoring (non-PPR): 14 Points Total - Rushing Yards – 5 Points - Receiving Yards – 3 Points - Touchdown – 6 Points

Points-Per-Reception (PPR): 20 Points Total - Rushing Yards – 5 Points - Receiving Yards – 3 Points - Receptions - 6 Points - Touchdown – 6 Points

LEAGUE MANAGER SCORING FORMATS (LM Leagues) 

LM leagues are nonstandard scoring leagues with a variable number of teams (4-20) and customized rule settings. All customizable leagues use the head-to-head scoring system. In this system, each team in your league faces off against one other team every week of the season. However, your league might contain bye weeks. The winner of each matchup is the team that accumulates the most fantasy points, determined by the weekly statistics of the players in each team’s lineup and the scoring settings of your league. Weekly results are compiled into an overall record and displayed on the league’s standings page. Below is a comprehensive list of scoring categories available in ESPN Fantasy Football. Each category lists the standard game settings and all options available in the custom game. In the custom game, the specific categories and their corresponding point values can be edited by the League Manager (LM) to align with your league’s scoring system. The numbers in brackets (e.g., 1, 5, 10) indicate the available buckets to select. Decimal values are allowed for each category (tenths and hundredths of a point). If your league is already set up, view your League Settings page to see how your league scores each category. On this page, all of the available stat categories and their corresponding point values can be edited to create your league’s unique scoring system. Team Manager Inactivity (LM Leagues)

The League Manager may contact the team managers of teams that remain inactive for extended periods. - The League Manager will send notifications to the email on record for the inactive team manager. - If the account still remains inactive after the email was sent by the League Manager, the League Manager reserves the right to reassign team managership of the inactive team.

Team Manager Invitation Issues (LM Leagues)

There are three common scenarios related to Team Manager issues:

No Invitation Received

If your League Manager claims to have sent you an invitation to the league, but you never received one in your inbox, there are a couple of potential reasons why: - Your League Manager could have entered your email address incorrectly. Double-check that they used your correct email address. - Your corporate or ISP’s firewall might potentially block emails from ESPN servers. We recommend that your League Manager use the “Send Me a Copy of Each Invite” option.

Once your League Manager receives the “cc’ed” email containing your team’s unique join URL, they can forward it to you from their personal email. #### Invitation Received but Unable to Join If you received the invitation from your League Manager, but the unique URL page says you can’t join the league, there is a potential reason why: - Your League Manager changed your email address after sending you the unique URL invitation, thereby nullifying and voiding the original invitation. Contact your League Manager to determine if this was the case.

Other Options Available

  • Speak to your League Manager about another email invitation; you can do this by removing and re-adding your email to the league.
  • Use an alternate email address, preferably one that is not work-related, such as Hotmail, Outlook, or Gmail.
  • Be sure to check your spam and junk folders, as it may have bounced in there by mistake. If that’s the case, add espnfantasy@fantasygames.com to your contact list.

Updated Standings

Updated Standings - Your league standing, playoff seeding, waiver order and everything else league-related is updated every night, normally by 3 am EST the following morning - ESPN Fantasy Football FantasyCast will display your point scoring stats in real-time as the games unfold

What happens if a professional game is suspended then resumed at a later date?

If the suspended game is resumed within seven (7) days of being suspended, all stats from the suspended game will count for the scoring period when the game began. If the suspended game is resumed after eight (8) or more days have passed, the stats from the resumed portion of the game will not count towards your fantasy output or totals. This is consistent with how other Stat Corrections are handled. EXAMPLE A game on Monday is suspended then resumed on Friday. The points/stats for both parts of the game will appear in the results for Monday. NOTE: This is the case even if the resumption of the suspended game occurs within the next matchup period. Additionally, your team will accrue points/stats generated in the resumed game based on the players who were in your original lineup on Monday (not those in your lineup on Friday). Please note that stats from the resumed portion of the game may not show up immediately on the site or the app. The points/stats will appear overnight the day the game concludes.

What is a Knockout League?

Knockout leagues (AKA Elimination Leagues) are a variation of Fantasy Football with a brutal twist – instead of competing head-to-head, managers compete as a group using total points to determine the winners. Each week, the manager whose team scored the lowest Total Points is cut from the league, and their players are released to the waiver wire! Every week thereafter, another manager is cut until, in the end, you have two powerhouse teams left to vie for the championship. We did say it was brutal! Click here to learn more!

Defense and Special Team (D/ST) SCORING: The Difference between Fumble Recovered and Fumble Lost.

The NFL has different stats for a Fumble Lost and a Fumble Recovered. ESPN Fantasy Football relies on the Fumble Recovered stat. Therefore, in ESPN FFL, Defensive/Special Teams (D/ST) are awarded points they recover a fumble and not when a fumble is lost by the opposing Offense. EXAMPLE On Sunday, October 20, 2019 during the Oakland Raiders versus Green Bay Packers game, Derek Carr lost control of the football when diving toward the end zone. The ball went out of bounds through the end zone resulting in a touchback. - Since the fumbled ball was not recovered by a Packers player, the Green Bay D/ST was not awarded points for Fumble Recovered. - Had the fumbled ball been recovered in bounds by a Packers player, the Green Bay D/ST would have been awarded points for a Fumble Recovered.

Defense and Special Teams (D/ST) Scoring

There are a few nuances to keep in mind when evaluating how the Defense and Special Teams units are awarded points for defensive scoring in fantasy. #### Interceptions Returned for TDs (Picks 6’s) are NOT Counted Against D/ST ESPN has changed the way interceptions returned for touchdowns (Pick 6s) affect your D/ST score. Beginning with the 2019 season, offensive points gained from Pick 6s or fumble recoveries for TDs will NOT affect your D/ST score. However, Special Team’s points still count against your D/ST score (i.e., a punt return for a TD against your D/ST). #### Why Do D/STs Show Points At The Start of the Game? - Your D/ST begins each game with 10 points (in standard scoring). At the time, they’ve given up 0 points. (worth 5 points), and they’ve allowed 0 offensive yards to their opponent (worth 5 points). - Your D/ST gains points by registering sacks, turnovers, and scoring points. - Your D/ST score will drop if they give up yards to the opponent’s offense in any way.

Point After Touchdown D/ST Scoring

  • D/ST earns a Safety during a PAT to receive 1 point.
  • D/ST returns the ball to their own end zone during a PAT to receive 2 points.

These scoring changes apply to all ESPN Fantasy Football League types, including Defense/Special Teams (D/ST) and IDP scoring models. #### “Stuff” on ESPN Fantasy As of November 12th, 2021, the definition of “Stuff” on ESPN Fantasy is as follows: - A “stuff” can only be recorded on a rush for no gain or negative yards. (behind or on the line of scrimmage). - “Tackles for loss” and “stuffs” are not the same thing. - A “tackle for loss” could be credited on a rushing play or on a passing play.

Fair Play / Conduct: Impeding Other Team Managers

ESPN Fantasy Sports is a place for sports fans to have fun competing with each other while enjoying the sports we love. ESPN is committed to providing a fair and respectful experience for everyone. The following behaviors are examples of unacceptable behaviors. Please note this is NOT a comprehensive list. - Losing games solely to deny another team’s manager the chance to make the playoffs - Cycling through players in free agency to make them unavailable to other teams in your league - Collusive trading where one team obtains top-ranked players for bottom-ranked players in order to stack one team at the expense of another

Fantasy Football Acronyms

Below is a list of all the acronyms you may see while playing ESPN Fantasy Football: Player Status - IR = Injured Reserve - O = Out - Q = Questionable - D = Doubtful - SSPD = Suspended

Player Positions - QB = Quarterback - RB = Running Back - WR = Wide Receiver - TE = Tight End - FLEX = Running Backs, Wide Receivers, and Tight Ends can be used in this position - D/ST = Defense and Special Teams - K = Kicker

Season and Week Columns - PRK = Position Rank - PTS = Total Season Points - AVG = Average Points Per Game - LAST = Last Game Points - PROJ = ESPN Projected Points for that Week - OPRK = Opponent Rank - %ST = Percent Started - %ROST = Percent Rostered - +/- = Change in Percent Rostered

How does the Injured Reserve / Injury List impact Waivers?

The system automatically places the IR (Injured Reserve) or IL (Injury List) tag on a player once ESPN receives the league’s status report. Only players with the IR (Injured Reserve) or IL (Injury List) tag are eligible; the day limit does not matter. At its most basic and simple level, when you place an eligible player into the IR/IL slot, you gain an open roster slot. As long as the IR/IL player is eligible for the IR/IL slot, basic waiver offers and free agent pickups will remain unchanged. Where it can get tricky is when you attempt to pick up a player via waiver claim or free agency, and the player’s status in the IR/IL slot changes. The system will always ensure that you do not exceed the roster size limit for your league. Some scenarios to consider when making a claim while you have a player in an IL slot: - If you have a healthy player in an IR/IL slot, you cannot add any new players to your roster.When you attempt to acquire a free agent with a healthy player in an IR/IL slot, you will receive a message to clear your IR/IL before you can make a claim.

  • You will still need to free up a roster slot before you can move the now healthy player out of the IR/IL slot.

What is a League ID? 

A League ID is the unique numeric identifier for your league among all ESPN Fantasy leagues. While there are millions of individual leagues, this League ID helps locate your exact league for any troubleshooting you may need. It is very important that you note and keep safe any IDs for the leagues you’re part of, whether public or private. #### Why do I need my League ID? A league ID can be used to locate a league among others when the account email has been lost/compromised. This ID can be used by ESPN Fan Support staff to locate leagues and investigate reported issues. Without the League ID, ESPN cannot guarantee we can locate your league among the millions of others in the system. Keep your league ID in a safe location for future reference, if needed. #### Where can I find a League ID? The League ID can be found in multiple spots. #### Traditional Web Browser - ESPN.com (image: league_ID.png) - 1. Email, text, or direct link invites: - Locate the email, click “join this league”.  A new window will appear from fantasy.espn.com - Within the URL bar of the new window will be LeagueID=

  • Within the link, you will be able to find LeagueID=

On the ESPN Fantasy App (iOS or Android)

  • Click “League Info”
  • League ID is available to view.

Similarly, when adding weeks to the regular-season schedule, matchups will be added at the end of the regular season and all teams will be on bye weeks. It is the League Manager’s responsibility to edit such matchups.

Moving Players on and off of the Injured Reserve (IR) and Injury List (IL)

The system will automatically place the IR (injured reserve) or Injury List (IL) tag on a player once ESPN receives the league report. NOTE: Only players with the (IR), (IL), or (O) tag can be placed on the IR (injured reserve)/Injury List (IL) slot. All other players must be moved to the bench if you do NOT want them on the active roster. NOTE: IR/IL is available in all Standard leagues and only in League Managers that use IR/IL slot(s). If you don’t see the link, let your League Manager know they need to add this feature. - League Managers can enable IR/IL slots in a league by going under the LM Tools tab and selecting Edit League Settings.

Managing IR on the ESPN Fantasy App

  1. On your team’s Roster page, click on the** IR or IL button**
  2. ​You will be provided with a short list of players eligible for the IR/IL slot and a list of either open slots or players already in those slots.
  3. Tap To IR/IL to move the player into an open slot
  4. If you have no open slots, you will need to select a player to move from IR/IL by tapping on the Activate button.
  5. You will see a confirmation pop-up as this change is automatically saved.

Managing IR on ESPN.com

  1. Click on the Manage IR/IL link at the top of your team page a
  2. You will be shown a short list of IR/IL eligible players. Click on To IR/IL to place them in an available IR/IL slot. NOTE: If all of your IR/IL slots are occupied, you will need to Activate a player to make the change.

To move a player back from IR to your active roster, follow the same steps: 1. Click on the Manage IR/IL link at the top of your team page a 2. You will be shown a short list of players in your IR/IL. Click on Activate a player to move the player to your active roster.

Naming Your Team

Team Names Overview

Your team name has two parts: a Location (such as a city or region) and a Nickname (such as your team’s actual name). Each part has a maximum of 15 characters. There’s no rule against two teams in the same league sharing a name, so get creative! You can also set a 4-character abbreviation for your team. Pro Tip: Several pages in the app use only abbreviations, so we recommend choosing one that makes sense on its own. Good to know: If you’re joining an existing team, it may already have a name — but you can change it at any time during the season, so don’t worry if you inherit something you’re not crazy about! IMPORTANT NOTE: Offensive team names in ESPN Fantasy leagues are subject to change and may result in further consequences. Please review our Offensive Content and Team Managers policy for more details. #### On the ESPN Fantasy App (Mobile) 1. Tap your team icon from the My Team dropdown to go to your Team Homepage 2. Tap your team icon again to open your Team Info section 3. Tap Edit in the top-right corner 4. Update your Location, Nickname, and/or abbreviation as desired 5. Tap Save when you’re done

On ESPN.com (Desktop)

  1. Click the Team Settings link in your team’s navigation menu, or find it just beneath your team logo
  2. Update your Location, Nickname, and/or abbreviation as desired
  3. Click Save when you’re done

Players on Injured Reserve (IR)

Injury Designations - ESPN Fantasy Football uses the NFL’s official injury/inactive list to update a player’s injury status - If the player in question on your team was recently put on IR, the system will register that change shortly - After the IR tag appears next to that player’s name, you’ll be able to send him to an IR slot on your roster, but only if your league makes use of that clutch feature NOTE: In ESPN Fantasy Football, players with either the Out (O) or Injured/Reserve (IR) status may be placed into the IR slot - NOTE: Suspended players (SSPD) are NOT eligible for IR on FFL.

  • If a player is designated as OUT or IR, they are IR eligible (as is today)
  • If a player in the IR slot has their status updated from OUT or IR to QUESTIONABLE or DOUBTFUL, the user’s roster is NOT invalid. Those players can remain in that IR slot, and the user can make claims/add players, adjust their lineups as they wish.
  • If a player goes from OUT to no longer having an injury designation, the user’s roster becomes INVALID, and they must update it accordingly.

NOTE: As of October 7, 2020, League Managers are able to add IR slots to their league’s Roster setting.

Position Eligibility

  • The NFL sends ESPN an updated list of every player’s position eligibility, including rookies, prior to the start of each season.
  • ESPN reserves the right to designate a different position for a player.
  • Once the season has begun, ESPN cannot change the primary position. However, a player can gain additional eligibility for other positions during the season if circumstances warrant it.
  • League Managers DO NOT have the ability to change a player’s position.
  • It’s important to note that roster minimums and maximums within your league’s settings relate to the primary position only (the first position listed next to a player), not any secondary positions granted

Under certain circumstances, ESPN reserves the right to change a player’s primary position. NOTE: For teams drafting Travis Hunter, this player is both a wide receiver and a cornerback. When drafted, he will always be placed in the primary position slot (WR) unless all WR slots have been filled. For leagues that include Individual Defensive Player (IDP) scoring, in accordance with league settings, Travis Hunter will accrue stats for both offensive and defensive plays, regardless of his position slot (WR, FLEX, OP, CB, DB, or DP). If your league does not have IDP scoring, Travis Hunter would only accrue stats for Offensive Plays, EXCEPT when stats accrued on the Defense or Special Teams fall into the categories for Miscellaneous scoring.

If he is slotted in the WR, Flex, or OP position, stats accrued on defense will be included in the total points, but will not show in the individual scoring breakdown on your fantasy Box Score

For more information about Travis Hunter in Fantasy Football, please visit https://www.espn.com/fantasy/football/story/_/id/45525668/2025-fantasy-football-idp-league-scoring-travis-hunter-eligibility

Scoring - Faked Field Goals

In the event that a faked Field Goal attempt results in a touchdown, the points will be assigned as follows: If the Touchdown was the result of a pass, the passer and the receiver will be awarded the number of points set for regular passing touchdowns. If the touchdown was scored via running, the player carrying the ball into the end zone will be assigned the points for a rushing touchdown. Example: On November 25, 2018, the Pittsburgh Steelers set up a fake field goal attempt. Pittsburgh kicker Chris Boswell completed a pass to Pittsburgh offensive lineman Alejandro Villanueva that resulted in a touchdown. Boswell received points for a passing touchdown while Villaneuva received points for a receiving touchdown. NOTE: D/ST units do not receive points, only the players involved in the play.

Undroppable Players List

The Undroppable Players List is a list of the top Fantasy players who can’t be sent to waivers/free agency. Without this feature, a team manager who is out of contention could drop a star player for their buddy, who is first on the waiver order, to pick up, thereby bolstering their team for the playoffs. Please Note: If a player designated Undroppable becomes injured, this does not mean they will be automatically removed from the ESPN Undroppable List. Players are put on the list before the season begins due to their star potential. ESPN may choose not to remove a player from the list who is still expected to return at some point during the season/playoffs. The Undroppable Player List is used in all Standard Leagues. Select No next to Observe ESPN’s Undroppable Player List 5. Save Changes
