Undroppable Players List

The Undroppable Players List is a list of the top Fantasy players who can’t be sent to waivers/free agency. Without this feature, a team manager who is out of contention could drop a star player for their buddy, who is first on the waiver order, to pick up, thereby bolstering their team for the playoffs. Please Note: If a player designated Undroppable becomes injured, this does not mean they will be automatically removed from the ESPN Undroppable List. Players are put on the list before the season begins due to their star potential. ESPN may choose not to remove a player from the list who is still expected to return at some point during the season/playoffs. The Undroppable Player List is used in all Standard Leagues. In a League Manager League, the League Manager (LM) can turn off the Undroppable List by doing the following: #### Turn off Undroppable Players List for League Manager leagues (Web Only).  NOTE: If necessary, the LM can do this temporarily. Once a player is dropped, the LM can turn it on again to prevent further drops. 1. Click on the** LM Tools** tab 2. Click on Edit League Settings 3. Click on Edit next to Player Rules 4. Select No next to Observe ESPN’s Undroppable Player List 5. Save Changes

Fantasy Hockey: Playoffs and Tiebreakers

Editing Your League’s Playoff Schedule

League Managers only: Only the League Manager can adjust the playoff schedule. This can only be done via the fantasy website, not the mobile app. Recommended browser: Google Chrome. #### To Edit Your League’s Playoff Schedule (Web Only) 1. Go to LM Tools. 2. Click Edit Schedule Settings. 3. Adjust any of the following settings as needed: Regular Season length 4. Tiebreakers 5. Home Field Advantage points 6. Playoff brackets, Matchup Duration, Seeding Tiebreaker, and Playoff Home Field Advantage 7. Reset Schedule 8. Scroll down and click** Save Changes.**

H2H Each Category League: Playoff Seeding Tiebreakers

When your fantasy league enters playoff mode, every team receives a seed based on their regular season results. That seed determines their bracket position. This article explains how seeds are assigned and how ties are broken in H2H Each Category leagues. Applies to: H2H Each Category leagues with playoff settings. For H2H Points leagues or H2H Most Categories leagues, refer to the tiebreaker articles for those formats. #### How Seeds Are Assigned When the regular season ends, the system assigns seeds automatically using two primary factors, in order: 1. Division Winners — Division winners always occupy the top seeds. This step is skipped in leagues with no divisions. 2. Winning Percentage — Among remaining seeds, the team with the best winning percentage earns the higher seed.

Reminder: Division winners always claim the first seeds in the bracket. In LM leagues, the League Manager has final authority over playoff rules. #### Tiebreaker Sequence: H2H Each Category When two or more teams finish with identical winning percentages, the following tiebreakers are applied in order. Once a team is seeded, the process resets from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams. - Step: Tiebreaker: How it works - 1: H2H Record (among tied teams)* Default setting; can be changed by the League Manager: Best head-to-head record among the tied teams wins. Only valid if all tied teams have played each other an equal number of times; otherwise, skip to Step 2. - 2: Intradivisional Record Only applies in leagues with multiple divisions*: Best head-to-head record within the same division wins. - 3: Coin Flip: A virtual coin flip determines the seed if all other tiebreakers are exhausted.

Tiebreaker Example: Four Teams, All have 86–88–16 records

The following example walks through the full seeding process for a four-team tie competing for seeds #3 through #6. All teams finished 86–88–16. - Team: Division: Intradivisional Record: vs. A: vs. B: vs. C / vs. D - Team A: Div 1, 2nd: 56–54–10: —: 6–4 (1 game): vs. C: 6–4 (1 game) vs. D: 6–4 (1 game) - Team B: Div 2, 2nd: 64–52–4: 4–6 (1 game): —: vs. C: 10–10 (2 games) vs. D: 16–4 (2 games) - Team C: Div 2, 3rd: 32–70–18: 4–6 (1 game): 10–10 (2 games): vs. D: 10–10 (2 games) - Team D: Div 2, 4th: 33–69–18: 4–6 (1 game): 4–16 (2 games): vs. C: 10–10 (2 games)

Round 1: Determine the #3 Seed (Teams A, B, C, D)

We start with H2H records among all four teams: - Team A: played 3 games among the tied group - Team B: played 5 games among the tied group - Team C: played 5 games among the tied group - Team D: played 5 games among the tied group

H2H tiebreaker is invalid: The four teams did not all play each other an equal number of times (Team A played only 3 games vs. the others’ 5). We move to Intradivisional Record. Intradivisional Record comparison (by winning percentage): - Team A: 56–54–10 (.509) - Team B: 64–52–4 (.547) ← best - Team C: 32–70–18 (.317) - Team D: 33–69–18 (.325)

Team B earns the #3 seed. Reset: The tiebreaker process restarts from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams (A, C, and D). ##### Round 2: Determine the #4 Seed (Teams A, C, D) We check H2H records among the three remaining teams: - Team A: played 2 games among the remaining group - Team C: played 3 games among the remaining group - Team D: played 3 games among the remaining group

H2H tiebreaker is invalid: Teams A, C, and D did not all play each other an equal number of times. We move to Intradivisional Record. Intradivisional Record comparison: - Team A: 56–54–10 (.509) ← best - Team C: 32–70–18 (.317) - Team D: 33–69–18 (.325)

Team A earns the #4 seed. Reset: The tiebreaker process restarts from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams (C and D). ##### Round 3: Determine the #5 Seed (Teams C and D) We check H2H records between the two remaining teams: - Team C vs. Team D: 10–10 across 2 games — a draw

H2H tiebreaker is a draw: A tied head-to-head record doesn’t break the tie. We move to Intradivisional Record. Intradivisional Record comparison: - Team C: 32–70–18 (.317) - Team D: 33–69–18 (.325) ← better

Team D earns the #5 seed. Team C receives the #6 seed. #### League Manager (LM) Leagues In LM leagues, the League Manager can customize or override the default tiebreaker sequence using the Edit Playoffs page in LM Tools. Best practice: If your league uses custom tiebreakers, define and publish them clearly on the League Office page before the season begins to avoid disputes.

H2H Most Categories League Playoff Seeding: How Tiebreakers Work

When your fantasy league enters playoff mode, every team receives a seed based on its regular-season results. That seed determines their bracket position. This article explains how seeds are assigned and how ties are broken in H2H Most Categories leagues. Applies to: H2H Most Categories leagues with playoff settings. For H2H Points leagues or H2H Each Categories leagues, refer to the tiebreaker articles for those formats. #### How Seeds Are Assigned When the regular season ends, the system assigns seeds automatically using two primary factors, in order: 1. Division Winners — Division winners always occupy the top seeds. This step is skipped in leagues with no divisions. 2. Winning Percentage — Among remaining seeds, the team with the best winning percentage earns the higher seed.

Reminder: Division winners always claim the first seeds in the bracket. In LM leagues, the League Manager has final authority over playoff rules. #### Tiebreaker Sequence: H2H Most Categories When two or more teams finish with identical winning percentages, the following tiebreakers are applied in order. Once a team is seeded, the process resets from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams. - Step: Tiebreaker: How it works - 1: H2H Record (among tied teams)* Default setting; can be changed by the League Manager: Best head-to-head record among the tied teams wins. Only valid if all tied teams have played each other an equal number of times; otherwise, skip to Step 2. - 2: Intradivisional Record Only applies in leagues with multiple divisions*: Best head-to-head record within the same division wins. - 3: Coin Flip: A virtual coin flip determines the seed if all other tiebreakers are exhausted.

Tiebreaker Example: Three Teams, All with 8–8–3 records

The following example walks through the full seeding process for a three-team tie. All teams finished 8–8–3. - Team: Division: Intradivisional Record: H2H vs. A: H2H vs. B - Team A: Div 1, 2nd: 4–3–2: —: 1–0 - Team B: Div 2, 2nd: 6–2–1: 0–1: — - Team C: Div 2, 3rd: 3–5–1: 0–0–1 (tie): 1–1–1

Step 1: Check H2H Records Among All Three Teams

We compare how many times each team played the others: - Team A played 2 games among the tied group (1–0–1 overall) - Team B played 4 games among the tied group (1–2–1 overall) - Team C played 4 games among the tied group (1–1–2 overall)

H2H tiebreaker is invalid: The three teams did not all play each other an equal number of times (Team A only played 2 games vs. the others’ 4). We move to Intradivisional Record. ##### Step 2: Compare Intradivisional Records Comparing winning percentages within each team’s division: - Team A: 4–3–2 (.556) - Team B: 6–2–1 (.722) ← best - Team C: 3–5–1 (.389)

Team B earns the top seed among the three tied teams. Reset: The tiebreaker process now restarts from Step 1 for the remaining tied teams (A and C). ##### Step 3: Break the Tie Between Teams A and C Both teams are 8–8–3. We start again at H2H record: - Team A vs. Team C: 0–0–1 (they tied their only matchup)

H2H tiebreaker is a draw: A tied matchup doesn’t break the tie. We move to Intradivisional Record. Intradivisional Record comparison: - Team A: 4–3–2 (.556) ← better - Team C: 3–5–1 (.389)

Team A earns the next seed. Team C receives the final seed. What if Teams A and C had identical intradivisional records? If both were, say, 4–4–1, the next tiebreaker would be a coin flip. #### League Manager (LM) Leagues In LM leagues, the League Manager can customize or override the default tiebreaker sequence using the Edit Playoffs page in LM Tools. Best practice: If your league uses custom tiebreakers, define and publish them clearly on the League Office page before the season begins to avoid disputes.

H2H Points League Playoff Seeding: How Tiebreakers Work

When your fantasy league enters playoff mode, every team receives a seed based on its regular-season results. That seed determines their bracket position. This article explains how seeds are assigned and how ties are broken. Applies to: H2H Points leagues with playoff settings, and all ESPN Fantasy Football leagues (which use the H2H Points format). For H2H Most Categories or H2H Each Category leagues, refer to the tiebreaker article for those formats. #### How Seeds Are Assigned When the regular season ends, the system assigns seeds automatically using two primary factors, in order: 1. Division Winners — Division winners always occupy the top seeds. This step is skipped in leagues with no divisions. 2. Winning Percentage — Among non-division-winner seeds, the team with the best winning percentage earns the higher seed.

Reminder: Division winners always claim the first seeds in the bracket. In LM leagues, the League Manager has final authority over playoff rules. #### Standard Tiebreaker Sequence When two or more teams finish the regular season with identical winning percentages, the following tiebreakers are applied in order until the tie is resolved. Once a team is seeded, the process restarts from the top for the next seed. - Step: Tiebreaker: How it works - 1: H2H Record (among tied teams): Best head-to-head record among the tied teams wins. Only valid if all tied teams have played each other an equal number of times; otherwise, skip to Step 2. - 2: Points For: Most total points scored during the regular season wins. - 3: Intradivisional Record: Best head-to-head record within the same division wins. - 4: Points Against: Most points scored against the team wins. A higher total suggests a tougher schedule. - 5: Coin Flip: A virtual coin flip determines the seed if all other tiebreakers are exhausted.

Tiebreaker Process: Two Teams Tied

  1. Compare H2H records between the two teams. Best record wins.
  2. If H2H records are equal, compare Points For. Most points wins.
  3. If Points For are equal, compare Intradivisional Record.
  4. If Intradivisional Record is equal, compare Points Against. Most points wins.
  5. If still tied, a** virtual coin flip** determines the seed.

Tiebreaker Process: Multiple Teams Tied

When more than two teams are tied, the process works one seed at a time — determine the top seed among the tied group, remove that team, then repeat for the next seed. 1. Compare H2H records among all tied teams. The team with the best overall record earns the top seed. 2. Among the remaining tied teams, compare H2H records again. 3. If the remaining teams did not play each other an equal number of times, skip to Points For. The team with the highest Points For earns the next seed. 4. Repeat until all tied teams are seeded.

Key rule: After each seed is assigned, the tiebreaker process resets from Step 1 (H2H Record) for the remaining tied teams. #### Tiebreaker Example: Five Teams, All win 7–5 records The following example shows the full seeding process for a five-team tie. All teams finished 7–5. - Team: Division / Standing: Points For: H2H Results vs. Other Tied Teams - Team A: Div 1, 3rd: 825: Beat B and E; lost to C and D - Team B: Div 1, 2nd: 918: Beat C; lost to A and E; did not play D - Team C: Div 2, 1st ★: 725: Beat A; lost to B, D, and E - Team D: Div 2, 2nd: 720: Beat A, C, and E; did not play B - Team E: Div 1, 1st ★: 920: Beat B and C; lost to A and D

★ = Division winner ##### Step 1: Seed the Division Winners (#1 and #2 seeds) Teams E and C are division winners. They go to the top two seeds. To determine which gets #1: - Team E beat Team C in their head-to-head matchup. - Team E → #1 seed. Team C → #2 seed.

No divisions? If your league has no divisions, skip this step. The team with the best winning percentage earns the #1 seed directly. ##### Step 2: Determine the #3 Seed (Teams A, B, D) All three teams are 7–5. We start with H2H records among the three: - Team A: 1–1 (beat B, lost to D) - Team B: 0–1 (lost to A; did not play D) - Team D: 1–0 (beat A; did not play B)

H2H tiebreaker is invalid here: The three teams did not all play each other an equal number of times (B and D never met). We move to Points For. Points For comparison: - Team A: 825 - Team B: 918 ← highest - Team D: 720

Team B earns the #3 seed. ##### Step 3: Determine the #4 Seed (Teams A and D) The tiebreaker resets. Both teams are 7–5. We compare their head-to-head matchup: - Team D beat Team A.

Team D earns the #4 seed. Team A receives the #5 seed. ##### League Manager (LM) Leagues In LM leagues, the League Manager can customize or override the default tiebreaker sequence using the Edit Playoffs page in LM Tools. Best practice: If your league uses custom tiebreakers, define and publish them clearly on the League Office page before the season begins to avoid disputes. Grandfathered Custom Leagues only: ”Most Points from Bench” is available as a tiebreaker option exclusively for grandfathered Custom Leagues that used this rule in prior seasons. It is not available for new leagues.

Playoff Scoring & Tiebreakers

Scoring

Playoff scoring follows the same rules as the regular season, with one key difference: Standard leagues: Each playoff round spans two weeks rather than the one-week matchup periods used during the regular season. League Manager leagues: Each playoff round is two weeks by default, but the LM can adjust the length to their desires. #### Tiebreakers If a playoff matchup ends in a tie: - The higher-seeded team advances. This is the default behavior in both standard leagues and League Manager leagues. - League Manager leagues: The League Manager has final authority over which team advances in a tied matchup. Custom tiebreaker systems can be configured using the Edit Head-to-Head Schedule option in LM Tools. The League Manager manually advances the winning team under the league’s chosen tiebreaker rules. - Grandfathered Custom Leagues only: ”Most Points from Bench” is available as a tiebreaker option exclusively for grandfathered Custom Leagues that used this rule in prior seasons. It is not available for new leagues.

Regular Season and Tiebreakers

Our system automatically generates playoff seeds for your league based on the regular season standings. There are two factors for determining these playoff seeds:

  1. Division Winner(s)
  2. Winning Percentage

Fantasy Hockey: Trades and Waivers

Change Acquisition and Waiver Settings (LM Only)

The League Manager (LM) can modify waiver settings and player signings allowed during the season. Players added via trade do not count against any team’s signing limits. This setting can be changed by the LM at any time during the season. 1. Click on LM Tools. 2. Click on Edit League Settings. 3. Click on Transactions and Keepers. 4. Click on the Edit button next to Signing and Waiver Rules.Options for Modification include: Lineup Changes 5. Player Signing System 6. Season Signing Limit 7. Matchup Signing Limit 8. Waiver Period 9. Waiver Order 10. Once you have made your selections, scroll down and click Save Changes.

Claim a Player Off Waivers

Waivers Overview

Waivers are the system that controls how players move from one team to another in your league. - Waivers process daily around 3:00 AM ET. - Players dropped after being rostered for more than 24 hours go to waivers. - Unclaimed players become Free Agents. - Free Agents can be added immediately and do not affect waiver priority. - Yellow button = Waiver claim. - Green button = Immediate Free Agent add. - You must confirm all transactions before they are processed.

QUICK LINKS

  • When Do Waivers Process?
  • When Does a Player Go on Waivers?
  • What Happens After the Waiver Processes?
  • How do Salary Cap Leagues Work?
  • How to Claim a Player in the ESPN Fantasy App
  • How to Claim a Player on the Web
  • Viewing Waiver Details
  • Managing Pending Claims
When Do Waivers Process?
  • Waivers are typically processed daily around 3:00 AM ET.
  • At that time, the system reviews all submitted waiver claims and awards players based on your league’s waiver rules.
When Does a Player Go on Waivers?

Whether a dropped player goes to waivers or becomes a free agent depends on how long they were on a team. - If a player is on a team for less than 24 hours and is dropped, they usually become a Free Agent immediately. - If a player is on a team for more than 24 hours and is dropped, they are placed on Waivers.

What Happens After the Waiver Process?

After the waiver period ends, one of two things happens: - If a team submits a successful claim, that team receives the player. - If no one claimed the player, they clear waivers.

Once a player clears waivers, they enter the Free Agent pool. Free Agents can be added immediately on a first-come, first-served basis, and adding them does not affect your waiver position. ##### How do Salary Cap Leagues Work? If your league uses a Salary Cap system: - Managers bid virtual dollars on players. - The highest bid wins. - If there is a tie, the waiver tiebreaker order determines the winner.

If you win a waiver claim in a Salary Cap league, you move to the bottom of the waiver tiebreaker order, the same as in non-Salary Cap leagues. #### How to Claim a Player in the ESPN Fantasy App ##### Open the Players Tab - Tap Players at the bottom of the app. - By default, you’ll see the top available Free Agents. - You can:

Use the Search field to find a specific player. - Browse the full list of available players.

Select a Player

Tap the player’s name to open their player card. You will see one of two buttons: - Yellow “Claim Player”

The player is currently on waivers. - They are not immediately available. - Tapping this submits a waiver claim. - If you have a higher priority than other teams claiming the same player, you will receive them during the waiver process.

Green “+ Add” - The player is a Free Agent. - They are immediately available. - Tapping this adds the player to your team right away (if you have roster space).

IMPORTANT NOTE: If your roster is full, you will be prompted to drop a player. Additionally, if you are in a league that limits the number of players you may have at a particular position, you will need to drop a player with that primary position. ##### Dropping a Player (If Needed) If required: - Tap the Drop button next to the player you want to remove. - The button will turn red to show it’s selected. - You may select more than one player if needed.

NOTE: Some players may have a “Can’t Drop” label. These players are on the Undroppables list and cannot be removed. ##### Confirm the Transaction - Tap Confirm to complete the claim. You will see a confirmation message once it has been submitted.

How to Claim a Player on the Web

Navigate to Add Players
  • Click the My Team tab.
  • Click Players.
  • Select Add Players.
Find a Player
  • Use the Free Agent filters or search by name.

IMPORTANT: If a player is already on another team, they will not appear as available. To view them, change the filter to All. To acquire that player, you must send a Trade Offer to their current team. ##### Select the Player - Yellow “+” = Player is on waivers - Green “+” = Player is a Free Agent

Drop a Player (If Required)

If your roster is full: - Click the Drop button next to the player you want to remove. - The button will turn red. - Click Continue.

NOTE: If the Drop button is greyed out, that player cannot be dropped. ##### Confirm the Transaction - Click Confirm to submit your claim. - A green confirmation banner will appear once submitted.

Viewing Waiver Details

You can track your waiver activity on the My Team page. There you can: - View your Waiver Claim Position. - Click Waiver Order List to see the full league priority order. - Click Pending Moves to view your submitted claims.

Managing Pending Claims

Inside Pending Moves, you can: - Reorder claims by dragging them into your preferred priority. - Cancel a claim by clicking Cancel Claim.

NOTE: Canceling a claim immediately removes it and cannot be undone. ##### Position Eligibility and Position Limits In League Manager (LM) leagues, the LM may set a cap on the number of players at a given position who can be on a single roster. This is common in larger leagues to help ensure every manager has a fair shot at building a competitive team. ###### How limits work If your league has a position limit and you want to add a player that would push you over that limit, you’ll need to drop an existing player at that position first before the transaction can go through. ###### What happens when a player qualifies at multiple positions? Some players are eligible at more than one position — for example, a player listed as 1B/3B. In these cases, the first position listed is always considered the primary position for roster limits. Here’s a practical example from ESPN Fantasy Baseball: Let’s say you need a third baseman. You’re under the limit at 3B, but you’ve already hit the limit at 1B. You try to claim a 1B/3B player off waivers. Even though you need him for third base, the system sees him primarily as a 1B—so you’ll need to drop one of your existing first basemen before the transaction will go through.

Free Agent Budget (FAB)

An option for ESPN Fantasy Hockey League Manager leagues is Free Agent Budget, or “FAB”. - Free Agent Budget (FAB) - Teams have a specific budget that they can use for player signings. All offers are processed after the league’s specified waiver period. If a team would like to add a player, that team will secretly offer the salary amount they are willing to pay. On the waiver process day, the team with the highest offer will be awarded the player, and the salary will be subtracted from that team manager’s budget. Players who are not claimed during offer processing become free agents available on a first-come, first-serve style pickup basis.

  • Free Agent Budget (FAB) (Continuous) - Teams will have a specific budget to use for player signings. All offers will be processed in batches one or more times each week (as specified in the settings). If a team would like to add a player, that team will offer the salary amount they are willing to pay. On the next waiver process day, the team with the highest offer will be awarded the player, and the salary amount will be subtracted from that team’s budget. All unclaimed players must go through the waiver process in order to be picked up by a team.

FAB waiver order is determined in the same fashion as non-FAB. If you make a waiver claim and win it, you get moved to the bottom of the waiver order list.

How does the Injured Reserve / Injury List impact Waivers?

The system automatically places the IR (Injured Reserve) or IL (Injury List) tag on a player once ESPN receives the league’s status report. Only players with the IR (Injured Reserve) or IL (Injury List) tag are eligible; the day limit does not matter. At its most basic and simple level, when you place an eligible player into the IR/IL slot, you gain an open roster slot. As long as the IR/IL player is eligible for the IR/IL slot, basic waiver offers and free agent pickups will remain unchanged. Where it can get tricky is when you attempt to pick up a player via waiver claim or free agency, and the player’s status in the IR/IL slot changes. The system will always ensure that you do not exceed the roster size limit for your league. Some scenarios to consider when making a claim while you have a player in an IL slot: - If you have a healthy player in an IR/IL slot, you cannot add any new players to your roster.When you attempt to acquire a free agent with a healthy player in an IR/IL slot, you will receive a message to clear your IR/IL before you can make a claim.

  • You will still need to free up a roster slot before you can move the now healthy player out of the IR/IL slot.

How does the Trade Deadline work?

The Trade Deadline is the latest a trade can be offered and accepted.  After the trade deadline passes, managers will NOT be able to send/accept trade offers from other teams. This is to ensure the playoffs are not influenced by trades between contenders and eliminated teams.  The date of the Trade Deadline depends on which type of league you are in. #### TRADE DEADLINES IN PUBLIC LEAGUES In all ESPN Public fantasy leagues, there is a universal Trade Deadline set by ESPN. #### TRADE DEADLINES IN LEAGUE MANAGER / CUSTOM LEAGUES When creating a League Manager (LM) league, you can choose different trade deadlines for the available dates/times.  After the trade deadline has passed, managers will NOT be able to send/accept trade offers to other teams. ##### IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS - Trades must be ACCEPTED by the trade deadline - Voting must be finished PRIOR to the trade deadline - Team managers are still free to add and drop players via free agency and waivers throughout the entire season - LM vetoes/upholds must be executed PRIOR to the trade deadline

EXAMPLE SCENARIOS

NOTE: For these examples, the Trade Deadline is August 19 at 12:00 EDT
Scenario #1 

Public League - 1-day trade review period Team A proposed a trade to Team B on Aug 18 at 7 pm EDT, and Team B accepted the offer at 8:30 pm EDT the same day. (would process Aug 19 at 8:30 pm EDT. Other teams will have until the trade deadline (Aug 19 at 12:00 PM EDT) to either vote to uphold or veto the trade. After the deadline, if the trade does not have enough veto votes, it will be processed as normal on August 19 at 8:30 pm EDT. ##### Scenario #2 Public League - 1-day trade review period Team A proposed a trade to Team B on Aug 19 at 11:15 am EDT, and the manager of Team B did NOT see the offer till 1 pm EDT the same day.  Team B will NOT be able to accept the offer as the trade deadline has passed. The trade will automatically disappear when it expires. ##### Scenario #3 Private League - 2-day trade review period Team A proposed a trade to Team B on Aug 18 at 2 pm EDT, and Team B accepted the offer at 8:30 pm EDT the same day (Aug 18). The trade would be scheduled to process on Aug 20 at 8:30 pm EDT.

Other teams will have until the trade deadline (Aug 19, at 12:00 PM EDT) to either vote to uphold or veto the trade. After the deadline, if the trade does not have enough veto votes, it will process as normal on Aug 20 at 8:30 pm EDT. If the League Manager wants to bypass the trade review period, the request must be made BEFORE the trade deadline. For League Managers who want to uphold/veto the trade after the trade deadline has passed, they will need to extend the trade deadline. Please note the deadline CANNOT be reverted to the original.

How to Vote on a Trade

If 50% of the league (excluding the two teams involved) says NO to a trade, it will be automatically vetoed. The threshold number can be adjusted higher and lower by LMs in League Manager leagues.  Once a trade is accepted, every manager will receive an email with the trade details. The title of the email: A Trade in Your ESPN Fantasy Baseball League Has Been Accepted. When you receive this email, you can click on the Vote on Trade link in the email. Or you can vote manually by visiting your league’s homepage. All accepted trades will show on your League Home Page under Recent Activity.  You will also see a Trade Voting notification beneath the Lgeau Name at the top of the page. You can also access Trades by clicking on League, then Recent Activity. NOTE: If the minimum number of votes to Veto is not met, even if no one votes, the Trade will proceed. To Vote on a Trade on ESPN.com 1. Click the League tab 2. Click Recent Activity 3. Locate the accepted trade 4. Click the Uphold or Veto button

To Vote on a Trade via the ESPN Fantasy App 1. Tap League 2. Scroll down and tap Recent Activity 3. Locate the accepted trade 4. Then tap the Uphold or Veto button

Proposing and Accepting Trade Offers

Trading for players can be one of the most fun aspects of Fantasy Sports. While everyone looks to get the better end of a trade, the most successful trade offers are those that are evenly matched and benefit both parties to the same extent. However, not all trades are balanced, and you should always evaluate any trade before proposing or accepting it. In addition, a severely unbalanced trade in which one team benefits far more than the other may be considered collusive and is prohibited by our rules of Fair Play and Conduct. - Propose Trade on the ESPN Fantasy App - Propose Trade on the Web - How to Accept a Trade - Accepting a Trade on the ESPN Fantasy App - Accepting a Trade on the Web - Position Eligibility and Position Limits - How to Veto or Protest a Trade

Propose Trade on the ESPN Fantasy App

  • Select which team you want to trade with
  • ​Click on “Propose Trade”
  • Click on the player(s) you want to trade
  • ​​Click on the player(s) you want to offer in return
  • Click on “Submit” to finalize the trade​

Propose Trade on the Web

  • First, select which team you’d like to trade with
  • Once on their team page, click on “Propose Trade.”
  • Select the player(s) you wish to receive
  • Give up at least one player by selecting a player (or players) you wish to trade
  • After the trade is submitted, the system will display a pending move on both your team’s and the other team manager’s pages

How to Accept a Trade

  • If you’ve had a trade proposed to you, you can either accept or decline it
  • The system will automatically cancel the trade offer within a specified number of days
  • The entire league will be emailed, so the other team managers can review it and vote against it if the league rules dictate that

Accepting a Trade on the ESPN Fantasy App

  • Navigate to your team’s home page
  • Tap on the clock next to your team name
  • Tap on “Trade Proposals”​​
  • ​Accept or decline the trade from this screen

Accepting a Trade on the Web

  • Navigate to your team’s home page
  • Pending trade offers should appear in a gray box in the middle of your screen
  • Click “Review Trade.”
  • Accept or decline the trade from this screen

Position Eligibility and Position Limits

In League Manager (LM) leagues, the LM may set a cap on the number of players at a given position who can be on a single roster. This is common in larger leagues to help ensure every manager has a fair shot at building a competitive team. How limits work If your league has a position limit and you want to add a player that would push you over that limit, you’ll need to drop an existing player at that position first before the transaction can go through. What happens when a player qualifies at multiple positions? Some players are eligible at more than one position — for example, a player listed as 1B/3B. In these cases, the first position listed is always considered the primary position for roster-limit purposes. Here’s a practical example: let’s say you need a third baseman. You’re under the limit at 3B, but you’ve already hit the limit at 1B. You try to trade for a 1B/3B player off waivers. Even though you need him for third base, the system sees him primarily as a 1B — so you’ll need to drop one of your existing first basemen before the transaction will go through.

Trade Deadline

The Trade Deadline setting determines if the league uses a deadline for trading players between teams. This option is offered to prevent teams from sandbagging at the end of the season by trading blue-chip players for average ones. Once the Trade Deadline date arrives, trading will be disabled. NOTE: Trades accepted before the trade deadline but scheduled to process after the deadline will still process normally. ESPN will set the default trade deadline for all Standard Leagues. This deadline can be adjusted by League Managers in private, League Manager leagues. #### To view your league’s Trade Deadline 1. Go to League 2. Click on** Settings 3. Click on Transactions and Keepers 4. Scroll down to Trade Rules**

All Standard Leagues use the following Trade Deadline

  • The trade deadline applies only to transactions between teams.
  • Team managers are still free to add and drop players via free agency and waivers throughout the entire season.

Set Trade Deadline for League Manager Leagues (Web Only)

  1. Click on LM Tools
  2. Click on Edit League Settings
  3. Click on Transactions and Keepers
  4. Click the Edit button next to Trade RulesOptions for modification include: Trade Limit
  5. Trade Deadline
  6. Trade Review Period
  7. Vetoes Required to Veto Trade
  8. Click the Save Changes button when finished

Trade Limit (LM Only)

Set Trade Limit (Web Only)

In League Manager Leagues, this setting can be changed by the League Manager at any time during the season 1. Click on the League tab.​ 2. Click on Settings. 3. Click on Transactions and Keepers. 4. Click on Trade Rules. 5. Select the number of trades in the dropdown. 6. Click Save Changes when finished.

Settings Options for Trade Limits

  • No Trades - (LM Leagues: Only the League Manager can trade players between teams).
  • No Limit - Default setting. No limit to the number of trades a team can make.
  • Limited - A specific number of transactions is selected (i.e., 5, 10, 15, 20). Once that number of accepted & processed trades has been reached, the team will not be allowed to propose or accept any more trades. However, this will NOT limit their ability to add/drop players via waivers.

Trade Review

Trade Review Period for ESPN League Manager Leagues - Trade Review is the span of time allotted to other team managers in the league who are not directly involved in the trade to decide whether it is fair. - League Managers can determine the duration of this review period:  1 day is the default - 2 days - 3 days - No Trade Review

Trade Review Process - There is a 48-hour trade review period after a trade is accepted, during which team managers can review it. - After the trade offer is submitted, the system will display a pending move on your team page and on other team managers’ pages. - That team manager can then go to his/her team page to review the deal, and accept or decline it - If no action is taken within the specified number of days, the system will automatically cancel the trade offer. The pending move will disappear on both team pages. - If the trade is rejected, the team proposing it will receive an email notifying them of the result. - If the offer is accepted, the entire league will be notified via email, and other team managers can review it according to your league settings. - League Managers can push each trade through before the review period has passed. - Standard leagues: During the trade review period, if four of the ten team managers vote to veto a trade, the trade will be canceled. A link on the main League Office page lets you view pending trades and, if you choose, submit your veto.

Veto or Protest a Trade

The ability to veto a trade is available in order to prevent collusion in a league.  There are two ways to veto a trade, and in League Manager (Private) leagues, these settings can be changed by the LM at any time during the season: Public leagues and/or private leagues with standard settings:  - EVERY team manager in the league has the power to cast a vote against a trade, EXCEPT the two teams involved in the trade. Once a trade is accepted, an email will be sent to every team manager in the league with detailed instructions on how to cast a vote. Follow those steps, and you’ll be all set. - If enough votes are cast against the trade (4 out of 10, 50% of teams NOT involved in the trade), it will be canceled immediately. - Teams with more than one team manager will only receive one vote. - Once player(s) are traded, the players will be on the team’s bench until the Team Manager manually moves them to the active lineup.

Private leagues: - Unless otherwise changed by the LM, all public league settings apply - In LM leagues, LM has the ultimate power to veto a trade or let it go through - LMs can see the number of votes for or against a trade before it is vetoed or processed - If the rare scenario occurs where the setting is changed while the trade is pending approval, that trade will be grandfathered to use the original setting in place when the trade was accepted Under LM Tools -> Edit League settings -> Transactions and Keepers

Waiver Order Overview and Salary Cap Tiebreakers

What’s the difference, and how do they work? Fantasy leagues use one of two systems to determine which team gets priority when adding players who are on waivers. These systems have different names, but they work in very similar ways. NOTE: If you’re unsure which system your league uses, check under Players in your league menu. This guide explains: - What is Waiver Order (Standard Leagues) - Where do I see my Waiver Order? - Who controls the Waiver Order? - What is a Salary Cap tiebreaker? - Similarities Between the Two Systems - Key Differences - What Transactions Affect the Waiver Order? - Position Eligibility and Position Limits

What is a Waiver Order? (Standard Waiver Leagues)

In standard waiver leagues, teams are placed in a ranked list called the Waiver Order. When multiple teams try to claim the same player during the waiver period, the team with the higher priority (closer to the top of the list) gets the player. #### Where do I see the Waiver Order? Go to:  Players → Waiver Order #### Who controls Waiver Order? - In public leagues, the waiver order is set automatically. - In private leagues, the League Manager (LM) can manually adjust the order:

Click Edit - Drag teams into the desired position - Click Save Changes to finalize

What is Salary Cap Tiebreaker?

In leagues that use a Salary Cap system, managers bid virtual dollars on players who are on waivers. - The team that bids the highest amount wins the player. - If two or more teams bid the same amount, a tiebreaker order determines who gets the player. - To see the details: Go to: Players → Budget Summary - In League Manager leagues, the League Manager can edit each team’s budget:

Click Edit - Change the budget amount - Click Save Changes

Similarities Between the Two Systems

Even though they work differently, both systems share some important rules. ##### How the Order Updates Both systems can refresh in one of two ways, depending on league settings: ##### Option A: Reset Each Week - Each Monday at 12:00 AM PT / 3:00 AM ET (when a new fantasy week begins), the order resets. - The reset is based on inverse standings (teams with worse records get higher priority).

Option B: Move to Last After Claim
  • When a team successfully claims a player during the waiver process, that team moves to the bottom of the order.
  • The order does not automatically reset under this setting.

Important: No matter which option is selected, once a team successfully makes a waiver claim, they move to the bottom of the waiver priority list. ##### How the Initial Order Is Set Both systems use the same rules to determine the starting order. ###### If your league uses a Salary Cap draft: - The team with the most money remaining after the draft gets the highest waiver priority. - If teams are tied, the team that completed its roster first during the draft gets higher priority.

If your league uses a Snake Draft:
  • The draft order is reversed.
  • The team that picked first in the draft starts last in waiver order.
  • The team that picked last in the draft starts first in waiver order.

In short, the waiver order begins as the inverse of the draft order. #### Key Differences ##### League Manager Editing - In standard waiver order leagues, the League Manager can edit the waiver order at any time. - In Salary Cap** leagues**, the League Manager cannot manually edit the tiebreaker order after the waiver process.

NOTE:  - The League Manager can reverse a player claim if needed. - However, they cannot manually adjust the tiebreaker order itself in Salary Cap leagues.

What Transactions Affect the Waiver Order?

Waiver Claim

A waiver claim happens when: - A player is on waivers (not immediately available) - You submit a claim request - The system processes the claim after the waiver period ends

Waiver claims affect waiver priority. ##### Free Agency Pickup A free agency pickup happens when: - A player is immediately available - You add them instantly without waiting for a waiver period

Free agency pickups do NOT affect waiver order. #### Position Eligibility and Position Limits In League Manager (LM) leagues, the LM may set a cap on the number of players at a given position who can be on a single roster. This is common in larger leagues to help ensure every manager has a fair shot at building a competitive team. ##### How limits work If your league has a position limit and you want to add a player that would push you over that limit, you’ll need to drop an existing player at that position first before the transaction can go through. ##### What happens when a player qualifies at multiple positions? Some players are eligible at more than one position — for example, a player listed as 1B/3B. In these cases, the first position listed is always considered the primary position for roster limits. Here’s a practical example from ESPN Fantasy Baseball: Let’s say you need a third baseman. You’re under the limit at 3B, but you’ve already hit the limit at 1B. You try to claim a 1B/3B player off waivers. Even though you need him for third base, the system sees him primarily as a 1B—so you’ll need to drop one of your existing first basemen before the transaction will go through.

Waivers Overview

Players who are free agents (i.e., undrafted or already on a team roster) are available to be picked up off waivers. If you are not happy with a specific player at a position and don’t want to worry about trading with another league team manager, you can add any player from the Free Agent list. You may need to drop a player to keep your roster at the league’s maximum. All undrafted players will be set as ‘On Waivers’ immediately after the draft, each week of play, or if dropped from another team’s roster. Players on waivers will remain on waivers for a set period, during which all teams will have the opportunity to claim any player. When the waiver period expires, the player will be awarded to the team with the highest waiver priority that made a claim, and that team will move to the end of the waiver order. This process continues until all waiver claims are processed, after which all players not added via waivers become free agents who can be acquired by any team on a first-come, first-served basis. #### Standard Waivers  All unsigned players are put on waivers immediately following the league’s draft. This happens from the start of the first game until a few hours past the end of the last, and when players are dropped from another team. When the waiver period expires, usually around 3 am ET, all claims from that period will be processed according to the waiver order.

Players on waivers will remain on waivers for a set period (Waiver period), during which all teams will have the opportunity to make a claim on any player. When the waiver period expires, the player will be awarded to the team with the highest waiver priority that made a claim, and that team will move to the end of the waiver order. This process continues until all waiver claims are processed, after which all players not added via waivers become free agents, which can be acquired by any team on a first-come, first-served basis. #### Salary Cap Continuous Teams will have a specific budget to use for player signings. All offers will be processed in batches one or more times each week (as specified in the settings). If a team would like to add a player, it will offer the salary it is willing to pay. On the next waiver process day, the team with the highest offer will be awarded the player, and the salary amount will be subtracted from that team’s budget. All unclaimed players must go through the waiver process in order to be picked up by a team. Salary Cap waiver order is determined in the same fashion as non-Salary Cap, except it will be called Salary Cap Tiebreaker. If you win a waiver claim, whether by bidding more or by winning via higher priority, you will be moved to the bottom of the waiver order. NOTE: Selecting this system means ALL players not on a roster will ALWAYS be on waivers. Managers will not be able to make game-time roster additions. The League Manager would be the only person able to add players to teams via LM Tools. #### No Waivers Every player is immediately available to be added to your team as a free agent once they enter the candidate pool. Most leagues choose to use waivers rather than No Waivers, as this system is often deemed unfair.

Players who are not drafted or on a current roster are available to be picked up off waivers at all times. If you are not happy with a specific player at a position and don’t want to worry about trading with another league team manager, you can add any player from the Free Agent list. You may have to drop a player to keep your roster at the league’s maximum number of players.

Login Issues: Clearing DNS Cache Windows, Mac, and Firefox

Fixing Login Issues — Clearing Your DNS Cache

Sometimes your computer holds onto old internet data that can interfere with logging in. Clearing it out (called “flushing your DNS”) is easier than it sounds! Just follow the steps below for your computer type. #### Windows Users First, figure out which version of Windows you have. Not sure? Click the Start button and search “About my PC” — it’ll tell you right there. ##### Windows 11 1. Click the Start button and type PowerShell in the search bar 2. Right-click Windows PowerShell and select Run as Administrator 3. Type exactly: ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter 4. You should see a message confirming the cache was cleared 5. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Windows 10
  1. Right-click the Start button (bottom left corner of your screen) and select Command Prompt (Admin)
  2. Type exactly: ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter
  3. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Windows 8
  1. Click the Start button and type cmd in the search bar
  2. When Command Prompt appears in the results, right-click it and select Run as Administrator
  3. Type exactly: ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Windows 7 or Vista
  1. Click the Start button, then navigate to All Programs → Accessories → Command Prompt
  2. Right-click Command Prompt and select Run as Administrator
  3. Type exactly: ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mac Users

On a Mac, this process works through an app called Terminal. You can find it by opening Spotlight Search (press ⌘ + Spacebar) and typing “Terminal.” Not sure which version of macOS you have? Click the Apple menu in the top left corner and select About This Mac — the version will be displayed right there. #### macOS Sequoia, Sonoma, Ventura, Monterey, or Big Sur (2020 and later) 1. Open Terminal 2. Type exactly: sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Enter 3. You’ll be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so (you won’t see the password as you type — that’s normal!) 4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

macOS Catalina (version 10.15)

  1. Open Terminal
  2. Type exactly: sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Enter
  3. You may be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

macOS Mojave, High Sierra, or Sierra (versions 10.14, 10.13, or 10.12)

  1. Open Terminal
  2. Type exactly: sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Enter
  3. You may be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

macOS El Capitan, Mavericks, or Mountain Lion (versions 10.11, 10.9, or 10.8)

  1. Open Terminal
  2. Type exactly: sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Enter
  3. You may be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mac OS X Yosemite (version 10.10)

  1. Open Terminal
  2. Type exactly: sudo discoveryutil udnsflushcaches and press Enter
  3. You may be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mozilla Firefox Users

  • Firefox users can install the DNS Flusher add-on then follow the instructions to clear the DNS cache.
  • Return to ESPN.com and attempt to Log In

 Tips:

  • When typing these commands, copy them exactly as written; spacing and capitalization matter!
  • On Mac, it’s normal for Terminal to show nothing after running the command — that means it worked!
  • If you’re still having trouble after following these steps, don’t hesitate to reach out to ESPN Support.

Login Issues: Clearing Your Cache & Cookies (Chrome, Safari & Firefox)

Fixing Login Issues — Clearing Your Cache & Cookies

Your browser stores bits of website data to help pages load faster—but sometimes that stored data becomes outdated, causing problems like login issues or pages not displaying correctly. Clearing it out is quick and easy! Just find your browser below and follow the steps. Heads up: After clearing your cache and cookies, you’ll likely be logged out of websites you normally stay signed into—including ESPN. Just log back in as usual, and you should be good to go! ##### Google Chrome (Desktop) 1. Click the three vertical dots (⋮) in the top-right corner of Chrome 2. Hover over History, then click History again in the menu that appears 3. On the left side, click Clear browsing data 4. Set the Time Range to All time 5. Make sure both Cookies and other site data, and Cached images and files are checked 6. Click Clear data 7. Close Chrome completely and reopen it, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Google Chrome (Mobile — iPhone or Android)
  1. Tap the three dots in the top-right corner (Android) or bottom-right corner (iPhone)
  2. Tap History, then Clear browsing data
  3. Set the Time Range to All time
  4. Make sure Cookies, site data, and Cached images and files are both selected
  5. Tap Clear data and confirm
  6. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Apple Safari (Desktop — Mac)
  1. Click Safari in the top menu bar and select Settings (or Preferences on older Macs)
  2. Click the Privacy tab
  3. Click Manage Website Data, then Remove All
  4. Confirm by clicking Remove Now
  5. Close and reopen Safari, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Shortcut option: You can also click History in the top menu bar, select Clear History, set it to All History, and click Clear History to confirm. ##### Apple Safari (Mobile — iPhone or iPad) 1. Open the Settings app on your device (not Safari itself) 2. Scroll down and tap Apps, then tap Safari 3. Tap Clear History and Website Data 4. Select your preferred timeframe and tap Clear History and Data to confirm 5. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mozilla Firefox (Desktop)
  1. Click the three horizontal lines (☰) in the top-right corner of Firefox
  2. Click Settings
  3. On the left, click Privacy & Security
  4. Scroll down to the Cookies and Site Data section and click Clear Data
  5. Make sure both Cookies, Site Data, and Cached Web Content are checked
  6. Click Clear, then confirm by clicking Clear Now
  7. Close Firefox completely and reopen it, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Pro Tip

On Windows or Mac, you can also use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + Delete (Windows) or ⌘ + Shift + Delete (Mac) while in any of these browsers to jump straight to the clear data screen! If you’ve cleared your cache and cookies and are still having trouble, don’t hesitate to reach out to ESPN Fan Support by clicking on the chat icon at the lower right of this screen— we’re happy to help!

ESPN Fantasy Sports - How to be a Great League Manager - Part 1

This brief video introduces the role of League Manager (LM). You will get an overview of LM responsibilities, league settings, and helpful tips to help avoid common issues.

ESPN Fantasy Sports - How to be a Great League Manager - Part 2

This short video provides an overview of the League Manager (LM) Tools and how to access them on either the ESPN Fantasy app or on ESPN.com. I also introduced common league settings and usage, along with helpful tips to create a hassle-free LM experience for you and your managers.

Fair Play and Conduct

Although Fantasy Sports are extremely competitive, we emphasize that all participants exercise good sportsmanship to prevent team managers from unintentionally crossing the line and maintain a fun environment. A note on Fair Play and Conduct in ESPN Fantasy Leagues: ESPN oversees all leagues on the platform. In standard public leagues, ESPN serves as your commissioner and is your first point of contact for any issues. In League Manager (LM) leagues, your LM handles day-to-day management and is your go-to for questions or concerns—with ESPN available as a backstop to help ensure every league runs smoothly for everyone involved. A. More than one team in the same league B. Collusive Transactions C. Impeding Other Team Managers D. Roster Dumping E. Team Manager Interactions F. Offensive Language G. Inactivity H. League Manager Leagues #### A: More Than One Team in the Same League (ESPN Standard Leagues) - One person can’t control more than one team in the same league. - If two or more teams in the same league are under the same account, they must be controlled by different people who share that account but not the teams. - Violation of this will result in team cancellation and expulsion from the game.

B: Collusive Transactions

  • Collusion occurs when one team makes moves to benefit another team, without trying to improve its own position.
  • One-sided trades are an example of collusive transactions.
  • Dropping a player so another team can pick up that player is another example of collusive transactions.
  • Teams found in violation of this policy will be canceled, and their team managers will be prohibited from participating in future ESPN Fantasy Games.

NOTE: Standard League members are expected to veto/protest any and all unfair or collusive trades throughout the season. At least 4 team managers’ votes are required in protest for a trade to be denied in a Standard League. #### C: Impeding Other Team Managers - Making certain transactions solely to impede other team managers is not allowed. - Tanking games solely to deny another player a chance to make the playoffs is against the rules. - Cycling through players in free agency to put them on waivers and make them unavailable to another team in your league is strictly prohibited and is grounds for expulsion from the game.

D: Roster Dumping

  • Team managers who are found to have dumped their players into the player pool to undermine the league may be expelled from the game.
  • If you are giving up on the season, we ask that you maintain league strength by fielding the most competitive team you can.

E: Team Manager Interaction

  • Team managers should always be polite and gracious when dealing with one another.
  • Threats and obscenities are against the rules and illegal in many jurisdictions.
  • Team managers who are found to have sent threatening emails to another team manager will be warned and/or permanently banned from the ESPN and/or Disney sites.
  • These rules extend to message board posts as well.

F: Offensive Language

  • Any language, including posts, messaging, league and team names, that is derogatory is strictly prohibited.
  • This includes chat rooms, message boards, or the league’s bulletin board.
  • Personal attacks and sexist or racist remarks also fall under this restriction.
  • There is a zero tolerance level. Offenders are subject to a ban from ESPN and/or Disney sites.

G: Inactivity (ESPN Standard Leagues)

  • To maintain the integrity of the league, the commissioner may contact the managers of teams that remain inactive for extended periods.
  • The league commissioner will send a notification to the email on record.
  • If the team remains inactive after the league commissioner sends an email to the inactive team manager, the commissioner reserves the right to reassign the team’s management.

H: League Manager Leagues

  • ESPN Fantasy Baseball League Manager leagues are created according to the specifications implemented by their league creators.
  • The League Manager and other team managers are responsible for handling all conduct, communication, and fair play issues that arise in these LM Leagues.

Fantasy Hockey

What are Fantasy Games?

Have you ever dreamed of what it would be like to own your own professional sports team? Fantasy games are a way to live out that dream. And to make things easier, all fantasy games are fundamentally the same — real athletes and their real-life performances are used to generate points for fantasy teams in fantasy leagues. In a traditional fantasy league, there is a set number of team managers, and a clear set of rules that govern everything from roster size to scoring to schedule. You and your fellow managers hold a draft, filling your fantasy roster with real-life athletes from across the sport. Then, throughout the season, you set your lineup based on how well you think your players will perform. The statistics they generate in real games are collected, and fantasy points are awarded based on those numbers. The better your players perform, the more points your team racks up. Ultimately, those points determine a winner. The team that accumulates the most points — or earns the most points-based wins over the course of the season, or prevails in the postseason — is declared the league champion. And with that title comes all the glory of lording it over your fellow managers… until next season, when they come back hungry for revenge. #### What is ESPN Fantasy Hockey? Welcome to the world of fantasy hockey—ESPN-Style! ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the closest thing you can find to buying your own professional franchise and becoming the team’s coach, team manager, and president. All decisions are yours to make. And lucky for you, hockey is a game filled with unbiased player performance statistics. Using these statistics, you have everything you need to understand which players are performing well and which are not. ESPN’s Fantasy Hockey (FHL) is as close as most of us will come to owning a franchise and becoming the team’s manager, team manager, and president. All decisions are yours to make. Each team manager is supplied with all the tools—multiple draft methods, unlimited waivers and trades, free agency, an empowering commissioner, chat rooms, league bulletin boards, player statistics, and more. In other words, everything needed to build a championship hockey team. Statistical reports, expert analysis, and up-to-date feature articles from ESPN editors are readily available to keep team managers informed. Armed with this information, team managers are free to create the team of their dreams. To win, a team manager has to be crafty, as each team competes directly with nine other team managers who are equally determined to come out on top. Team managers can choose who they compete against and are free to join a league at their own level. Like the race for the final NHL playoff spot, the league title could be determined on the very last day of the season in rotisserie leagues. For head-to-head scoring, the top four teams in each league will play each other in the playoffs, which are held during the final weeks of the NHL regular season. The remaining teams compete in the consolation bracket. Regardless of your regular-season record, your team is guaranteed to play every week of the NHL season. Once you join a league, ESPN provides you with everything needed to build the best possible hockey team. And sure, you got your cut-throat, 11th-hour wheeling and dealing between armchair LMs, fully customizable league rules and scoring, multiple draft methods, live box scores, waivers, trades, free agency, custom player updates, a commissioner, league bulletin boards, sortable stats for all players, and more. There’s plenty of room to sling trash-talk throughout your league, and enough stats and weekly analysis to make you the next ESPN Fantasy Hockey champion. We just want to make sure you know what to do with it all! So sit back as we take you through the keys to ESPN Fantasy Hockey. It’s now time to get crackin’ on creating the next ESPN Fantasy Hockey dynasty!

Network Connection Issues: ESPN Fantasy App

Try these steps in order to identify and fix the issue. Step 1: Verify Your Internet Connection Open Safari (iOS) or Chrome (Android) and go to games.espn.com. If you see an error message, your internet connection is the problem, and the error should indicate the cause. These issues are outside of ESPN’s control, so contact your internet provider if needed. Good to Know: The ESPN Fantasy App requires a moderately strong connection to function. Keep in mind that signal bars on your phone reflect voice/call strength but not the actual speed or reliability of your data connection. Step 2 (iOS Only): Check Cellular Data Settings Make sure Cellular Data is enabled for the ESPN Fantasy App: 1. Open Settings 2. Tap Cellular 3. Scroll down to the app list and find ESPN Fantasy 4. Make sure the toggle is On (green)

Step 3: Try a Different Internet Connection - On Wi-Fi? Try switching to cellular (3G/4G/LTE). - On cellular? Try connecting to a Wi-Fi network instead. - Confirm that other apps or websites load normally on your current connection.

Step 4: Verify Access to the ESPN API In any browser, test your access at http://games.espn.com/ffl/connectivity. If no error messages appear, your device can successfully reach the ESPN API. Step 5: Force-Quit and Reopen the App - iOS: Double-tap the Home button and swipe up on the ESPN Fantasy App. - Android: Open the task manager (long-press Home or use your device’s app switcher) and swipe away the ESPN Fantasy App.

Step 6: Clear the App Cache - iOS: Force-quit the app (Step 5), then go to Settings → Fantasy (look for the rainbow logo) and tap the Reset slider. Relaunch the app. - Android: Force-quit the app (Step 5), then go to App Settings → ESPN Fantasy App and tap Clear Data and Clear Cache. Relaunch the app.

Step 7: Reinstall the App - iOS: Press and hold the app icon, tap the X to uninstall, then reinstall from the App Store. - Android: Uninstall via App Settings, then reinstall from the Play Store.

Still Not Working? If none of these steps help, there may be a larger outage that our team is already working to resolve. Check support.espn.com for the latest updates or open a Chat with ESPN Fan Support by clicking on the icon at the bottom right of this screen.

Fantasy Women’s Basketball: Draft

Autopick Draft

What is an Autopick Draft?

The Autopick Draft option automatically drafts players for every team on a scheduled draft date. Team managers do not need to be online during the draft. #### Preparing Your Draft List - Team managers can pre-rank players to improve their chances of building their preferred roster. - Draft lists can be edited until midnight the day before the scheduled draft.

If No Draft List Is Submitted

  • The system will use the default ESPN draft rankings.

How the Autopick Draft Works

When the draft begins: 1. The system loads each team manager’s draft list. 2. For each pick, the system selects the highest-ranked available player from that list. 3. The player must fit an open roster slot and not exceed roster position limits. 4. The process continues until all roster spots for each team are filled.

Autopick Draft: Post Draft

Conclusion of The Draft

  • After the system finishes processing the autopick draft, it requires a few minutes to convert the league to regular-season mode.
  • Team managers will receive an email notifying them when the draft is complete so they can begin managing their team.

Post-Draft

  • The system automatically fills all of the team rosters with each team’s selected players

  • All undrafted players are put on waivers for two days.

  • Team managers can place claims on undrafted players. Once the two-day waiver period ends, the system will automatically execute the pending waiver claims in priority order.

  • When the waiver period ends, all remaining unclaimed players become free agents and can be picked up on a first-come, first-served basis.

  • League Manager leagues’ waiver rules are based on the League Manager’s initial setup and preferences.

Draft Dates

  • Teams that join a preseason league will draft on the date listed on the league page
  • Always check the listed draft day and draft type before joining a group
  • In Free Standard Leagues, ESPN reserves the right to merge undrafted leagues if they are not filled by the draft time. Leagues will not be split to complete other leagues in order to run a draft.
  • However, if the number of teams in each league equals five, they can be combined to make one full league (at the discretion of the ESPN Fantasy League Office)

Draft Methods

Draft Overview

Your draft is an important factor for a successful season. Teams that begin with a strong draft are most likely to find themselves in good shape for the rest of the season. #### ESPN Standard Leagues  Each team receives a specified number of players during the draft. For example, in a 10-team league where each team has 9 roster slots each, a total of 90 players will be drafted for that league. In ESPN Standard Leagues, there are two draft options available: - Live Snake draft - Live Salary Cap draft

League Manager Leagues

In League Manager (LM) leagues, your final player total depends on your roster settings. LMs have the option of four different draft methods: - Autopick - Live Online Draft - Offline Draft - Salary Cap Draft

LIVE AND MOCK DRAFT LOBBY LEAGUES

The Live Draft Lobby is where it all starts once you are ready to join a Free Standard or League Manager league. Once you’re there, click on a room name. NOTE: The listed Standard League names are for quick identity purposes only, and will change to generic league names, which you can customize by league vote after the draft is complete. After entering the lobby you will see the “Join This League” button. Another method is to locate a Standard league via the League Directory. NOTE: The listed Standard League names are for quick identity purposes only, and will change to generic league names, which you can customize by league vote after the draft is complete. After entering the lobby you will see the “Join This League” button. A #### WAITING FOR THE DRAFT TO START After you successfully join a lobby league, your team name and info will appear on the page in bold. The league’s draft start time is displayed in the middle of the page and on the countdown clock below it. NOTE: In order for a league draft in the live draft lobby to move into drafting mode, all Open Slots must be filled before the listed draft start time. If open slots remain, try recruiting members to join via the message board or simply wait and hope the room will fill itself in time (the page automatically reloads itself every 30 seconds). Any live draft Lobby league (ESPN created league) that is not full before the draft start will have their draft time continually pushed back in five-minute intervals until the league is filled. Draft Schedule Issue

Standard Leagues - In Standard Leagues, the draft will only start once all 4, 6, 8, or 10 team managers join. If one of the team managers forgets to set up their team, your draft cannot start. - The missing team manager(s) need to officially join the league and then a majority of your league members need to cast a vote on when the new draft should happen.

Editing Autopick Draft Strategy

If you’re worried about missing your draft or getting disconnected, you can set an Auto-Pick Draft Strategy ahead of time so the system drafts according to your preferences. #### Accessing Draft Strategy You can edit your draft strategy from your main team page before the draft begins. 1. Click Edit Auto-Pick Strategy. 2. The edit page displays each round of the draft with a pulldown menu.

Choosing a Draft Strategy

For each round, you can select how the system should draft. - The default option is Best Available. - On this setting, the system drafts the highest-ranked remaining player from any position.

You can also choose a specific position. Example: In Fantasy Baseball (applies to all fantasy sports), selecting First Base (1B) will cause the system to draft the highest available First Baseman during that round. #### Setting Position Limits You can control how many players are drafted at each position. - This is managed in the Position Limits table on the right side of the page. - Set the minimum and maximum number of players you want drafted for each position.

Drafting by Stat

You can also instruct the system to draft based on a specific statistic. Example: In Fantasy Baseball (applies to all fantasy sports), selecting RBIs will prioritize players who perform best in that category. #### Editing Deadline You can edit your draft strategy any time until one hour before the scheduled draft time. #### Availability The Edit Auto-Pick Strategy page is only available for leagues using: - Live Snake Draft - Auto-Pick Draft

Enable/Disable Draft Pick Trading: LM Leagues

The League Manager (LM) is the only person who can enable or disable Draft Pick Trading in a league. Draft Pick Trading allows team managers to trade draft slots before the draft begins. Example: A manager might trade their 2nd- and 3rd-round picks to another manager in exchange for that manager’s 1st-round pick. Draft pick trades can be completed on both the ESPN Fantasy App and the web. Note: Draft pick trades can only be made before the draft and apply only to the current season. #### Enabling Draft Pick Trading 1. Go to LM Tools. 2. Select Edit Draft Settings. 3. Set Draft Order to Manually Set by League Manager. 4. Set Allow Draft Pick Trading to Yes. 5. Click Save Changes.

Alternative method: 1. Go to LM Tools. 2. Select Begin Draft Pick Trading. 3. Click Allow Draft Pick Trading and Confirm.

Disabling Draft Pick Trading

  1. Go to LM Tools.
  2. Select Stop Draft Pick Trading and Reset Draft Picks.
  3. Click Confirm.
Important Note

When Draft Pick Trading is disabled: - All traded draft picks are returned to their original teams. - Any players traded along with those picks will remain on their current teams.

To move those players back, the League Manager must manually adjust rosters using LM Tools.

Live Online Snake Drafts

In the Live Online Snake Draft, each team’s manager drafts unique players via a back-and-forth, round-by-round draft order (i.e., 1-10, 10-1, 1-10, 10-1, etc.) until all roster slots are full. Like any prospective team manager, you want to assemble the best possible roster of players, so it’s smart to be prepared before you set out. The following information will brief you on the ins-and-outs of how the Snake Draft works: #### Editing Draft Lists - We highly recommend that all live draft participants customize their draft list before the actual draft. This protects you in case you are unable to participate in your live draft. - The Player list can be reordered using our Pre-Rank tool.  You can also determine which position to draft each round with the Draft Strategy tool.  Both are available on your preseason “My Team” page.  PRO-TIP: Make sure you SAVE your changes before you leave! - NOTE: You may edit your draft list as often as you like, up until one hour before your scheduled draft time.

  1. On your preseason League Office page in the “Draft Info” box.
  2. On your main team page.

  • You may enter your live draft as early as one hour before the scheduled start time.
  • Links to enter the draft are available on your “League Office” and “My Team” pages.
  • Please keep in mind that all leagues MUST be full in order for a draft to begin. If a league is not full, it will NOT convert into draft mode, and the draft time will be rescheduled.IMPORTANT: League Managers, make sure that all of your league’s team managers have joined the league at least one hour before your draft! If not, then you will have to select a new Draft Date/Time.

Offline Draft

The offline draft option is only available in League Manager Leagues. If your league is set up to use the offline draft option, you and your fellow team managers will conduct your own draft without the use of ESPN’s online draft system. The format of an offline draft is up to the league members to coordinate, though they should use established league settings as a foundation. For an offline draft to work, it is critical that someone record each team’s draft picks. #### Input Offline Draft Results 1. Click on LM Tools  2. Click on Input Offline Draft Results 3. Click on the roster slot you wish to fill. As soon as you start typing, player names will begin to appear. Click on the desired player to fill the slot. 4. Click Make Rosters Available when finished to share the rosters with the league.

Online Draft Player Queue

  • Team managers can highlight a player’s name and either drag-and-drop them into the player queue area, or right-click the player’s name and select the “Add to Top of List” link, moving the player to the Player Queue.
  • There is no limit to the number of players that can be added to the queue.
  • In Snake Drafts, players listed in the Player Queue will be automatically drafted if on Autopick.
