Trade Limit (LM Only)

Set Trade Limit (Web Only)

In League Manager Leagues, this setting can be changed by the League Manager at any time during the season 1. Click on the League tab.​ 2. Click on Settings. 3. Click on Transactions and Keepers. 4. Click on Trade Rules. 5. Select the number of trades in the dropdown. 6. Click Save Changes when finished.

Settings Options for Trade Limits

  • No Trades - (LM Leagues: Only the League Manager can trade players between teams).
  • No Limit - Default setting. No limit to the number of trades a team can make.
  • Limited - A specific number of transactions is selected (i.e., 5, 10, 15, 20). Once that number of accepted & processed trades has been reached, the team will not be allowed to propose or accept any more trades. However, this will NOT limit their ability to add/drop players via waivers.

Trade Review

Trade Review Period for ESPN League Manager Leagues - Trade Review is the span of time allotted to other team managers in the league who are not directly involved in the trade to decide whether it is fair. - League Managers can determine the duration of this review period:  1 day is the default - 2 days - 3 days - No Trade Review

Trade Review Process - There is a 48-hour trade review period after a trade is accepted, during which team managers can review it. - After the trade offer is submitted, the system will display a pending move on your team page and on other team managers’ pages. - That team manager can then go to his/her team page to review the deal, and accept or decline it - If no action is taken within the specified number of days, the system will automatically cancel the trade offer. The pending move will disappear on both team pages. - If the trade is rejected, the team proposing it will receive an email notifying them of the result. - If the offer is accepted, the entire league will be notified via email, and other team managers can review it according to your league settings. - League Managers can push each trade through before the review period has passed. - Standard leagues: During the trade review period, if four of the ten team managers vote to veto a trade, the trade will be canceled. A link on the main League Office page lets you view pending trades and, if you choose, submit your veto.

Transaction Counter

The Transaction Counter is a tool that helps League/Team Managers track the number and types of transactions in a league. The tool helps keep track of the following types of transactions: #### Loss (Only in H2H leagues) - Number of losses in the season - This number is auto-generated by the system and cannot be adjusted

Trade 

  • The number of trades made by a certain team in the season
  • This number is auto-generated by the system. LMs can adjust this number
  • Team A trades with Team B. Both A and B will see their trade counters increase by 1

Offseason Acquisition 

  • Number of acquisitions (adds) made during the offseason
  • This number is auto-generated by the system. LMs can adjust this number
  • Team A adds a player prior to the draft and selects it as a Keeper; the Acquisition counter increases by 1

In-Season Acquisition

  • Number of acquisitions (Adds) made AFTER the draft
  • In Season Points/ROTO leagues, this value is generated by the system and cannot be adjusted
  • In H2H leagues, the weekly value can be adjusted by LM
  • Team D successfully made a claim and is awarded a player. The acquisition counter increases by 1

Drop

  • Number of Drops made AFTER the draft
  • This number is auto-generated by the system. LMs can adjust this number
  • Team A drops a player who suffered a season-ending injury. The drop counter increases by 1

Activate

  • Number of Activations from Bench spots to Active Lineup
  • The system automatically calculates this amount. and can be adjusted by LM
  • This increases every time you activate someone from the Bench to an active spot

Injured Reserve (IR / Injury List (IL)

  • Number of times you utilize IR/IL spots
  • The system automatically calculates this amount. and can be adjusted by LM
  • Team D puts a player who’s out for 3 weeks on IR/IL. The counter increases by 1. 3 weeks later, that player is replaced by another player who just got injured, the IR/IL counter increases by 1 again

Veto or Protest a Trade

The ability to veto a trade is available in order to prevent collusion in a league.  There are two ways to veto a trade, and in League Manager (Private) leagues, these settings can be changed by the LM at any time during the season: Public leagues and/or private leagues with standard settings:  - EVERY team manager in the league has the power to cast a vote against a trade, EXCEPT the two teams involved in the trade. Once a trade is accepted, an email will be sent to every team manager in the league with detailed instructions on how to cast a vote. Follow those steps, and you’ll be all set. - If enough votes are cast against the trade (4 out of 10, 50% of teams NOT involved in the trade), it will be canceled immediately. - Teams with more than one team manager will only receive one vote. - Once player(s) are traded, the players will be on the team’s bench until the Team Manager manually moves them to the active lineup.

Private leagues: - Unless otherwise changed by the LM, all public league settings apply - In LM leagues, LM has the ultimate power to veto a trade or let it go through - LMs can see the number of votes for or against a trade before it is vetoed or processed - If the rare scenario occurs where the setting is changed while the trade is pending approval, that trade will be grandfathered to use the original setting in place when the trade was accepted Under LM Tools -> Edit League settings -> Transactions and Keepers

Waiver Order Overview and Free Agent Budget Tiebreakers

What’s the difference, and how do they work? Fantasy leagues use one of two systems to determine which team gets priority when adding players who are on waivers. These systems have different names, but they work in very similar ways. NOTE: If you’re unsure which system your league uses, check under Players in your league menu. This guide explains: - What is Waiver Order (Standard Leagues) - Where do I see my Waiver Order? - Who controls the Waiver Order? - What is a Salary Cap tiebreaker? - Similarities Between the Two Systems - Key Differences - What Transactions Affect the Waiver Order? - Position Eligibility and Position Limits

What is a Waiver Order? (Standard Waiver Leagues)

In standard waiver leagues, teams are placed in a ranked list called the Waiver Order. When multiple teams try to claim the same player during the waiver period, the team with the higher priority (closer to the top of the list) gets the player. #### Where do I see the Waiver Order? Go to:  Players → Waiver Order #### Who controls Waiver Order? - In public leagues, the waiver order is set automatically. - In private leagues, the League Manager (LM) can manually adjust the order:

Click Edit - Drag teams into the desired position - Click Save Changes to finalize

What is Salary Cap Tiebreaker?

In leagues that use a Salary Cap system, managers bid virtual dollars on players who are on waivers. - The team that bids the highest amount wins the player. - If two or more teams bid the same amount, a tiebreaker order determines who gets the player. - To see the details: Go to: Players → Budget Summary - In League Manager leagues, the League Manager can edit each team’s budget:

Click Edit - Change the budget amount - Click Save Changes

Similarities Between the Two Systems

Even though they work differently, both systems share some important rules. ##### How the Order Updates Both systems can refresh in one of two ways, depending on league settings: ##### Option A: Reset Each Week - Each Monday at 12:00 AM PT / 3:00 AM ET (when a new fantasy week begins), the order resets. - The reset is based on inverse standings (teams with worse records get higher priority).

Option B: Move to Last After Claim
  • When a team successfully claims a player during the waiver process, that team moves to the bottom of the order.
  • The order does not automatically reset under this setting.

Important: No matter which option is selected, once a team successfully makes a waiver claim, they move to the bottom of the waiver priority list. ##### How the Initial Order Is Set Both systems use the same rules to determine the starting order. ###### If your league uses a Salary Cap draft: - The team with the most money remaining after the draft gets the highest waiver priority. - If teams are tied, the team that completed its roster first during the draft gets higher priority.

If your league uses a Snake Draft:
  • The draft order is reversed.
  • The team that picked first in the draft starts last in waiver order.
  • The team that picked last in the draft starts first in waiver order.

In short, the waiver order begins as the inverse of the draft order. #### Key Differences ##### League Manager Editing - In standard waiver order leagues, the League Manager can edit the waiver order at any time. - In Salary Cap** leagues**, the League Manager cannot manually edit the tiebreaker order after the waiver process.

NOTE:  - The League Manager can reverse a player claim if needed. - However, they cannot manually adjust the tiebreaker order itself in Salary Cap leagues.

What Transactions Affect the Waiver Order?

Waiver Claim

A waiver claim happens when: - A player is on waivers (not immediately available) - You submit a claim request - The system processes the claim after the waiver period ends

Waiver claims affect waiver priority. ##### Free Agency Pickup A free agency pickup happens when: - A player is immediately available - You add them instantly without waiting for a waiver period

Free agency pickups do NOT affect waiver order. #### Position Eligibility and Position Limits In League Manager (LM) leagues, the LM may set a cap on the number of players at a given position who can be on a single roster. This is common in larger leagues to help ensure every manager has a fair shot at building a competitive team. ##### How limits work If your league has a position limit and you want to add a player that would push you over that limit, you’ll need to drop an existing player at that position first before the transaction can go through. ##### What happens when a player qualifies at multiple positions? Some players are eligible at more than one position — for example, a player listed as 1B/3B. In these cases, the first position listed is always considered the primary position for roster limits. Here’s a practical example from ESPN Fantasy Baseball: Let’s say you need a third baseman. You’re under the limit at 3B, but you’ve already hit the limit at 1B. You try to claim a 1B/3B player off waivers. Even though you need him for third base, the system sees him primarily as a 1B—so you’ll need to drop one of your existing first basemen before the transaction will go through.

Waivers Overview

Players who are not drafted or on a current roster are available to be picked up off of waivers. If you are not happy with a specific player at a position and don’t want to worry about trading with another league team manager, you can add any player from the Free Agent list. You may have to drop a player in order to keep your roster at its league maximum number of players. All undrafted players will be set as ‘On Waivers’ immediately after the draft, each week of play, or if dropped from another team’s roster. Players on waivers will remain so for a set period of time, during which all teams will have the opportunity to make a claim on any player. When the waiver period expires, the player will be awarded to the team with the highest waiver priority that made a claim, and that team will move to the end of the waiver order. This process continues until all waiver claims are processed after which all players not added via waivers become free agents who can be acquired by any team on a first-come, first-served basis. - Standard Waivers - All unsigned players are put on waivers immediately following the league’s draft. This happens from the start of the first game until a few hours past the end of the last, and when players are dropped from another team. When the waiver period expires, usually around 3 am EST, all the claims from that period will be processed based on the waiver order. - Free Agent Budget (FAB) (Continuous) - Teams will have a specific budget to use for player signings. All offers will be processed in batches one or more times each week (as specified in the settings). If a team would like to add a player, that team will offer the salary amount they are willing to pay. On the next waiver process day, the team with the highest offer will be awarded the player, and the salary amount will be subtracted from that team’s budget. All unclaimed players must go through the waiver process in order to be picked up by a team. - No Waivers - Every player is immediately available to be added to your team as a free agent once they enter the candidate pool. Most leagues choose to utilize waivers instead of No Waivers as this system is often deemed unfair.

Login Issues: Clearing DNS Cache Windows, Mac, and Firefox

Fixing Login Issues — Clearing Your DNS Cache

Sometimes your computer holds onto old internet data that can interfere with logging in. Clearing it out (called “flushing your DNS”) is easier than it sounds! Just follow the steps below for your computer type. #### Windows Users First, figure out which version of Windows you have. Not sure? Click the Start button and search “About my PC” — it’ll tell you right there. ##### Windows 11 1. Click the Start button and type PowerShell in the search bar 2. Right-click Windows PowerShell and select Run as Administrator 3. Type exactly: ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter 4. You should see a message confirming the cache was cleared 5. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Windows 10
  1. Right-click the Start button (bottom left corner of your screen) and select Command Prompt (Admin)
  2. Type exactly: ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter
  3. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Windows 8
  1. Click the Start button and type cmd in the search bar
  2. When Command Prompt appears in the results, right-click it and select Run as Administrator
  3. Type exactly: ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Windows 7 or Vista
  1. Click the Start button, then navigate to All Programs → Accessories → Command Prompt
  2. Right-click Command Prompt and select Run as Administrator
  3. Type exactly: ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mac Users

On a Mac, this process works through an app called Terminal. You can find it by opening Spotlight Search (press ⌘ + Spacebar) and typing “Terminal.” Not sure which version of macOS you have? Click the Apple menu in the top left corner and select About This Mac — the version will be displayed right there. #### macOS Sequoia, Sonoma, Ventura, Monterey, or Big Sur (2020 and later) 1. Open Terminal 2. Type exactly: sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Enter 3. You’ll be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so (you won’t see the password as you type — that’s normal!) 4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

macOS Catalina (version 10.15)

  1. Open Terminal
  2. Type exactly: sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Enter
  3. You may be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

macOS Mojave, High Sierra, or Sierra (versions 10.14, 10.13, or 10.12)

  1. Open Terminal
  2. Type exactly: sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Enter
  3. You may be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

macOS El Capitan, Mavericks, or Mountain Lion (versions 10.11, 10.9, or 10.8)

  1. Open Terminal
  2. Type exactly: sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder and press Enter
  3. You may be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mac OS X Yosemite (version 10.10)

  1. Open Terminal
  2. Type exactly: sudo discoveryutil udnsflushcaches and press Enter
  3. You may be prompted to enter your Mac password — go ahead and do so
  4. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mozilla Firefox Users

  • Firefox users can install the DNS Flusher add-on then follow the instructions to clear the DNS cache.
  • Return to ESPN.com and attempt to Log In

 Tips:

  • When typing these commands, copy them exactly as written; spacing and capitalization matter!
  • On Mac, it’s normal for Terminal to show nothing after running the command — that means it worked!
  • If you’re still having trouble after following these steps, don’t hesitate to reach out to ESPN Support.

Login Issues: Clearing Your Cache & Cookies (Chrome, Safari & Firefox)

Fixing Login Issues — Clearing Your Cache & Cookies

Your browser stores bits of website data to help pages load faster—but sometimes that stored data becomes outdated, causing problems like login issues or pages not displaying correctly. Clearing it out is quick and easy! Just find your browser below and follow the steps. Heads up: After clearing your cache and cookies, you’ll likely be logged out of websites you normally stay signed into—including ESPN. Just log back in as usual, and you should be good to go! ##### Google Chrome (Desktop) 1. Click the three vertical dots (⋮) in the top-right corner of Chrome 2. Hover over History, then click History again in the menu that appears 3. On the left side, click Clear browsing data 4. Set the Time Range to All time 5. Make sure both Cookies and other site data, and Cached images and files are checked 6. Click Clear data 7. Close Chrome completely and reopen it, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Google Chrome (Mobile — iPhone or Android)
  1. Tap the three dots in the top-right corner (Android) or bottom-right corner (iPhone)
  2. Tap History, then Clear browsing data
  3. Set the Time Range to All time
  4. Make sure Cookies, site data, and Cached images and files are both selected
  5. Tap Clear data and confirm
  6. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Apple Safari (Desktop — Mac)
  1. Click Safari in the top menu bar and select Settings (or Preferences on older Macs)
  2. Click the Privacy tab
  3. Click Manage Website Data, then Remove All
  4. Confirm by clicking Remove Now
  5. Close and reopen Safari, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Shortcut option: You can also click History in the top menu bar, select Clear History, set it to All History, and click Clear History to confirm. ##### Apple Safari (Mobile — iPhone or iPad) 1. Open the Settings app on your device (not Safari itself) 2. Scroll down and tap Apps, then tap Safari 3. Tap Clear History and Website Data 4. Select your preferred timeframe and tap Clear History and Data to confirm 5. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mozilla Firefox (Desktop)
  1. Click the three horizontal lines (☰) in the top-right corner of Firefox
  2. Click Settings
  3. On the left, click Privacy & Security
  4. Scroll down to the Cookies and Site Data section and click Clear Data
  5. Make sure both Cookies, Site Data, and Cached Web Content are checked
  6. Click Clear, then confirm by clicking Clear Now
  7. Close Firefox completely and reopen it, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Pro Tip

On Windows or Mac, you can also use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + Delete (Windows) or ⌘ + Shift + Delete (Mac) while in any of these browsers to jump straight to the clear data screen! If you’ve cleared your cache and cookies and are still having trouble, don’t hesitate to reach out to ESPN Fan Support by clicking on the chat icon at the lower right of this screen— we’re happy to help!

Click the Profile icon in the top-right corner of the ESPN.com homepage. 2. Select Log In from the left-side menu. 3. Click Need help signing in?

Step 2: Request a Passcode

ESPN Fantasy Sports - How to be a Great League Manager - Part 1

This brief video introduces the role of League Manager (LM). You will get an overview of LM responsibilities, league settings, and helpful tips to help avoid common issues.

ESPN Fantasy Sports - How to be a Great League Manager - Part 2

This short video provides an overview of the League Manager (LM) Tools and how to access them on either the ESPN Fantasy app or on ESPN.com. I also introduced common league settings and usage, along with helpful tips to create a hassle-free LM experience for you and your managers.

ESPN Fantasy Women’s Basketball

What are Fantasy Games?

Have you ever dreamed of what it would be like to own your own professional sports team? Fantasy games are a way to live out that dream. And to make things easier, all fantasy games are fundamentally the same — real athletes and their real-life performances are used to generate points for fantasy teams in fantasy leagues. In a traditional fantasy league, there is a set number of team managers, and a clear set of rules that govern everything from roster size to scoring to schedule. You and your fellow managers hold a draft, filling your fantasy roster with real-life athletes from across the sport. Then, throughout the season, you set your lineup based on how well you think your players will perform. The statistics they generate in real games are collected, and fantasy points are awarded based on those numbers. The better your players perform, the more points your team racks up. Ultimately, those points determine a winner. The team that accumulates the most points — or earns the most points-based wins over the course of the season, or prevails in the postseason — is declared the league champion. And with that title comes all the glory of lording it over your fellow managers… until next season, when they come back hungry for revenge. #### What is ESPN Fantasy Women’s Basketball? Welcome to the world of fantasy basketball - ESPN Style! ESPN Fantasy Women’s Basketball is the closest thing you can find to buying your own professional franchise and becoming the team’s coach, owner, and president. All decisions are yours to make. And lucky for you, basketball is a game filled with unbiased player performance statistics. Using these statistics, you have everything you need to understand which players are performing well and which are not. ESPN’s Fantasy Women’s Basketball is as close as anyone will come to owning a winning franchise and becoming the team’s manager, coach, and president. All team decisions are yours to make. Each team owner is supplied with all of the tools—multiple draft methods, unlimited waivers and trades, free agency, an all-powerful commissioner, chat rooms, league bulletin boards, player statistics, etc. In other words, everything needed to build a championship team. Statistical reports, expert analysis, and up-to-date feature articles from ESPN.com editors are readily available to keep owners informed. Armed with this information, team managers are free to create the team of their dreams. To win, a team manager has to be crafty, as each team competes directly with nine other owners who are equally determined to come out on top. Team managers can choose who they compete against and are free to join a league at their own level. Like the race for the final WNBA playoff spot, the league title could be determined on the very last day of the season in rotisserie leagues. For head-to-head scoring, the top four teams in each league will play each other in the playoffs, which are held during the final weeks of the WNBA regular season. The remaining teams compete in the consolation bracket. Regardless of your regular-season record, your team is guaranteed to play every week of the WNBA season. Once you join a league, ESPN provides you with everything needed to build the best possible basketball team. And sure, you got your cut-throat, 11th-hour wheeling and dealing between armchair League Managers, fully customizable league rules and scoring, multiple draft methods, live box scores, waivers, trades, free agency, custom player updates, a league commissioner, league bulletin boards, sortable stats for all players, and more. There’s plenty of room to sling trash-talk throughout your league, and enough stats and weekly analysis to make you the next Fantasy Women’s Basketball champion. We just want to make sure you know what to do with it all! So sit back as we take you through the keys to ESPN Fantasy Women’s Basketball. Then get crackin’ on creating the next fantasy dynasty!

Fair Play and Conduct

Although Fantasy Sports are extremely competitive, we emphasize that all participants exercise good sportsmanship to prevent team managers from unintentionally crossing the line and maintain a fun environment. A note on Fair Play and Conduct in ESPN Fantasy Leagues: ESPN oversees all leagues on the platform. In standard public leagues, ESPN serves as your commissioner and is your first point of contact for any issues. In League Manager (LM) leagues, your LM handles day-to-day management and is your go-to for questions or concerns—with ESPN available as a backstop to help ensure every league runs smoothly for everyone involved. A. More than one team in the same league B. Collusive Transactions C. Impeding Other Team Managers D. Roster Dumping E. Team Manager Interactions F. Offensive Language G. Inactivity H. League Manager Leagues #### A: More Than One Team in the Same League (ESPN Standard Leagues) - One person can’t control more than one team in the same league. - If two or more teams in the same league are under the same account, they must be controlled by different people who share that account but not the teams. - Violation of this will result in team cancellation and expulsion from the game.

B: Collusive Transactions

  • Collusion occurs when one team makes moves to benefit another team, without trying to improve its own position.
  • One-sided trades are an example of collusive transactions.
  • Dropping a player so another team can pick up that player is another example of collusive transactions.
  • Teams found in violation of this policy will be canceled, and their team managers will be prohibited from participating in future ESPN Fantasy Games.

NOTE: Standard League members are expected to veto/protest any and all unfair or collusive trades throughout the season. At least 4 team managers’ votes are required in protest for a trade to be denied in a Standard League. #### C: Impeding Other Team Managers - Making certain transactions solely to impede other team managers is not allowed. - Tanking games solely to deny another player a chance to make the playoffs is against the rules. - Cycling through players in free agency to put them on waivers and make them unavailable to another team in your league is strictly prohibited and is grounds for expulsion from the game.

D: Roster Dumping

  • Team managers who are found to have dumped their players into the player pool to undermine the league may be expelled from the game.
  • If you are giving up on the season, we ask that you maintain league strength by fielding the most competitive team you can.

E: Team Manager Interaction

  • Team managers should always be polite and gracious when dealing with one another.
  • Threats and obscenities are against the rules and illegal in many jurisdictions.
  • Team managers who are found to have sent threatening emails to another team manager will be warned and/or permanently banned from the ESPN and/or Disney sites.
  • These rules extend to message board posts as well.

F: Offensive Language

  • Any language, including posts, messaging, league and team names, that is derogatory is strictly prohibited.
  • This includes chat rooms, message boards, or the league’s bulletin board.
  • Personal attacks and sexist or racist remarks also fall under this restriction.
  • There is a zero tolerance level. Offenders are subject to a ban from ESPN and/or Disney sites.

G: Inactivity (ESPN Standard Leagues)

  • To maintain the integrity of the league, the commissioner may contact the managers of teams that remain inactive for extended periods.
  • The league commissioner will send a notification to the email on record.
  • If the team remains inactive after the league commissioner sends an email to the inactive team manager, the commissioner reserves the right to reassign the team’s management.

H: League Manager Leagues

  • ESPN Fantasy Baseball League Manager leagues are created according to the specifications implemented by their league creators.
  • The League Manager and other team managers are responsible for handling all conduct, communication, and fair play issues that arise in these LM Leagues.

Network Connection Issues: ESPN Fantasy App

Try these steps in order to identify and fix the issue. Step 1: Verify Your Internet Connection Open Safari (iOS) or Chrome (Android) and go to games.espn.com. If you see an error message, your internet connection is the problem, and the error should indicate the cause. These issues are outside of ESPN’s control, so contact your internet provider if needed. Good to Know: The ESPN Fantasy App requires a moderately strong connection to function. Keep in mind that signal bars on your phone reflect voice/call strength but not the actual speed or reliability of your data connection. Step 2 (iOS Only): Check Cellular Data Settings Make sure Cellular Data is enabled for the ESPN Fantasy App: 1. Open Settings 2. Tap Cellular 3. Scroll down to the app list and find ESPN Fantasy 4. Make sure the toggle is On (green)

Step 3: Try a Different Internet Connection - On Wi-Fi? Try switching to cellular (3G/4G/LTE). - On cellular? Try connecting to a Wi-Fi network instead. - Confirm that other apps or websites load normally on your current connection.

Step 4: Verify Access to the ESPN API In any browser, test your access at http://games.espn.com/ffl/connectivity. If no error messages appear, your device can successfully reach the ESPN API. Step 5: Force-Quit and Reopen the App - iOS: Double-tap the Home button and swipe up on the ESPN Fantasy App. - Android: Open the task manager (long-press Home or use your device’s app switcher) and swipe away the ESPN Fantasy App.

Step 6: Clear the App Cache - iOS: Force-quit the app (Step 5), then go to Settings → Fantasy (look for the rainbow logo) and tap the Reset slider. Relaunch the app. - Android: Force-quit the app (Step 5), then go to App Settings → ESPN Fantasy App and tap Clear Data and Clear Cache. Relaunch the app.

Step 7: Reinstall the App - iOS: Press and hold the app icon, tap the X to uninstall, then reinstall from the App Store. - Android: Uninstall via App Settings, then reinstall from the Play Store.

Still Not Working? If none of these steps help, there may be a larger outage that our team is already working to resolve. Check support.espn.com for the latest updates or open a Chat with ESPN Fan Support by clicking on the icon at the bottom right of this screen.

TC - Tournament Challenge: Bracket FAQs

How do I change my Bracket Name?

Changing your Bracket Name is easy! Start by selecting Dashboard on the TC banner. The dashboard is where you can view all of your brackets. Now click on the bracket name. This will bring up the bracket view. (image: TC bracket name 0.png) In the bracket view, you will see either the countdown clock or your selections (depending on when you access it).  To change your bracket name, clock on the Gear icon to the right of your default bracket name. (image: TC bracket name 1.png) Type in your desired Bracket name in the Name Your Bracket field.  Please note that the ESPN Terms of Use and House Rules apply, so please be mindful of your choice of bracket names. Click Save Settings to save your changes! (image: TC bracket name 2.png)

How do I create a bracket/entry?

Creating a bracket in ESPN Tournament Challenge is simple! NOTE: The bracket creation process is identical for both Men’s and Women’s Tournament Challenge. Simply tap on the appropriate header to begin! - Create a Bracket on ESPN.com - Create a Bracket on the ESPN TC App

Create a Bracket on ESPN.com

  1. Begin by logging in to your ESPN.com account.
  2. From the Tournament Challenge Frontpage, click on the “Create A Bracket” button.
  3. A confirmation panel will pop up with options to either Create a Group or Join a Group. Click on the “x” to dismiss the confirmation.
  4. From your entry page, you can make your selections for the NCAA Basketball Tournament and create or join a group.
  5. Please note: Selections can only be made once the timer reaches 0 days, 0 hours, 0 minutes, and 0 seconds!

Create a Bracket on the ESPN TC App

  1. Launch the ESPN TC app and log in!
  2. Once logged in, simply tap Create a Bracket! You will see the confirmation pop-up with the options to Create or Join a Group. Tap the “x” to dismiss.

How do I delete my bracket/entry?

Once a bracket/entry is created it cannot be deleted. It can be renamed and you can edit the entry settings or change your picks before the tournament starts but it cannot be removed. 

There is no penalty for not filling-out all of your created brackets/entries with team selections or using them to enter into a group.

If you have erroneously created a bracket, you can simply ignore it until the NCAA Tournaments are over and all brackets will be removed.

Best of luck with your selections!

What is the Second Chance Challenge?

Despite your best efforts, sometimes brackets shatter before the Tournament gets past the Round of 64.  That is where the Second Chance Challenge comes in. Women’s TC 2nd Chance -  - Brackets Open - Afternoon of March 20, 2026 - Brackets Close  - Tipoff of the first game on Friday, March 27, 2026.  

Both Second Chance brackets lock at the start of the Sweet 16 for each tourney.

ESPN has a Challenge game for both the Men’s and Women’s NCAA Tournaments. Both Challenge games function the same way, and only the teams in each bracket differ. The steps below apply to both the Men’s and Women’s Tournament Challenge.  Creating a bracket in the ESPN Women’s Tournament Challenge is simple! - Create a Bracket on ESPN.com - Create a Bracket on the ESPN TC App

Create a Bracket on ESPN.com

  1. Begin by logging in to your ESPN.com account.
  2. From the ESPN Women’s Tournament Challenge Frontpage, click on the “Create A Bracket” button.
  3. A confirmation panel will pop up with options to either Create a Group or Join a Group. Click on the “x” to dismiss the confirmation.
  4. From your entry page, you can make your selections for the NCAA Women’s Basketball Tournament and create or join a group.

Please note: Selections can only be made once the timer reaches 0 days, 0 hours, 0 minutes, and 0 seconds! #### Create a Bracket on the ESPN TC App 1. Launch the ESPN TC app and log in! 2. Once logged in, simply tap Create a Bracket! 3. You will see the confirmation pop-up with the options to Create or Join a Group. 4. Tap the “x” to dismiss.

Your Bracket - Explained

The first step in playing Tournament Challenge is to create your bracket/entry. You will need to have a bracket/entry created before you’re able to join any Tournament Challenge Groups. The ability to fill out your bracket/entry with team picks will become available after all the teams in the Tournament have been set, and the timer counts down to “0”. Once the Tournament tip-off begins, bracket creation will be locked.

Once you’ve filled out your bracket and the Tournament is underway, you will notice that the accuracy of your picks is displayed directly on the bracket. See below for explanations of each notation; please also note that the example screenshot below is a mockup! - GREEN = Correct pick: You have selected the right team to win the game. In addition, a green checkmark icon will appear next to your pick. RED = Incorrect pick: You picked the wrong team to win the game. In addition, a red “x” icon will appear next to your pick. - WHITE = Winning Team: The team that won the matchup - GREY = Losing Team: The team that lost the matchup

National Championship

For the National Championship, you will be asked to predict both the winner of the game and the total score for each team. The “Predicted Score” would only be used in the event of a tie between two brackets.  Example: #### Let’s say your predicted score was 67 - 63, and the actual game score was 77 - 85. #### To calculate, you’d simply subtract the lower scores from the higher scores to get the number of total points you were away from getting the score exactly correct. #### In this case, it would be (77 - 67) + (85 - 63)= 32 points off the exact score. #### Whoever is closest to the final score will be declared the winner.

TC - Tournament Challenge: Group FAQs

How do edit my group settings?

To edit your group settings, simply log in and select Groups in the TC menu Banner. Select the desired Group. Click on the Gear icon next to your Group’s name. This will open the Group Details panel where you can see your editing options Group Lock Settings  Locked: After the Tournament starts group members can no longer add/remove brackets from the group. Unlocked: Anytime during the Tournament your group members can add/remove brackets from the group.

Public or Private Private: Cannot be seen by users who have not been provided an invitation. You will also have the option to set a group password for private leagues. Public: Can be found by all users through the Group Directory. Able to be joined. No Password.

Entries Per User The amount of brackets each member is allowed to enter into your group. Users can have up to 25 brackets per person (no limit) by default but the limit for each group can be set to 1 per person via this setting.

How do I add a logo to my group?

Your group settings must be PRIVATE to utilize the logo feature. You will not see the option to upload an image for a public league. Select Groups in the TC menu Banner. Select the desired Group. Click on the default trophy logo before your Group’s name. The list of available logos will appear, select the category and the logo you wish to use, then click Save Logo Selection.

How do I create a Group?

Click on Groups in the TC banner menu. Click on the Create Group button. Enter the Group’s name, select the type of Group, the Group password if Private, and number of entries allowed then click continue. Please note that the ESPN Terms of Use and House Rules apply, so please be mindful of your choice of Group name. Now you will be prompted to select the bracket(s) to use in this Group. When ready click on Add to Group. That’s it! Now you can invite others to join your Group!

How do I invite members to my group?

Select Groups on the TC banner. Then click on your desired Group Now click on Invite Friends You will be shown three options - Invite Friends - a direct email form that allows you to edit the message, add email addresses, and select friends from other Groups you are in.

  • Copy Link - use this to paste into custom invites such as email, texts, fourms, etc.
  • More Sharing Options -  A variety of different methods to utilize

How do I leave a Group?

REMINDER: You can only leave a group if its settings allow it. If your group settings are “locked,” once the first game tips off, you will NOT be able to leave your group. You can always leave a group before tipoff.  To leave a group, begin by clicking on Groups Now click on the Group Name. This will open the Group page Now click on the Gear icon next to the Group name. This will open the Group Details popup. To leave, click on Remove Entry. NOTE: You must select each entry to be removed in multiple-entry leagues.

How do I re-join last year’s Group?

Great news, once the Group creator restarts the previous season’s Group, everyone will be automatically added.

How do I remove brackets/entries from my private Group?

Select Groups on the TC banner. Then click on your desired Group Now toggle Edit Members You will now be able to Add a Group Co-Creator and/or Remove Entry by clicking on the relevant button You will now be asked to confirm the removal. Click Confirm to remove teh entry from your Group

How to Join a Tournament Challenge Group

To join a Tournament Challenge group, you must first create a bracket entry. #### Quick Summary - You must create a bracket before joining a group. - Go to My Groups → Create or Join a Group. - Select the group and add your bracket. - Group entry limits are controlled by the Group Creator. - If the app isn’t working, try joining through a web browser.

Step 1: Create a Bracket Entry

Before you can join a group, you must create at least one bracket. 1. Go to the My Bracket menu. 2. Select Create a Bracket. 3. Complete the bracket creation process.

IMPORTANT: You do not need to make your picks right away. Simply creating the bracket is enough to join a group. #### Step 2: Join or Rejoin a Group Once your bracket is created: 1. Go to the My Groups menu. 2. Select Create or Join a Group. 3. You will be taken to the Group Directory. 4. Search for or select the group you want to join. 5. Click Join/Rejoin to open the group page.

Step 3: Add Your Bracket to the Group

After opening the group page: 1. Scroll down to the section labeled Select a bracket to add to the group. 2. Use the checkbox to select the bracket you want to enter. 3. Click Join Group to complete the process. Your bracket will now appear in the group standings.

Entry Limits

Each group may limit the number of brackets a single user can enter. This setting is called Group Entries Per User and is shown in the group’s information section. Only the Group Creator can change this setting. If you are unable to add another bracket, you may have reached the group’s entry limit. #### Having Trouble Joining in the Mobile App? If you’re experiencing issues joining a group in the ESPN Tournament Challenge mobile app: - Try using a web browser (such as Google Chrome). - Go to ESPN.com and join the group from there. - After joining, log out of the app and log back in to refresh your groups.

NOTE: Some features and settings may not be fully available in the mobile app due to device settings or app version differences. The website may provide more complete functionality.

What is the Group Directory?

The Group Directory displays all the groups that have been formed in Men’s Tournament Challenge. Groups allow participants of the game to compete against each other and the Group Directory makes it easy to find a specific group. You can use this section to search and join custom Groups, find celebrity groups to join, or rejoin the Group that you played in last year! From the Group Directory, you can join a public Group or a private Group or rejoin a Group you were in last season.  You can search for Groups using the directory drop-down filters. When you see a Group that interests you, simply click on Join/Rejoin. After you click on Join, you will be asked to select which of your brackets you wish to use in this Group. Note that Group rules determine which brackets can be used (for example, single bracket versus multiple brackets). When you are ready, click Join Group.

What should I do if I’ve forgotten the password to the private group I created?

Simply log in and select Groups in the TC menu Banner. Select the desired Group. Click on the Gear icon next to your Group’s name. This will open the Group Details panel where you can see the Group Password.

Why are my members not receiving email invites?

There are many reasons why a member(s) of your group may not be receiving the email invitation to join your Tournament Challenge group. A few common issues and resolutions are provided below.

Common Issues/Resolutions #1 - The email address entered is incorrect.  - Double check the spelling/format of the email addresses you’ve entered. #2 - The email is being received but is going to a “Spam/Trash” folder. - Have the member(s) check all the folders in their email account. #3 - The email is being blocked by your members web service or firewall - Ask the member(s) to turn-off firewalls or access their email through a different network connection. #4 - The domain (@yahoo.com, @suddenlink.com, etc.) your member uses is performing slowly. - Ask the member(s) to wait for the servers of the web mail provider to catch up and receive the invitation. #5 - Due to high volume (Selection Sunday –> Tip Off) ESPN servers are currently sending out an extremely high volume of invitations from the millions of Tournament Challenge groups being created.  - Give the ESPN servers some time to process and send the invitation correctly. If the member(s) has not received it within 24 hours then use the direct link method found below.

Send Direct Link Follow the steps in the following FAQ to invite members using a Direct Link: How do I invite members to my group Utilize Group Directory Have your potential member(s) navigate to the Group Directory and use the “search” function to find the Group Name. If the league is “Private” they will need to enter the Password the Group Creator provides them before being able to join. If you have forgotten the password of your group, click here

TC - Tournament Challenge: Welcome to Tournament Challenge

Can I play against ESPN Celebrities?

If you know the name of the group you are searching for, use the search engine in the Group Directory. Type the first letters of the group name, and select the group you want to join. In addition, you can use the Group Type dropdown to see all available Celebrity Groups.  As we get celebrity-created Groups, they will be featured here.

How do I know which bracket had the closest tiebreaker score?

Group Administrators will need to compute these tiebreakers on their own, if two brackets tie with the same bracket points value in their group(s). Tie breakers are decided by “winner score + loser score” relative to the “actual game score”.

Due to the extremely high volume of brackets and the taxing computations needed by ESPN to automatically break ties in a near real-time fashion this has been left up to each Group Administrator to calculate in the event of a tie between their group members.

Login Issues: Clearing Your Cache & Cookies (Chrome, Safari & Firefox)

Fixing Login Issues — Clearing Your Cache & Cookies

Your browser stores bits of website data to help pages load faster—but sometimes that stored data becomes outdated, causing problems like login issues or pages not displaying correctly. Clearing it out is quick and easy! Just find your browser below and follow the steps. Heads up: After clearing your cache and cookies, you’ll likely be logged out of websites you normally stay signed into—including ESPN. Just log back in as usual, and you should be good to go! ##### Google Chrome (Desktop) 1. Click the three vertical dots (⋮) in the top-right corner of Chrome 2. Hover over History, then click History again in the menu that appears 3. On the left side, click Clear browsing data 4. Set the Time Range to All time 5. Make sure both Cookies and other site data, and Cached images and files are checked 6. Click Clear data 7. Close Chrome completely and reopen it, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Google Chrome (Mobile — iPhone or Android)
  1. Tap the three dots in the top-right corner (Android) or bottom-right corner (iPhone)
  2. Tap History, then Clear browsing data
  3. Set the Time Range to All time
  4. Make sure Cookies, site data, and Cached images and files are both selected
  5. Tap Clear data and confirm
  6. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Apple Safari (Desktop — Mac)
  1. Click Safari in the top menu bar and select Settings (or Preferences on older Macs)
  2. Click the Privacy tab
  3. Click Manage Website Data, then Remove All
  4. Confirm by clicking Remove Now
  5. Close and reopen Safari, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Shortcut option: You can also click History in the top menu bar, select Clear History, set it to All History, and click Clear History to confirm. ##### Apple Safari (Mobile — iPhone or iPad) 1. Open the Settings app on your device (not Safari itself) 2. Scroll down and tap Apps, then tap Safari 3. Tap Clear History and Website Data 4. Select your preferred timeframe and tap Clear History and Data to confirm 5. Head back to ESPN and try logging in again

Mozilla Firefox (Desktop)
  1. Click the three horizontal lines (☰) in the top-right corner of Firefox
  2. Click Settings
  3. On the left, click Privacy & Security
  4. Scroll down to the Cookies and Site Data section and click Clear Data
  5. Make sure both Cookies, Site Data, and Cached Web Content are checked
  6. Click Clear, then confirm by clicking Clear Now
  7. Close Firefox completely and reopen it, then head back to ESPN and try logging in again
Pro Tip

On Windows or Mac, you can also use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Shift + Delete (Windows) or ⌘ + Shift + Delete (Mac) while in any of these browsers to jump straight to the clear data screen! If you’ve cleared your cache and cookies and are still having trouble, don’t hesitate to reach out to ESPN Fan Support by clicking on the chat icon at the lower right of this screen— we’re happy to help!

What do PTS, PCT, and RK mean?

PTS (Points): The total amount of points that your team has accumulated since the start of the tournament. PCT (Percentile): The percentile your performance falls within, graded against all other entrants in the game. RK (Rank): Your numerical rank in the entire field of entrants. As participants of Tournament Challenge,  your goal is to get your numbers in those categories to be as high as possible. The higher that your PTS, PCT or RK are, the better you are doing in picking the winning team in each matchup. Check your standing on the Leaderboard.

What is the deadline for entries?

Entries (and any changes to the bracket) must be completed before the first game’s tipoff! Men’s TC -  - Brackets Open - Selection Sunday March 15, 2026  - Brackets Close  - Tipoff of the first game on Thursday, March 19, 2026.  

Women’s TC  -  - Brackets Open - Selection Sunday March 15, 2026 - Brackets Close  - Tipoff of the first game on Friday, March 20, 2026.  

Men’s TC 2nd Chance-  - Brackets Open - Afternoon of March 19, 2026 - Brackets Close  - Tipoff of the first game on Thursday, March 26, 2026.  

Women’s TC 2nd Chance -  - Brackets Open - Afternoon of March 20, 2026 - Brackets Close  - Tipoff of the first game on Friday, March 27, 2026.  

NOTE: All brackets lock on tipoff and cannot be changed (not even by us).

Please leave yourself ample time to submit your picks before the tip-off date!

Millions of brackets are submitted to ESPN each day during the tournament’s lead-up, so it’s essential to lock in your picks as early as possible to avoid any technical delays, which may prevent you from fully setting your bracket before the Tournament begins. NOTE: Once the tournament starts, the only way to create a bracket is when the Second Chance Challenge opens.

What’s my ranking? - Leaderboard Explanation

Throughout the Tournament Challenge, every bracket created will accumulate points, and ESPN will update the “Leaderboard” to show you an approximation of where your bracket ranks compared to all other brackets created. 

Each game in every round of the Tournament is worth a different number of total points. The object of the game is simple: Correctly pick the winner of the most matches in the 63 games following the “First Four” round of the tournament. See below for the points breakdown for each round. NOTE: This information applies equally to Men’s and Women’s Tournament Challenge. - ROUND: TEAMS: GAMES: POINTS (per win): POINTS (total) - Second Round: 64: 32: 10: 320 - Third Round: 32: 16: 20: 320 - Sweet Sixteen (regional      semifinals): 16: 8: 40: 320 - Elite Eight (regional finals): 8: 4: 80: 320 - Final Four (semifinals): 4: 2: 160: 320 - National Championship (finals): 2: 1: 320: 320 - Totals: –: 63: –: 1920

Navigate to “Leaderboard” via the Tournament Challenge homepage/banner. 

The section at the top will show you a list of all of YOUR brackets, how they rank against each other, and how they rank against everyone else (“Rank” - Left Side or “PCT” - Right Side). 

Below that you’ll find the overall Tournament Challenge Leaderboard. This will display the top-performing brackets across all of ESPN, the points they’ve accumulated in each round, and the “Percentile” (PCT) they rank in vs. all other brackets created for the TC season.
